- `codex-rs/app-server-daemon/src/update_loop.rs`: the Unix installer-cancellation path
  (`cancel_installer`) correctly keeps the shell process unreaped across the `SIGTERM`/`SIGKILL`
  group-kill sequence before checking and removing the installer's fallback lock directory, so a
  reused PID cannot be mistaken for the lock owner; the `pin!`-based reuse of a single
  `terminate.recv()` future across the stdin-write and `child.wait()` selects is a valid and
  correct use of a persistently-pinned future, not a double-consumption bug.
- `codex-rs/app-server-daemon/src/manual_update.rs`: the request/replacement-deadline state
  machine (falling back to a fresh daemon-updater startup when a one-shot updater's socket
  disappears, and retrying against a successor's socket after a replacement) matches its
  covering tests (`manual_request_retries_after_updater_replacement`,
  `manual_request_recovers_when_one_shot_updater_exits`,
  `unsupported_request_preserves_updater_schedule`).
- `codex-rs/app-server-daemon/src/lib.rs`: `Daemon::run`/`start`/`restart`/`stop`/
  `set_remote_control_locked` consistently require exclusive ownership (erroring on an unmanaged
  process at the control socket) for every mutating lifecycle operation while allowing read-only
  operations (`start` when already running, `version`) to report status for an unmanaged process
  without erroring; this asymmetry is deliberate and consistent across the module.
- The generated files under `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/schema/typescript/` (all 15 in this
  shard) are marked `GENERATED CODE! DO NOT MODIFY BY HAND!`; spot-checked `ClientRequest.ts`
  for duplicate `"method"` discriminants (a class of bug that would silently break the
  discriminated union) and found all 105 method strings unique.
- `codex-rs/app-server-protocol-noop-macros/src/lib.rs`: the no-op `JsonSchema`/`TS` derive
  macros correctly declare their helper attributes (`schemars`, `ts`) so real annotations on
  production structs don't trigger "unknown attribute" errors, consistent with the crate's
  stated purpose.

All 30 files in this shard are ts-rs-generated TypeScript mirrors of Rust types in `codex-rs/app-server-protocol` (and, transitively, `codex-rs/protocol`), each headed "GENERATED CODE! DO NOT MODIFY BY HAND!". Given that, the review focused on whether the generated shape is internally consistent and matches its Rust source, rather than on logic (there is none to review in a type alias/union).

- Spot-checked several generated types against their Rust definitions for field-for-field and nullability fidelity: `ConversationSummary` (`app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v1.rs`), `FileChange` (`protocol/src/protocol.rs`), and the `FuzzyFileSearch*` family (`app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs`, see the finding above for the one place it drifted). All others matched the expected `Option<T>` -> `T | null`, `#[serde(skip_serializing_if)]`-style optional -> `field?:`, and enum/tag conventions with no drift.
- `FileChange`'s `Delete { content: String }` variant carrying a `content` field (rather than being empty) looked odd at first glance but matches the Rust enum exactly (`codex-rs/protocol/src/protocol.rs`), presumably to let a client render/undo the removed content; not a defect.
- Several types use snake_case field names that intentionally mirror an external wire format rather than drifting from local convention: `FunctionCallOutputContentItem` (`image_url`, `audio_url`, `encrypted_content`) is explicitly documented as "Responses API compatible", and `InternalChatMessageMetadataPassthrough`'s `turn_id` is explicitly documented as Responses-API-typed passthrough that must not be changed without upstream API approval. These are correct as generated.
- `GetAuthStatusResponse.authToken: string | null` looked like a potential credential-exposure concern in isolation, so I checked the corresponding handler (`codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/account_processor.rs`, outside this shard but needed to resolve the concern): the token is only populated when the caller explicitly passes `includeToken: true` in `GetAuthStatusParams`, otherwise `auth_token: None` is returned. This is an intentional, caller-gated opt-in over a local IPC channel, not an unconditional leak.
- The remaining files (enums such as `ConversationTextRole`, `ForcedLoginMethod`, `ImageDetail`, `InputModality`, `FuzzyFileSearchMatchType`; simple param/response wrappers such as `GitDiffToRemoteParams/Response`, `GetConversationSummaryParams/Response`, `ExecCommandApprovalParams/Response`, `InitializeParams/Response/Capabilities`) are straightforward, well-formed mirrors of their Rust counterparts with no internal inconsistency, and expose no credentials or unsafe defaults.

the generated TypeScript by hand:

  `AppsInstalledParams`, `AppsInstalledResponse`, `AppsListParams`, `AppsListResponse`,
  `AppsReadParams`, `AppToolSummary`, `AppListUpdatedNotification` →

- `AppLinksConfig`, `AppToolsConfig`, `AppToolApproval`, `AppsConfig`, `AppsDefaultConfig`,
  `AnalyticsConfig` → `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/config.rs`
- `ApplicationNetworkRequirements`, `ApplicationRequirements` →
  `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/application.rs`
- `AllowDenyRequirement` → `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/config.rs`

  via `#[ts(type = ...)]` to include the legacy `"guardian_subagent"` alias, which is intentional:
  the enum only ever *serializes* `AutoReview` as `"auto_review"`, but `#[serde(alias =

  `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/plugin.rs`

In every case, field names/casing (camelCase mapping of `snake_case` Rust fields), optionality
(`?` for fields with `#[ts(optional)]`/`skip_serializing_if`, vs. plain `| null` for bare
`Option<T>` without that attribute), enum variant spelling/casing (`rename_all` attributes), nested
type references, and carried-over doc comments all match the Rust source exactly. I also verified
serde's actual behavior for bare `Option<T>` struct fields (no `#[serde(default)]`) with a small
reproduction (`cargo run` against a throwaway crate): missing keys still deserialize to `None`
because serde special-cases `Option<T>` fields, so the "required-but-nullable" shape ts-rs emits
for fields like `AdditionalFileSystemPermissions.read`/`.write` does not cause spurious
deserialization failures for JSON producers that omit them — it is merely a stricter-than-necessary
TypeScript type, not a functional bug.

`AppsReadParams.appIds` documents "The server accepts at most 100 ids and deduplicates repeated ids
while preserving their first-request order." This is enforced in

dedup via `HashSet` while iterating in order), so the documented contract matches the actual
server-side behavior.

No inconsistencies, contract mismatches, or hand-edit drift were found among the 30 files
assigned to this shard.

- `FsRemoveParams` (`codex-rs/app-server-protocol/schema/typescript/v2/FsRemoveParams.ts`): the doc comments "Defaults to `true`" for both `recursive` and `force` accurately match the implementation in `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/fs_processor.rs` (`params.recursive.unwrap_or(true)`, `params.force.unwrap_or(true)`) and the identical logic in `codex-rs/exec-server/src/fs_helper.rs`. This is a maximally destructive default for an unqualified `fs/remove({path})` call, but it is deliberate and explicitly covered by `codex-rs/app-server/tests/suite/v2/fs.rs::fs_remove_...` (asserting `"fs/remove should default to recursive+force for directory trees"`), so it is a documented, intentional, tested design choice rather than a doc/implementation mismatch.
- `FsCopyParams.recursive` (`FsCopyParams.ts`): doc says "Required for directory copies; ignored for file copies." Confirmed by `codex-rs/app-server/tests/suite/v2/fs.rs::fs_copy_rejects_directory_without_recursive`, which asserts the server rejects a directory copy with `recursive: false` with `"fs/copy requires recursive: true when sourcePath is a directory"`.
- `FeedbackUploadResponse.promptHash` (`FeedbackUploadResponse.ts`): doc claims a "whitespace-normalized SHA-256 of the session base instructions" that excludes later developer messages and is `null` when the rollout has no prompt metadata. Verified against `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/feedback_processor.rs::normalized_prompt_hash` (`prompt.split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" ")` then SHA-256) and `feedback_turn_metadata_from_rollout`, which only reads `RolloutItem::SessionMeta(..).meta.base_instructions` and returns `None` when absent.
- `FsGetMetadataResponse.createdAtMs` / `modifiedAtMs` (`FsGetMetadataResponse.ts`): doc claims Unix milliseconds "when available, otherwise `0`." Verified against `codex-rs/exec-server/src/local_file_system.rs` (`metadata.created().ok().map_or(0, system_time_to_unix_ms)`), and `system_time_to_unix_ms` itself falls back to `0` rather than panicking for pre-epoch or overflowing timestamps.

- Enum string-literal values match `#[serde(rename = ...)]` / `#[serde(rename_all = ...)]` on the Rust side, including mixed casing conventions per type (`PluginAvailability`/`PluginInstallPolicy` use `SCREAMING_SNAKE`-ish literal strings, `PluginDisabledReason` uses `snake_case`, `PluginListMarketplaceKind` uses kebab-case, `PluginSearchScope` uses camelCase) — each matches its Rust enum's own attribute, so the inconsistency across types is intentional and source-driven, not a generation bug.

`codex-rs/app-server-protocol/schema/typescript/v2/` (the `ThreadSection*` through
`ThreadUnarchivedNotification` alphabetical slice). Each file carries the
"GENERATED CODE! DO NOT MODIFY BY HAND!" banner, and the crate enforces this
mechanically: `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/schema_fixtures_tests.rs::typescript_schema_fixtures_match_generated`
diffs the vendored fixture tree against a freshly regenerated tree from the Rust
source on every test run, and `stable_precomputed_exports_match_schema_fixtures` /
`experimental_precomputed_exports_match_generated` further check precomputed
export bundles. This means any drift between these `.ts` files and their Rust
source-of-truth (`codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread.rs` and
related modules) would fail CI, so I cross-checked several of the more
interesting shapes directly against that source rather than treating the CI
guarantee as a substitute:

- `ThreadShellCommandParams` — the doc comment ("this runs unsandboxed with full
  access rather than inheriting the thread sandbox policy," and the
  non-negative/zero-means-immediate-timeout semantics for `timeoutMs`) matches
  the struct definition and doc comments in `thread.rs`, and the handler
  (`thread_shell_command_inner` in `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs`)
  validates `timeoutMs` is non-negative via `u64::try_from`, rejects an empty
  command, and gates the call behind `ensure_direct_input_allowed` before
  submitting `Op::RunUserShellCommand`, consistent with the documented contract.
- `ThreadTimelineEntry` — the four discriminated-union variants (`item`,
  `realtime`, `turnStarted`, `turnCompleted`) and their field names/optionality
  (e.g. `startedAt: number | null` on both `turnStarted` and `turnCompleted`)
  match the `ThreadTimelineEntry` enum in `thread.rs` exactly, including the
  `#[ts(rename = ...)]` and `#[ts(type = "number | null")]` overrides.
- `ThreadStartParams.serviceTier` renders as `string | null | null` (a doubled
  null union). This looks like a typo at first glance, but it is the correct,
  intentional rendering of a triple-state field: the Rust field is
  `service_tier: Option<Option<String>>` with
  `deserialize_with = "deserialize_double_option"` /
  `serialize_with = "serialize_double_option"`, used to distinguish "omitted"
  from "explicitly set to null" from "set to a value." The `#[ts(optional =
  nullable)]` attribute makes the outer `Option` both optional and nullable,
  and `ts-rs` separately renders the inner `Option<String>` as `string | null`,
  producing the redundant-but-harmless union. TypeScript treats `T | null |
  null` identically to `T | null`, so this has no functional effect on
  consumers; it is just a slightly confusing artifact of the codegen for this
  one intentionally double-`Option` field.
- Verified that every relative `import type { X } from "./X"` / `"../X"` path
  across the files that have imports (`ThreadSectionListResponse`,
  `ThreadSectionUpdateParams/Response`, `ThreadSettings`,
  `ThreadSettingsUpdatedNotification`, `ThreadStartParams/Response`,
  `ThreadStartedNotification`, `ThreadStatus`, `ThreadStatusChangedNotification`,
  `ThreadTimelineEntry`, `ThreadTokenUsage(UpdatedNotification)`,
  `ThreadTurnsListParams/Response`, `ThreadUnarchiveResponse`,
  `ThreadUnarchivedNotification`) resolves to an existing sibling `.ts` file on
  disk; none are dangling.
- Confirmed `ThreadStartParams.ts` intentionally omits several fields present
  on the Rust struct (`allowProviderModelFallback`, `runtimeWorkspaceRoots`,
  `permissions`, `multiAgentMode`, `historyMode`) — these are all tagged
  `#[experimental(...)]` in `thread.rs` and are filtered out of the stable
  (non-experimental) TypeScript export by the experimental-fields filter in
  `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/export.rs`, which itself has dedicated unit
  tests (e.g. `experimental_type_fields_ts_filter_handles_generated_command_params_shape`).
  This is by design, not a missing-field bug.

No correctness, security, error-handling, or API-contract defects were found
in this shard; the files are pure generated type declarations with no logic of
their own, and the parts of the generation pipeline and consuming Rust
handlers I spot-checked to validate specific shapes were consistent with what
these files declare.

- All 30 files are `ts-rs`-generated TypeScript mirrors of Rust structs/enums under `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/` (`turn.rs`, `thread_data.rs`, `thread.rs`, `thread_usage.rs`, `item.rs`, `config.rs`). Cross-checked each generated shape (field names, optionality via `?`, nullability, enum variants, camelCase renaming) against the corresponding `#[derive(TS)]` struct/enum definitions and found them accurate, including the `#[ts(optional = nullable)]` vs plain-`Option` distinction and enum `#[serde(rename_all = ...)]` conventions.
- `TurnStartParams.ts` / `TurnSteerParams.ts` omit several fields that exist on the corresponding Rust structs (`responsesapiClientMetadata`, `additionalContext`, `environments`, `runtimeWorkspaceRoots`, `permissions`, `collaborationMode`, the deprecated multi-agent-mode field). This looked at first like a stale/incomplete export, but it is intentional: every omitted field carries `#[experimental("...")]` in `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/turn.rs`, and `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/export.rs` (`filter_experimental_ts` / `filter_experimental_type_fields_ts_contents`) deliberately strips experimental fields from the default (non-experimental) generated schema. The public `v2/` schema files are expected to exclude these fields.
- `TurnStartParams.serviceTier` is typed `string | null | null` (a duplicated `| null`). This traces to `service_tier: Option<Option<String>>` in the Rust struct with custom `serialize_double_option`/`deserialize_double_option` helpers implementing an intentional tri-state (absent = don't change, explicit null = reset, string = set). The doubled `null` in the union is a harmless `ts-rs` cosmetic artifact of not collapsing nested `Option` — `T | null | null` is semantically identical to `T | null` in TypeScript — not a functional defect.
- `ToolRequestUserInputParams.ts` / `ToolRequestUserInputResponse.ts` / `ToolRequestUserInputAnswer.ts` / `ToolRequestUserInputOption.ts` / `ToolRequestUserInputQuestion.ts` match their Rust source (`codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs`) including the custom `Deserialize` impl that defaults `isBlocking` to `true` for backward compatibility on the read side, which does not affect the `Serialize`-derived shape reflected in the `.ts` file.
- `ToolsV2.ts` (`web_search`) correctly reflects `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]` on the Rust struct, unlike most other files in this shard which use `camelCase` — verified this is a deliberate per-struct override, not an inconsistency.

- `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/export.rs` and `precomputed_exports.rs`: the TypeScript/JSON-schema export pipeline (namespace rewriting, experimental-field/method filtering for both the live-codegen and precomputed-artifact code paths, `build_flat_v2_schema`'s ref-flattening/rewriting, definition-collision detection) is exercised by an extensive matching test suite and the logic reads correctly, including the `validated_relative_path` traversal guard in `precomputed_exports.rs` applied to the embedded, compile-time `include_bytes!` archives.
- `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs`: the large `client_request_definitions!` / `server_request_definitions!` / `server_notification_definitions!` / `client_notification_definitions!` macros and their generated `ClientRequest`/`ServerRequest`/`ServerNotification`/`ClientResponse` enums, `TryFrom<JSONRPCRequest>` conversions, and experimental-reason propagation were read in full; the generated code and accompanying serialization round-trip tests are internally consistent.
- `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/item_builders.rs` and `item_builders_tests.rs`: command/patch/guardian item projection (secret redaction via `redact_secrets`, path resolution via `PathUri::join`, guardian-status-to-approval-review mapping) reads correctly and the cross-turn guardian stdin-review regression test is a meaningful check.
- `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/export_user_verification.rs` and its tests: the TS/JSON filtering of the experimental `openai/userVerification` elicitation mode preserves the other stable elicitation modes as verified by both directions of the round-trip tests.

- `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/thread_history.rs` / `thread_history_projection.rs` /
  `thread_history_projection_tests.rs`: reviewed the full `ThreadHistoryBuilder` state machine
  (turn open/close/rollback, `TurnItemIndex` push/upsert dedup, the `ThreadHistoryChangeAccumulator`
  coalescing logic, and the stateless `project_rollout_line` projector). Traced the turn-id
  resolution order for `TurnAborted`/`TurnComplete` (exact match on `current_turn` → exact match in

- `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread_data.rs` — the hand-written `Deserialize for Thread` (via the `ThreadCompatibility` shim, added to tolerate old servers omitting `projectId`) mirrors every field of `Thread` with matching `#[serde(default)]` placement; no field is dropped or misdefaulted.

- `codex-rs/app-server-test-client/src/plugin_analytics_mutation_smoke.rs` — the install/uninstall mutation smoke flow's error handling correctly distinguishes clean/dirty/unknown restoration states and always attempts to leave the remote account in its original (uninstalled) state, printing an explicit recovery command on failure.

I read all 30 files assigned to this shard in full (including every test file) and traced the
security- and correctness-critical paths below against their test coverage. No defect met the bar
for a finding (exploitable now, wrong under ordinary conditions, wrong under conditions a reader
would not expect to be excluded, or a safe-to-defer-but-real issue).

- **`transport/auth.rs` websocket bearer auth (capability token + signed JWT).** The capability
  token path compares SHA-256 digests with `constant_time_eq_32` (no timing side channel). The
  signed-bearer path pins `Validation::new(Algorithm::HS256)` (so an `alg: none` or RS256-signed
  token cannot bypass verification — confirmed against the `signed_bearer_token_verification_rejects_alg_none_tokens`
  test), disables the library's own `exp`/`nbf`/`aud` checks and re-implements them manually with
  clock-skew handling in `validate_jwt_claims`, and enforces a 32-byte minimum shared secret. The
  `exp` claim is structurally required by `JwtClaims` (non-`Option`), so `required_spec_claims.clear()`
  does not weaken the missing-`exp`-is-rejected guarantee. Traced against all nine unit tests in
  the file, including the tamper/duplicate/multi-audience/alg-none cases.
- **`transport/remote_control/protocol.rs` `normalize_remote_control_base_url`.** The scheme/host
  allowlist (`chatgpt.com`, `*.chatgpt.com`, `chatgpt-staging.com`, `*.chatgpt-staging.com` over
  HTTPS only, plus HTTP/HTTPS for loopback/`localhost`) correctly rejects the suffix-confusion
  cases in its own test (`chatgpt.com.evil.com`, `evilchatgpt.com`, `foo.localhost`) — verified the
  `ends_with(".chatgpt.com")` logic manually against `"evilchatgpt.com"` (15 chars) vs the 12-char
  suffix `.chatgpt.com`, which does not match because there is no separating dot.
- **`transport/remote_control/segment.rs` reassembly.** Per-chunk decode bounds
  (`chunk_end = min(message_size_bytes, chunk_start + decoded_len)`) keep the base64 decode target
  slice from ever exceeding the declared `message_size_bytes`, and an over-budget decode correctly
  surfaces as `DecodeSliceError::OutputSliceTooSmall` → drop rather than a panic or OOB write.
  Metadata-mismatch, out-of-order, and stale/duplicate-chunk cases are all exercised by
  `segment_tests.rs` and match the implementation.
- **`daemon_shutdown.rs` PID-scoped shutdown file.** `take_shutdown_request` bounds the read to 11
  bytes (`u32::MAX` is 10 digits + 1 guard byte) and does an exact byte-for-byte comparison against
  `pid.to_string()`, so a descendant process that inherited the env var cannot match a shorter PID
  by prefix (verified against `inherited_control_path_cannot_consume_another_process_request`).
- **`transport/remote_control/server_api.rs` retry/backoff/error-kind classification.** Traced
  `RemoteControlServerRequestError::io_error`'s status→`ErrorKind` mapping and `is_transient`
  against every case in `remote_control_server_request_error_classifies_status_before_timeout`;
  `retry_after_with_jitter`/`parse_retry_after`/`refresh_deferral` correctly treat `Retry-After` as
  a lower bound (jitter only ever adds, never subtracts) and preserve absolute deadlines across a
  slow body read.
- **`transport/remote_control/mod.rs` / `controller.rs` / `desired_state.rs` account-switch and
  enrollment-selection state machine.** `RemoteControl::session()` forces `Disabled` on the next
  session after an account switch away from a previously-authenticated session (so remote control
  does not silently carry over to a new ChatGPT account), while preserving the prior desired state
  across a switch away from an *unauthenticated* session. `RemoteControlEnrollmentLease`'s
  `Drop` always commits the current (possibly partially-updated) enrollment snapshot back to the
  shared `StdMutex`, including on early-return error paths, which is the intended "cache what we
  learned even on failure" behavior and matches `persisted_enable_does_not_follow_auth_to_an_account_without_a_preference`.
- **`transport/remote_control/client_tracker.rs` / `websocket.rs` seq/ack bookkeeping.**
  `BoundedOutboundBuffer::ack`'s cumulative-then-per-segment cursor comparison
  (`(seq_id, segment_id) <= (acked_seq_id, acked_segment_id.unwrap_or(usize::MAX))`) is idempotent
  against replayed acks (already-removed entries simply don't match again, so the `used_tx` counter
  cannot underflow), and `close_client`/`remove_client` unconditionally clean up the corresponding
  `legacy_stream_ids` entry on every teardown path, so that map cannot grow unbounded.
- Grepped every non-test path in this shard for `.unwrap()`/`.expect()`/raw `Mutex::lock().unwrap()`:
  all production-code lock acquisitions use `unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner)`
  (poison-tolerant) and every `.unwrap()`/`.expect()` hit is inside a `#[cfg(test)]` module or
  `*_tests.rs` file — no panic-on-attacker-input path was found in production code in this shard.

- `codex-rs/app-server-transport/src/transport/unix_socket.rs`: `set_control_socket_permissions`
  chmods the bound socket to `0o600` *after* `UnixListener::bind`, which looks like a TOCTOU
  window at first glance. It isn't exploitable: `prepare_control_socket_path` calls
  `codex_uds::prepare_private_socket_directory(parent)` first, and that helper (in
  `codex-rs/uds/src/lib.rs`, `SOCKET_DIR_MODE = 0o700`) chmods the *containing directory* to
  owner-only before the socket file is created there, including when the directory already
  existed with looser permissions (verified via
  `prepare_private_socket_directory_sets_existing_permissions_to_owner_only` in
  `codex-rs/uds/src/lib_tests.rs`). A directory that unauthorized users cannot traverse makes
  the interim file mode on the socket irrelevant; the later chmod is defense in depth, not the
  primary control.
- `codex-rs/app-server/src/connection_rpc_gate.rs`: `ConnectionRpcGate::run` reads `accepting`
  and calls `self.tasks.token()` while still holding the `accepting` mutex guard, and `close()`
  takes the same mutex before flipping `accepting` and closing the tracker. This fully
  serializes admission against shutdown so a handler can never be admitted after `close()` has
  started, matching the documented "queued work is rejected, started handlers finish" contract;
  the test suite (`close_returns_while_started_run_remains_active`,
  `shutdown_drops_late_runs_while_waiting_for_inflight_work`, etc.) exercises this correctly.
- `codex-rs/app-server/src/dynamic_tools.rs`: the `InputAudio`/`InputImage` content checks
  reject any URL that isn't an inline `data:` URL (or, for images, a known-safe reference),
  which is a reasonable SSRF guard against dynamic-tool responses smuggling remote URLs for the
  host to fetch. The `.get(.."data:".len())` bounds check on `audio_url` uses `str::get`, which
  returns `None` rather than panicking on short strings or non-char-boundary indices, so
  malformed/short URLs are correctly treated as invalid rather than causing a panic.
- `codex-rs/app-server/src/config_manager_service.rs` /
  `config_manager_service_credential_edits.rs`: `apply_edits` restricts all config writes to
  the resolved user config path (`paths_match(&allowed_path, &provided_path)`), rejects writes
  to fields covered by exact managed requirements, and validates the resulting effective config
  (including credential-provider remapping) before persisting. This is exercised by an extensive
  set of tests in `config_manager_service_tests.rs` covering managed overrides, legacy profile
  rejection, and credential-provider source-ownership edge cases; nothing in the code path I
  read allows writing outside the user config file or bypassing managed/exact requirements.

- `codex-rs/app-server/src/image_url.rs` (`is_remote_image_url`) and its
  callers in `turn_processor.rs`/`dynamic_tools.rs`: even though the
  scheme-prefix check is fairly permissive (e.g. a scheme with embedded
  whitespace before the colon would not be classified as remote), the same
  `is_remote_image_url` logic is independently duplicated in
  `codex-rs/core/src/image_preparation.rs::prepare_image`, which core runs on
  every image before use. Any input that slips past the app-server-side
  validation is still rejected by core's own check, so there is no client
  observed bypass of the "no remote image URL" invariant.
- `codex-rs/app-server/src/notification_media.rs`: `without_notification_media`
  and `without_thread_item_media` are exhaustive matches over
  `ServerNotification`/`ThreadItem`/`ResponseItem` variants, so the compiler
  forces new variants to be classified; the one known gap (oversized MCP tool
  results that core has already collapsed into a text preview that can still
  contain inline media) is called out in-source via `TODO(ruslan)` and is not
  a silent omission.
- `codex-rs/app-server/src/fs_watch.rs`: watch/unwatch state is keyed by
  `(connection_id, watch_id)`, and `connection_closed` removes only the
  entries owned by the closing connection; the existing tests
  (`unwatch_is_scoped_to_the_connection_that_created_the_watch`,
  `connection_closed_removes_only_that_connections_watches`) match the
  implementation's scoping behavior.
- `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/account_processor.rs`
  (`get_auth_status_response`): token values are withheld for
  workload-identity, `Headers`, `AgentIdentity`, and `PersonalAccessToken`
  credentials even when `include_token` is requested, and refresh-failure
  errors/messages are never logged verbatim (only `err.code`), consistent
  with the "don't leak credentials" comments elsewhere in the file.

- `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/apps_processor/installed.rs` and
  `installed_tests.rs`: force-refresh vs. cached-snapshot dispositions, metric recording
  (including the failure path that intentionally records no duration sample), and the
  `model_visible_tool_names` gating for hosted-thread vs. threadless refresh were traced
  end-to-end and behave as the tests assert.
- `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/feedback_thread_index.rs` and its test
  file: verified the omission-count arithmetic (`omitted_count - omitted_thread_ids.len()`)
  cannot underflow — `omitted_thread_ids` is always a prefix-bounded subset of the same
  filtered iterator used to compute `omitted_count` — and that dedup/sort/priority
  ordering matches the two accompanying tests.
- `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/mcp_event_stream.rs`: subscription-limit
  enforcement is check-and-insert under a single mutex acquisition (no TOCTOU window),
  cleanup on timeout/stop aborts and awaits the task, and the exponential-backoff
  reconnect loop is bounded by both `MAX_MCP_EVENT_STREAM_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS` and an
  absolute deadline.
- `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/command_exec_processor.rs`: confirmed
  `StartedNetworkProxy`/`NetworkProxyHandle` have `Drop` impls that stop the proxy
  runtime, so the early-return path after `start_proxy` succeeds but
  `build_exec_request` fails does not leak a running proxy process.
- `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/fs_processor.rs` and
  `process_exec_processor.rs`: both pass no sandbox/no shell-environment-policy
  filtering to their underlying operations, but this matches the documented contract of
  `process/spawn` (`"Spawn a standalone process ... without a Codex sandbox on the host
  where the app server is running"` in `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/process.rs`)
  and is consistent with the local-environment-gated, host-trust model used throughout
  this shard (as opposed to `command_exec_processor.rs`, which does apply the configured
  `shell_environment_policy` because it models the agent-sandboxed exec path). Not a
  defect.
- `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/mcp_processor.rs`:
  `with_mcp_tool_call_thread_id_meta`'s `other => other` fallthrough (non-object `_meta`
  silently skips threadId injection) mirrors the identical, pre-existing pattern in
  `codex-rs/core/src/mcp_tool_call.rs::with_mcp_tool_call_ids_meta`, so this is an
  established codebase convention rather than a defect specific to this file.
- Pagination/cursor handling in `catalog_processor.rs` (`list_models`,
  `experimental_feature_list_response`, `permission_profile_list_response`) and
  `mcp_processor.rs` (`list_mcp_server_status_response`) was checked for off-by-one and
  panic-on-slice risk (`start > total` rejected, `end = start.saturating_add(limit).min(total)`,
  zero-length slices instead of panics when `total == 0`); all four are consistent and
  correct.
- Grepped all 30 files for `.unwrap()`/`.expect()` outside `#[cfg(test)]` modules: none
  found, so no obvious panic-on-untrusted-input paths in this shard.

- `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/search.rs`: initially suspected that `pending_fuzzy_searches` could leak entries keyed by client-supplied `cancellationToken` strings if the enclosing request future were dropped before the post-search cleanup ran. Traced the call path through `message_processor.rs`'s request dispatch into `connection_rpc_gate.rs`'s `ConnectionRpcGate::run`: once a request future is admitted (token acquired), `close()`/`shutdown()` only stop *new* futures from starting — an in-flight future always runs to completion (`future.await` is never aborted). So the `pending_fuzzy_searches` cleanup at the end of `fuzzy_file_search` always executes; no leak.
- `codex-rs/app-server/src/turn_admission.rs` + `turn_admission_tests.rs`: admit/drain reference counting via `Mutex<AdmissionState>` and `watch::Sender<usize>` is correct and covered by a test that exercises drain racing with in-flight and automatic admissions.
- `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_serialization.rs`: the per-key FIFO/shared-read queue (exclusive vs. shared-read batching, `discard_closed` for connection-closed requests) is extensively covered by its own test suite (FIFO ordering, concurrent distinct keys, closed-gate skipping, shared-read concurrency, and write/read fairness), and the logic matches those tests on inspection.
- `codex-rs/app-server/src/thread_status.rs`: `ThreadWatchManager`'s runtime-fact tracking (`RuntimeFacts`, guard-based pending-request counters with `saturating_add`/`saturating_sub`, per-thread `watch` channels) correctly derives `ThreadStatus` and only emits change notifications when the computed status actually changes.
- `codex-rs/app-server/src/transport.rs` + `transport_tests.rs`: outbound routing correctly filters experimental notifications by per-connection capability, strips `additionalPermissions` from `CommandExecutionRequestApproval` for non-experimental clients, and disconnects (rather than blocks) slow connections during broadcast while non-broadcast sends to a full stdio queue correctly wait instead of dropping.
- `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_resume_redaction.rs`: redaction of MCP tool call arguments/results/errors and removal of image-generation items for ChatGPT remote clients is correct and matches its tests.
- `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/remote_control_processor.rs`: error-kind-to-JSONRPC-error mapping and the `pairingCode`/`manualPairingCode` XOR validation are consistent with their tests.

- `codex-rs/app-server/src/turn_cost_worker.rs` and
  `codex-rs/app-server/src/turn_cost_worker_chatgpt.rs`: traced the full
  observation → tracking → polling → pricing pipeline, including the
  `MAX_TRACKED_TURNS` / `MAX_TRACKED_RESPONSES_PER_TURN` / `MAX_QUERY_TURNS` /
  `MAX_STALLED_POLL_ATTEMPTS` bounds, the `BackendAvailability` state machine
  (`Ready` / `RetryProbe` / `AwaitingAuthChange` / `Disabled`) and its status-code
  mapping (401/403 vs 429 vs other 4xx vs 5xx/timeout), the auth-change
  invalidation path that clears in-flight turns and drains the channel, and the
  SiWC/ChatGPT-specific path that requires every locally observed response id to
  appear in `settled_response_ids` before emitting a price (guarding against a
  partial/projected estimate being treated as final). Verified the integer
  micros→dollars formatting (`format!("{}.{:06}", micros / 1_000_000, micros %
  1_000_000)`) against the exhaustive `test_case` table in
  `turn_cost_worker_chatgpt_tests.rs`, including the `i64::MAX` boundary. Also
  confirmed, by reading every `warn!`/`debug!` call site, that only HTTP status
  codes are logged on failure and response bodies are never included, matching
  `turn_cost_failures_do_not_log_response_bodies`.
- `codex-rs/app-server/src/user_verification.rs`,
  `user_verification_adapter.rs`, and `user_verification_auth.rs`: traced the
  request-guard/cancellation lifecycle (`CancelOnDrop`, the bounded native
  worker semaphore, the double `guard.check()` before and after native work,
  and the re-check performed after the response is queued but before it is
  actually sent), the origin gating that blocks `WebSocket`/`RemoteControl`
  connections from every operation except `Status`, and the input validation in
  `validate()` (base64 length bounds consistent with the 4096-byte decoded
  challenge cap, verified arithmetically against the 5462-character encoded
  bound). Cross-referenced the ownership/eligibility logic in
  `outgoing_message.rs` (`send_request_to_connections`,
  `take_connection_callback`, `connection_closed`) that this module relies on,
  and confirmed it re-checks eligibility after acquiring the callback lock to
  close the race the `verification_disconnect_during_registration_leaves_no_callback_or_request`
  test exercises, and that a revision-only mismatch (independent of identity)
  is treated as a hard invalidation as intended by
  `account_switch_back_rejects_proof_before_the_auth_watcher_runs`. No
  panics/unwraps/expects were found in any of the non-test production files in
  this shard.
- `codex-rs/app-server/src/user_verification_response.rs`: confirmed
  `_meta` is stripped unconditionally before returning any elicitation
  response and that only content shaped like `UserVerificationProof` is
  forwarded on `Accept`, with every other case (missing/invalid content,
  decode/RecvError) collapsing to `Cancel`.
- `codex-rs/app-server/tests/common/*.rs`: reviewed all fixture/helper files
  (`analytics_server.rs`, `auth_fixtures.rs`, `config.rs`, `json_logging.rs`,
  `mock_model_server.rs`, `models_cache.rs`, `responses.rs`, `rollout.rs`,

This shard consists entirely of `codex-rs/app-server` integration-test sources and
their shared test-support helpers (`tests/common/rpc_delay.rs`,
`tests/common/rpc_delay_tests.rs`, `tests/common/test_app_server.rs`, and the
`tests/suite/**` files including the full `v2/` subtree). No production
(non-test) code is present in this shard. I read every file in full (including
paginated re-reads for the three files that exceeded a single page:
`test_app_server.rs`, `v2/account.rs`, and `v2/config_rpc.rs`) and did not find
a defect meeting the bar for a `CR-###` finding. Areas specifically scrutinized:

- **`rpc_delay.rs` / `rpc_delay_tests.rs`** — the hand-rolled one-way-delay TCP
  proxy used to simulate exec-server latency. Traced the chunk-timestamping
  queue, the bounded-channel backpressure (`FORWARD_QUEUE_CHUNKS`), error
  propagation from the spawned reader task through `AbortOnDropHandle` and the
  double `?` on `JoinHandle::await`, and the `JoinSet`/`Drop` cleanup chain in
  `WebsocketDelayInterposer` (dropping the outer accept task drops the
  `JoinSet`, which tokio aborts on drop, correctly tearing down all
  in-flight proxied connections). This held up under a full trace of both the
  happy path and the write-failure/cancellation path exercised by
  `write_error_cancels_reader`.

- **`test_app_server.rs`** — the `TestAppServer` field declaration order versus
  the documented Drop-order requirement (delayed exec-server torn down before
  the owned `CODEX_HOME` TempDir is removed) is correct: fields drop
  top-to-bottom, `_delayed_exec_server` precedes `_owned_codex_home`, and the
  custom `Drop for TestAppServer` impl synchronously waits for the main child
  process to exit (via `try_wait`/`start_kill` polling) before the compiler's
  auto-generated field drops run, so the primary app-server child cannot still
  be alive with `codex_home` as its cwd when the TempDir is deleted.
  `shutdown_gracefully`'s `tokio::select!` race between `process.wait()` and
  draining stdout to a sink is sound for both exit orderings.

- **`v2/connection_handling_websocket.rs` / `connection_handling_websocket_unix.rs`**
  — websocket auth tests (missing/invalid capability tokens, expired/not-yet-valid/
  wrong-issuer/wrong-audience/wrong-signature signed bearer tokens, browser-origin
  rejection without auth, short shared-secret rejection, unauthenticated
  non-loopback listener refusal) each assert on the specific rejection reason,
  not just "some error", and the signed-bearer-token helper constructs a
  correctly-shaped compact JWT for both valid and tampered cases.

- **`v2/command_exec.rs`** — the managed `deny_read` enforcement test
  (`command_exec_enforces_managed_deny_read_requirements`) correctly
  distinguishes managed (requirements.toml) restrictions, which apply
  regardless of the chosen sandbox mechanism, from ordinary permission-profile
  restrictions, which only apply when that profile is selected; and the env
  override test confirms the server strips client-supplied
  `OPENAI_FEDERATION_RULE_ID`/`openai_identity_token_file` overrides rather
  than honoring them, which is the security-relevant property the test name
  implies.

- **`v2/config_rpc.rs`** — spot-checked several of the managed-vs-user config
  precedence and provider-remapping/atomicity tests (e.g.
  `managed_auth_settings_are_exposed_enforced_and_read_only`,
  `config_provider_remapping_rejects_invalid_replacements_atomically`) for
  internal consistency between the request sent and the expected persisted
  TOML / returned origins; found no mismatches.

No credential-bearing files (`.env`, `*.pem`, `id_rsa`, `.npmrc`, etc.) appear
in this shard's file list; the synthetic secrets written by tests (`auth.json`,
`.env`, fake AWS credentials files) are test fixtures with hardcoded
placeholder values, not real credentials.

- `curated_mcp_sync.rs` (`existing_thread_loads_api_curated_mcp_after_auth_switch_sync`): verifies
  that curated marketplace Git sync never executes a malicious `insteadOf`/`ext::` rewrite placed
  in the *local* (repo-scoped) git config of `$CODEX_HOME`, which would only fire if sync code ran
  `git` with `cwd` inside `$CODEX_HOME`'s repository. The fixture correctly isolates the "legitimate"
  rewrite via `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` and gates a real network operation (`ls-remote`) behind a barrier so
  the assertion (`!malicious_git_helper_marker.exists()`) is checked before sync can race past it.
- `daybreak_access.rs` (`daybreak_access_respects_plugin_provenance`): confirms that a caller-supplied
  `openai/entitlementContext` value in a direct `McpServerToolCall` request is never honored (only the
  model-invoked path for a verified/selected plugin can populate it), and that the ChatGPT bearer token
  never leaks into the returned tool metadata (`!metadata.to_string().contains("daybreak-test-token")`).
- `executor_mcp.rs` (`selected_executor_plugin_exposes_its_mcps_only_to_that_thread`): confirms
  host-owned OAuth credentials for a plugin-selected MCP server are never sent to the executor's
  copy of the same server, and that the executor-issued OAuth credential is persisted under a
  different `server_name` than the host's, keeping the two credential stores from merging.
- `git_attribution.rs` (`git_attribution_follows_authenticated_workspace_policy`): confirms that a
  per-thread `chatgpt_base_url` config override cannot redirect the attribution-settings lookup
  away from the process-level base URL (`settings_server` receives zero requests to
  `/backend-api/wham/settings/user`), preventing a workspace/project config from hijacking that
  network call.
- `dynamic_tools.rs`: remote (non-data-URL) image/audio URLs returned from a dynamic tool call are
  correctly rejected and surfaced as a model-visible error rather than fetched, and legacy vs.
  canonical dynamic-tool schema variants are correctly rejected when mixed.
- `guardian_v2.rs` and its `guardian_*_tests.rs` submodules: broad, consistent coverage of Guardian
  sync/async review invalidation on root/user authorization changes, checkpoint-compatibility
  fail-closed behavior, and cross-thread isolation of reviewer sessions — the assertions align with
  the described intent in every scenario I traced.

This shard consists entirely of `codex-rs/app-server` integration test files (v2 suite):
`initialize.rs`, `luna_reserve.rs`, `marketplace_add.rs`, `marketplace_remove.rs`,
`marketplace_upgrade.rs`, `mcp_event_stream.rs`, `mcp_protocol_default.rs`,
`mcp_resource.rs`, `mcp_resource_origin.rs`, `mcp_server_elicitation.rs`,
`mcp_server_status.rs`, `mcp_tool.rs`, `memory_read.rs`, `memory_reset.rs`,
`misalignment_policy.rs`, `mod.rs`, `model_auto_review.rs`, `model_list.rs`,
`model_provider_capabilities_read.rs`, `multi_agent_v2_developer_instructions.rs`,

`plugin_install.rs`, `plugin_list.rs`, `plugin_read.rs`, `plugin_reconcile.rs`,

Every file in the shard was read in full (several — `mcp_resource.rs`, `plugin_install.rs`,
`plugin_list.rs`, `plugin_read.rs` — are 1,800 to 5,900 lines and were read across
multiple paginated calls). These are black-box JSON-RPC integration tests that spin up
`TestAppServer` instances against mocked OpenAI Responses/Apps/plugin-catalog backends
(`wiremock`, custom `axum` routers, and `rmcp` MCP servers) and assert on protocol
responses, notifications, persisted config/cache files, and analytics payloads.

Specific things checked and found consistent:
- Resource cleanup: every test that `tokio::spawn`s a custom MCP/apps/OAuth server via
  `axum::serve` pairs it with `handle.abort(); let _ = handle.await;` (or `drop`s a
  reserved `TcpListener` before the real server binds to that port), so no dangling
  server tasks were found.
- Negative "no extra network call happened" assertions (`wait_for_remote_plugin_request_count`
  with `expected_count: 0` and similar) are consistently placed either after a full
  JSON-RPC response has already been received (guaranteeing any synchronous backend calls
  already happened) or after a separate helper (`wait_for_cached_remote_catalog_plugin_ids`,
  etc.) has already confirmed the relevant background work completed — so the pattern isn't
  actually racy despite the reliance on `sleep`-then-check in a few spots.
- Auth/callback/OAuth test fixtures (`mcp_server_status.rs`, `plugin_install.rs`) use only
  synthetic bearer tokens/account ids (`"chatgpt-token"`, `"account-123"`) consistent with the
  rest of the test-support crate; nothing resembling a real credential is embedded.
- Cross-file helper duplication (e.g. `write_plugin_marketplace`, `write_installed_plugin`,
  `mount_remote_plugin_bundle` appear with slightly different signatures in `plugin_install.rs`,
  `plugin_list.rs`, `plugin_read.rs`, `plugin_share.rs`, `plugin_search.rs`) is intentional
  per-file duplication rather than a shared crate, and each copy was checked independently
  for correctness against its own call sites.

No correctness, security, or error-handling defects were found in this shard that could be
substantiated with a concrete repro from the source alone (these are test files exercising
an implementation not included in the shard, so behavioral bugs in the server itself are out
of scope for this review pass).

This shard consists entirely of Rust integration test files (`codex-rs/app-server/tests/suite/v2/`), with no production source in scope:

- `plugin_uninstall.rs` — remote/local plugin uninstall flows, cache namespace scoping, analytics event payloads, and pre-network-call validation of malformed/spaced/path-traversal plugin ids.
- `process_exec.rs` — process spawn/kill lifecycle, output-cap truncation, and local-environment-disabled error path.
- `projects.rs` — project CRUD, recency-based sorting/pagination, thread-to-project assignment/reassignment, cascading unassignment on project delete, and atomic project import with idempotency.
- `rate_limit_reset_credits.rs` / `rate_limits.rs` — auth gating (codex account vs chatgpt auth), backend outcome mapping, timeout-releases-auth-queue behavior, and rate-limit snapshot/banner filtering by account identity.
- `realtime_conversation.rs` — large (4200+ line) end-to-end harness covering WebRTC/websocket v1/v2/v3 realtime sessions, handoff routing, steering, transcript segmentation, and timeline persistence; verified request/response pairing and notification ordering assertions are internally consistent.
- `recommended_plugins.rs`, `remote_control.rs`, `remote_control_auth.rs` — external login plugin-suggestion gating; remote-control enable/disable/pairing/client-management against a hand-rolled HTTP+WebSocket mock backend, including managed-requirements gating and owner-change relay teardown; env var mutation in `remote_control.rs` is confined to a single `#[serial]`-annotated test, avoiding cross-test races.
- `remote_thread_store.rs` — non-local `ThreadStore` config routing and the accompanying "no local persistence artifacts" tripwire assertions.
- `request_permissions.rs`, `request_user_input.rs`, `request_validation.rs` — permission round-trip and question round-trip via server requests, and remote-image-URL / legacy-permission-profile rejection prior to any network call.
- `residency.rs` — managed residency header override verified over both HTTP and WebSocket transports.
- `review.rs` — inline/detached review delivery, deprecation-notice emission, and skill-name collision handling between user and system skills.
- `rollout_migration.rs`, `safety_check_downgrade.rs` — legacy-to-paginated background migration preserving model context; model-reroute/cyber-policy/model-verification/moderation-metadata notification mapping.
- `selected_capability_stack.rs`, `selected_environment.rs` — selected-executor plugin/MCP/skill availability gating across mention timing, environment attach/detach/resume, and environment-scoped instruction/context injection.
- `server_diagnostics.rs`, `session_end.rs` — diagnostics gauge reporting and experimental-capability gating; SessionEnd hook firing on archive/delete/shutdown with correct transcript content.
- `skills_list.rs` — bundled/system skill cache sharing across processes, per-cwd skill configuration, remote-plugin skill cache invalidation/refresh, and extra-roots handling.
- `sleep.rs` — control-tool analytics for clock/sleep tools (including redaction of tool-call argument content from analytics), and external-clock-source sleep polling.
- `thread_archive.rs`, `thread_delete.rs`, `thread_environments.rs`, `thread_fork.rs`, `thread_fork_multi_agent_tests.rs`, `thread_goal_empty_responses.rs` — cross-process writer-ownership conflicts, cascading archive/delete of spawned descendants (including partial-failure and missing-descendant cases), fork boundary semantics (`lastTurnId`/`beforeTurnId`/`exclude_turns`/ephemeral), interrupted-turn freezing on fork, deferred goal continuation across fork/resume, and the empty-goal-continuation breaker.

I read each file in full and traced the assertions against the request/response and notification sequencing each test relies on; I did not find logic errors, unsound assumptions, or missing error handling in the test code itself. No credential-bearing files were present in this shard (auth tokens used are test fixtures such as `"chatgpt-token"` / `"sk-test-key"` passed to local wiremock/loopback servers, not real secrets).

This shard consists entirely of `codex-rs/app-server` integration test files (30 files under
`codex-rs/app-server/tests/suite/v2/`), covering thread lifecycle (`thread_start`, `thread_resume`,
`thread_revert`, `thread_rollback`, `thread_read`, `thread_list`, `thread_loaded_list`,
`thread_sections`, `thread_settings_update`, `thread_metadata_update`, `thread_unarchive`,
`thread_unsubscribe`, `thread_inject_items`, `thread_shell_command`, `thread_status`,
`thread_timeline`, `thread_memory_mode_set`, `thread_name_websocket`, `thread_queue`), turn
lifecycle (`turn_start`, `turn_start_zsh_fork`, `turn_steer`, `turn_interrupt`,
`turn_settings_update`, `turn_cost_otel`), plus `user_verification`, `user_verification_mcp`,
`view_image`, `web_search`, and `windows_sandbox_setup`.

No production (non-test) source files are in this shard, so the review focused on test
correctness: whether assertions actually validate the claimed behavior, whether security-relevant
tests (credential redaction, sub-agent isolation, prompt-injection resistance, remote-client
payload redaction) exercise the right code paths, and whether async/timing-sensitive tests are
free of obvious races or tautological assertions.

Specific areas read in full and found to correctly exercise their target behavior:

- `thread_inject_items.rs`'s `thread_inject_items_cannot_forge_configuration_update_before_or_after_resume`
  test intentionally injects a forged `configuration_update` item and a forged `system` role message
  (including the literal string "Ignore all previous instructions.") as a payload to verify the
  server strips/rejects harness-authored-looking injected content before and after resume. This is a
  defensive test, not a real prompt-injection vector in the codebase; a repo-wide injection scanner
  flagged the substring but it is test fixture data, not an instruction to this reviewer or any agent.
- `thread_metadata_update.rs`'s `thread_metadata_update_sanitizes_git_origin_before_persisting` and
  `thread_list.rs`'s `thread_list_sanitizes_git_info_from_existing_rollouts` correctly assert that
  embedded git credentials are stripped from the API response, the SQLite-backed metadata, and the
  on-disk rollout file.
- `thread_resume.rs`'s `thread_resume_redacts_payloads_for_chatgpt_remote_clients` correctly asserts
  MCP tool arguments/results and image-generation items are redacted/dropped for remote ChatGPT
  clients while a non-remote client retains the full payload (verified via `client_name` gating both
  branches of the same fixture).
- `turn_start.rs`'s `turn_start_exec_approval_toggle_v2` and
  `run_turn_start_exec_approval_rejection_v2` correctly distinguish the client-facing redacted command
  string (bearer token replaced with `[REDACTED_SECRET]`) from the real command actually executed
  (verified indirectly via the subprocess's stdout confirming the unredacted token reached the child
  process), and verify the raw token appears only in the approval request payload, never in
  displayed/aggregated output.
- `turn_start.rs`'s multi-agent-v2 sub-agent isolation test
  (`direct_input_to_multi_agent_v2_subagent_is_rejected`) enumerates a broad set of direct-input RPCs
  (`thread/inject_items`, `turn/start`, `turn/steer`, `thread/approveGuardianDeniedAction`,
  `thread/settings/update`, `thread/shellCommand`, `mcpServer/tool/call`, `thread/compact/start`,
  `turn/settings/update`, `thread/rollback`, `thread/revert`, `review/start` (both delivery modes),
  all `thread/realtime/*` methods, `thread/goal/set`, `thread/goal/clear`) and asserts every one is
  rejected with the same invalid-request error for a v2 sub-agent thread, which is a thorough
  regression guard against a new RPC accidentally bypassing sub-agent isolation.
- `thread_unsubscribe.rs`'s idle-unload tests correctly validate that resubscribing (via
  `thread/resume`) cancels a pending unload timer even past the original deadline, and that losing
  the last subscriber starts a fresh countdown, without any of the classic "assert something didn't
  happen after a too-short sleep" false-negative patterns (the negative-assertion windows are
  deliberately shorter than the configured delay, and the eventual positive assertion still waits on
  the full default timeout).
- `thread_resume.rs`'s `thread_resume_rejoins_running_paginated_thread_with_initial_page` explicitly
  tolerates the known race between a queued resume response and an in-flight turn completing,
  documenting the tolerance in a comment rather than asserting a single racy expected value.
- `windows_sandbox_setup.rs`, `user_verification.rs`, and `user_verification_mcp.rs` are small,
  self-contained, and their assertions match their stated purpose (experimental-capability gating,
  typed unavailability errors, and the elicitation round-trip through a real MCP transport).

No correctness, security, or test-quality defects were found in this shard at medium-depth review.

- `codex-rs/apply-patch`: the chunk-matching/replacement pipeline (`seek_sequence.rs`, `file_update.rs::compute_replacements`/`apply_replacements`, `text_file.rs::SourceFile`), the streaming and non-streaming parsers (`streaming_parser.rs`, `parser.rs`), and the bash-heredoc interception logic (`invocation.rs::extract_apply_patch_from_bash`) were read in full. All 69 lib unit tests and all 30 integration tests (`cli.rs`, `no_follow.rs`, `scenarios.rs`, `tool.rs`) pass against this worktree. I traced the ordering/overlap invariants that `text_file.rs::SourceFile::apply_replacements` relies on (guarded only by a `debug_assert!`, which is compiled out in release builds) and confirmed by construction that `compute_replacements` can never produce out-of-order or overlapping replacements for a single file — the `eof` search branch's `eof_start.max(start)` clamp for `PreserveLineEndings` mode, together with monotonically advancing `line_index` across chunks, makes the invariant hold for all parser-produced input.
- `codex-rs/aws-auth`: reviewed SigV4 signing (`signing.rs`), config/credentials loading (`config.rs`), profile discovery (`discovery.rs`), and the public `AwsAuthContext`/`AwsCredentialsProvider` surface in `lib.rs`, including the `Debug` impls that redact `AwsAccessKeys` fields. I specifically tested the hypothesis that `AwsAuthContext::load_with_access_keys`/`load_with_credentials_provider` could spuriously fail via `Self::load`'s `MissingCredentialsProvider` check when no ambient AWS credentials are discoverable (env vars, profile files) — built and ran a scratch test with `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`/`AWS_PROFILE` unset and `HOME`/`AWS_CONFIG_FILE`/`AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE` pointed at a nonexistent path — and confirmed `load_with_access_keys` still succeeds, because `aws_config`'s default loader always attaches a credentials-provider object (lazy failure happens later, at `provide_credentials()`, not at the `credentials_provider()` accessor used here). No defect.
- `codex-rs/arg0`: `arg0_dispatch`, PATH-alias construction (`prepare_path_entry_for_codex_aliases`), the per-session lock file and `janitor_cleanup` stale-directory sweep, and `.env` loading (`load_dotenv`/`set_filtered`, which correctly blocks `CODEX_*`-prefixed keys case-insensitively) were reviewed; all crate tests pass.
- `codex-rs/backend-client`: reviewed the REST wrapper surface (`client.rs`, `chatgpt_turn_cost.rs`, `rate_limit_resets.rs`, `thread_usage.rs`) including the rate-limit/plan-type mapping functions and the `RequestError`/`decode_json` error paths; the `get_rate_limits` non-empty-vec invariant (`snapshots[0]` indexing) was checked and is guaranteed by `rate_limit_snapshots_from_payload` always pushing at least one entry. All 32 crate tests pass.
- `codex-rs/attachment-store` and `codex-rs/async-utils`: small, fully covered by their own tests; `AttachmentRef`'s `Debug` impl correctly redacts the credential-bearing `url` field while retaining the non-sensitive `file_id`, per its own test.

- `codex-rs/backend-client/src/client/turn_usage.rs`, `thread_usage_tests.rs`, `client_request_tests.rs`, `lib.rs`, `types.rs` — reviewed the API-key/turn-cost header-merge logic (provider headers overridden by client auth), the thread-usage thread-id validation (`get_thread_usage` rejects mismatched thread ids), the hand-rolled `CodeTaskDetailsResponse` extraction helpers, and the raw-socket integration test for query/auth/JSON-body propagation. Ran `cargo test -p codex-backend-client`: all 32 unit/integration tests pass, including the header-precedence and thread-usage-mismatch cases that exercise the logic described above.
- `codex-rs/build-info/*` — `BuildInfo::resolve`/`build_id`/`from_version` version and commit-provenance logic, including the `build_id` SHA-256 stamping (hex-digest validity checks, case-insensitivity, target-triple requirement) and the legacy/invalid-manifest fallback paths. `cargo test -p codex-build-info`: all 8 tests pass.
- `codex-rs/bwrap/build.rs` and `src/main.rs` — build-time vendored bubblewrap compilation (source-dir resolution, libcap probing via pkg-config, `-idirafter` include ordering for musl cross builds) and the `main` FFI wrapper (argv-to-CString conversion, null-terminated argv construction, exit-code propagation). No defects found; the non-Linux/`bwrap_available`-absent fallbacks correctly panic with actionable messages rather than silently no-op.
- `codex-rs/chatgpt/src/chatgpt_client.rs`, `connectors.rs`, `apply_command.rs`, `lib.rs`, and the `apply_command_e2e` integration tests — reviewed the cached-HTTP-client reuse (`psp_chatgpt_client`, keyed by factory+residency header, with poisoned-mutex recovery), the connector metadata/tool-summary merge and cache-commit-filters-to-requested-ids logic in `read_connector_metadata`, and the git-apply plumbing in `apply_diff_from_task`/`apply_diff`. `cargo test -p codex-chatgpt --lib` and `--test all` (git-repo based apply/merge-conflict e2e tests): all pass.
- `codex-rs/cli/src/debug_sandbox.rs`, `debug_sandbox/cloud_config.rs` (+ tests), `debug_sandbox/pid_tracker.rs`, `debug_sandbox/seatbelt.rs` — reviewed the permission-profile resolution for sandbox-state hand-off (including the `PermissionProfile::External` → `read_only()` downgrade for producer/consumer sandbox mismatches, confirmed the `External` file-system-policy kind round-trips correctly through `with_additional_readable_roots`/`from_runtime_permissions` by reading `protocol/src/models.rs` and `protocol/src/permissions.rs`), the seatbelt `TIOCSTI` ioctl deny-policy injection, the macOS `kqueue`-based descendant PID tracker (fd lifecycle on every early-return path), and the sandbox-denial log-stream parser/matcher. `cargo test -p codex-cli --lib debug_sandbox::` (14 tests, including the macOS PID-tracker fork/subshell-descendant tests and the cloud-managed-permission-profile bootstrap test) and `cargo test -p codex-cli --bin logs_client` (5 tests): all pass.
- `codex-rs/cli/src/desktop_app/mac.rs` — reviewed the Desktop-app discovery/install/launch flow, including that a caller-supplied `--download-url` override cannot be used to install an unsigned/non-OpenAI app: `install_codex_app_bundle`/`open_codex_app` always run `verify_codex_app_bundle`, which enforces a `codesign -R="identifier ... and certificate leaf[subject.OU] = <OpenAI team id>"` designated-requirement check before installing or launching, regardless of where the DMG came from.
- `codex-rs/cli/src/app_cmd.rs`, `cli/src/desktop_app/mod.rs`, `cli/build.rs`, `cli/e2e_benches/codex_help.rs`, `cli/src/cloud_config.rs`, `cli/src/bin/logs_client.rs` — confirmed `app_cmd`/`desktop_app` are gated by `#[cfg(any(target_os = "macos", target_os = "windows"))]` at both the module and call-site level in `main.rs`, so the platform-specific `run_app` bodies never need a non-matching-arm fallback. `logs_client`'s timestamp parsing, log-level filtering, and backfill/tail cursoring logic were traced end-to-end and are consistent with their tests.

- `codex-rs/cli/src/desktop_app/windows.rs`: `open_url`/`codex_app_is_installed` pass the target URL as a separate `powershell.exe` process argument bound to a `param($target)` script rather than interpolating it into the `-Command` string, so a crafted `--download-url-override` value cannot break out into arbitrary PowerShell execution. `display_workspace_path` / `codex_new_thread_url` prefix-stripping and URL encoding match their unit tests.
