This shard covers the code-mode wire protocol (`codex-rs/code-mode-protocol`), its
gRPC/stdio integration tests (`codex-rs/code-mode-host/tests`), and the callback
plumbing in `codex-rs/code-mode-runtime/src/cell_actor`. I read all 30 assigned
files and additionally ran the crate's own checks rather than relying on reading
alone:

- `cargo test -p codex-code-mode-protocol --lib` — all 37 unit tests pass,
  including the wire round-trip "pinning" tests in `host/host_tests.rs`
  (`handshake_v1_variants_are_pinned`, `client_to_host_v1_variants_are_pinned`,
  `host_to_client_v1_variants_are_pinned`, `every_nested_v1_object_rejects_unknown_fields`)
  and the frame-codec tests in `host/codec_tests.rs` (truncated/trailing/oversized/
  malformed frames, fragmented reads, EOF-only-at-boundary). `EncodedFrame`/
  `FramedReader`/`FramedWriter` in `host/codec.rs` correctly bound frame size to
  `MAX_FRAME_BYTES` on both encode and decode paths and reject partial trailing
  bytes.
- `cargo clippy -p codex-code-mode-protocol --all-targets` — clean, no warnings.
- The `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` + explicit `rename`/`rename_all_fields`
  annotations across `host/message.rs`, `host/payload.rs`, and `host/types.rs`
  are internally consistent with the pinned JSON fixtures in the tests (e.g. the
  camelCase envelope fields vs. the snake_case `WireExecuteRequest`/
  `WireToolDefinition` payload fields), and the `TryFrom` conversions between
  domain (`usize`/`i64`) and wire (`u64`/`i32`) integer types correctly reject
  out-of-range values (`execute_request_integer_bounds_are_enforced`,
  `session_cell_execution_limits_reject_heap_sizes_that_exceed_usize`).
- `json_schema_types.rs`'s defenses against a malicious/adversarial JSON Schema
  (used to render nested-tool TypeScript declarations from MCP tool schemas) —
  `$ref` cycle bounding (`MAX_LOCAL_REF_EXPANSIONS_PER_PATH`,
  `MAX_TOTAL_LOCAL_REF_EXPANSIONS`), the incremental byte-work budget
  (`MAX_RENDER_WORK_BYTES`) charged before each string is grown, and the final
  hard size cap (`MAX_RENDERED_SCHEMA_BYTES`) — hold up against the existing
  adversarial-schema tests. I additionally checked the one gap those budgets
  don't close: plain (non-`$ref`) nesting via `items`/`properties` recurses
  without an explicit depth counter, and a `serde_json::Value` built
  programmatically 200,000 levels deep does overflow the renderer's call stack
  (confirmed with a temporary local repro, reverted afterward). However this is
  not reachable through the crate's actual deserialization entry points: I
  confirmed `serde_json`'s default parser already refuses to deserialize JSON
  nested past its built-in recursion limit (a 5,000-level-deep document fails
  to parse with "recursion limit exceeded" at ~128 levels), and no crate in the
  workspace enables the `unbounded_depth` feature that would lift that limit.
  Since `input_schema`/`output_schema` only ever reach this renderer after
  passing through `serde_json` deserialization on the wire, the practical depth
  is capped far below any stack-overflow threshold. Worth keeping in mind if a
  future caller ever constructs a `JsonValue` schema without going through
  `serde_json`'s parser, but not exploitable today.
- `code-mode-runtime/src/cell_actor/callbacks.rs` — tool/notification delegate
  panics are caught via `AssertUnwindSafe(...).catch_unwind()` and converted
  into a `RuntimeCommand::ToolError`/reported failure rather than crashing the
  callback task or poisoning the runtime, matching
  `tool_callback_panic_rejects_the_js_promise_and_reports_failure` and
  `notification_callback_panic_reports_failure`. `finish_callbacks` correctly
  drains notification tasks first (without forcing cancellation on normal
  completion) before force-cancelling and draining tool tasks, matching the
  "drain pending notifications before completion" vs. "termination cancels
  pending notifications" behavior exercised in
  `code-mode-host/tests/grpc_notifications.rs`.
- The extensive `code-mode-host/tests/*` integration suite (gRPC over TCP/Unix
  socket, stdio/process-owned host, timing isolation, cancellation-before-
  admission, dropped-cell/dropped-session cleanup, host-restart recovery,
  oversized-frame handling) reads as correct and internally consistent; I did
  not find a test asserting behavior the implementation (outside this shard)
  would not actually provide, and the credential-redaction test
  (`grpc_endpoints_reject_credentials_without_disclosing_them`) asserts both
  that the rejection message names the reason and that it never echoes the
  rejected username/password back to the caller.

No other defects were found in this shard at medium-depth review across
correctness, security, error handling, and API-contract lenses.

- `codex-rs/code-mode-runtime/src/cell_actor/mod.rs` and `cell_actor/types.rs`: traced the `CellState` phase machine (`Running` / `Terminating` / `Completed` / `CompletionClaimed` / `Tombstone`) against the extensive scenarios in `cell_actor/tests.rs` (dropped observers pre/post dequeue, races between natural completion and explicit termination, buffered initial-yield ordering ahead of buffered completion for both `YieldAfter` and `PendingFrontier` observers). The state transitions are consistent and every non-trivial `panic!` in the module is guarded by an invariant that the accompanying tests exercise.
- `codex-rs/code-mode-runtime/src/runtime/audio.rs` (`wav_duration_seconds`): re-derived the RIFF chunk-walking loop by hand. All slicing uses `.get()`/`checked_add`/`?` rather than direct indexing, the declared chunk `size` is clamped to the remaining buffer before slicing, and `chunks` strictly shrinks (or the function returns `None`) on every iteration, so oversized or truncated/malformed WAV payloads cannot panic or loop forever. The pre-decode `payload.len()` bound also prevents `BASE64_STANDARD.decode` from being handed an unbounded string.
- `codex-rs/code-mode-runtime/src/runtime/value.rs`: image/audio output helpers correctly restrict output URLs to the `data:` scheme (rejecting `http(s):` explicitly and anything else implicitly) in both `normalize_output_image` and `normalize_output_audio`; this matches the behavior exercised by `image_helpers_reject_remote_urls` and `audio_helper_rejects_non_data_urls` in `service_tests.rs`.
- `codex-rs/code-mode-runtime/src/service_tests.rs::global_scope_contains_only_allowed_items` cross-checked against `runtime/globals.rs`'s `install_globals`: the deleted (`console`, `Atomics`, `SharedArrayBuffer`, `WebAssembly`) and added globals match the allowlist asserted by the test.
- `codex-rs/code-mode/src/grpc_session/deadline.rs` and `completion.rs`: the transport-timeout composition (`runtime_timeout.saturating_add(TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT)`) and the gRPC message-size fallback in `request_with_maximum` (falling back to a bounded `Failed` outcome when `encoded_len()` exceeds the limit) were checked against their respective test suites and behave as documented, including the exact-limit boundary case.
- `codex-rs/code-mode/src/grpc_session/generation.rs`: the `public_cell_id`/`remote_cell_id` prefixing scheme correctly special-cases generation 1 (no prefixing, so pre-existing opaque IDs that happen to look like `g2:42` are passed through unchanged) and correctly rejects stale-generation IDs on reconnect; this matches the test names and assertions in `generation_tests.rs`.

- `codex-rs/codex-api/src/auth.rs`: `AuthProvider::apply_auth`'s default implementation does `request.headers.extend(self.resolve_auth_headers().await?)`. Initially this looked like it could append a duplicate `Authorization` header when the base request already carried one (e.g. from `Provider.headers` or caller-supplied `extra_headers`, both merged the same way in `endpoint/session.rs::make_request`). I verified against the `http` crate's `HeaderMap::extend` source (`http-1.5.0/src/header/map.rs`): because the argument is an *owned* `HeaderMap` (whose `IntoIterator::Item = (Option<HeaderName>, T)`), the `Extend<(Option<HeaderName>, T)>` impl is selected, which replaces the destination's existing entry for a key via `OccupiedEntry::insert` rather than appending to it (the append-only `Extend<(HeaderName, T)>` impl is only selected when the source iterator yields bare `(HeaderName, T)` tuples, e.g. a `Vec`). So `extend()` here correctly overwrites a pre-existing `Authorization`/other header rather than duplicating it. No bug.
- `codex-rs/code-mode/src/grpc_session/` session/execution/wait lifecycle (`mod.rs`, `operations.rs`, `reconnect.rs`, `state.rs`): traced the `ExecutionOwnership`/`WaitCancellation`/`OpeningSession` drop-guard patterns and the `ReconnectableSession` generation handoff for races between concurrent `execute`/`wait`/`shutdown` calls and connection failure. The `wait_slots` active-flag swap happens while still holding the slot-table mutex, so there is no window for two concurrent `wait()` calls on the same cell to both win; `close_state`/`fail` correctly no-op once already closed so the various cleanup paths (`ExecutionOwnership::drop`, explicit `self.fail(...)`) cannot double-remove or double-terminate a cell.
- `codex-rs/code-mode/src/remote_session/connection/driver/` (`commands.rs`, `responses.rs`, `request_tracker.rs`, `session_registry.rs`, `types.rs`, `cell_ids.rs`, `delegate_runtime.rs`, `cleanup.rs`) and its test suite `driver_tests.rs`: reviewed the abandoned-execute/terminate-on-cancel paths, the deferred-delegate-request queue (bounded by `MAX_PENDING_DELEGATE_CALLS`), and the generation-based cell ID namespacing. Cancellation, admission, and failure propagation are internally consistent with the accompanying tests.
- `codex-rs/codex-api/src/api_bridge.rs` + `api_bridge_tests.rs`: cross-checked the HTTP status/body dispatch order (503 overload, 400/403 misalignment, 400 cyber-policy vs. generic invalid-request, 429 usage-limit/quota/rate-limit disambiguation, identity-error header extraction) against the test cases; the branching is consistent and each branch is exercised by a corresponding test.
- `codex-rs/codex-api/src/endpoint/realtime_call.rs`: verified `decode_call_id_from_location`/`is_realtime_call_id_segment` correctly extract the rightmost `rtc_*` or UUID path segment from a server-supplied `Location` header, matching both the plain and backend-forwarded location shapes exercised in tests.

- Header construction throughout this shard (`build_session_headers`,
  `subagent_header` + `insert_header` in `requests/headers.rs`,
  `with_session_id_header` and both `merge_request_headers` copies in
  `endpoint/realtime_websocket/methods.rs` and `endpoint/responses_websocket.rs`)
  relies on `http::HeaderValue::from_str`, which I confirmed experimentally
  rejects CR/LF-bearing values (`Err(InvalidHeaderValue)`), so
  attacker/caller-controlled strings (thread ids, subagent labels, session ids)
  cannot be used for HTTP header/response-splitting injection; the failure mode
  is "header silently omitted," not a crash or injection.
- `merge_request_headers` in both `methods.rs` and `responses_websocket.rs`
  gives `extra_headers` precedence over `provider_headers` on key collision. I
  verified with a standalone `http = "1.3.1"` reproduction that
  `HeaderMap::extend(other_header_map)` replaces same-named entries (last write
  wins, `len`/`keys_len` stay singular) rather than accumulating duplicate
  multi-value entries, matching the intent of the existing
  `merge_request_headers_matches_http_precedence` tests.
- `rate_limits.rs` builds header *names* by string-formatting a caller-supplied
  `limit_id` (`parse_rate_limit_for_limit`). I verified experimentally that
  `HeaderMap::get(&str)` returns `None` rather than panicking when the
  constructed string contains characters that are not valid header-name bytes
  (spaces, `!`, non-ASCII), so a malformed/unexpected `limit_id` cannot crash
  rate-limit header parsing.
- `websocket_url_from_api_url_for_call` (`methods.rs`) rejects `call_id` values
  of exactly `.` or `..`, and for all other values relies on
  `Url::path_segments_mut().push(call_id)`, which percent-encodes the segment
  (confirmed by `frameless_websocket_url_encodes_call_id_as_one_path_segment`,
  where `../../admin` becomes the single literal segment `..%2F..%2Fadmin`), so
  a hostile `call_id` cannot escape the `/v1/live/<call_id>` sideband path.
- `truncate_active_transcript` / `append_transcript_delta` /
  `apply_transcript_done` (`methods.rs`) manage a byte-bounded transcript
  buffer with saturating arithmetic and an explicit `is_char_boundary` walk
  before slicing; I traced the underflow-prone paths (empty text budget, a
  single oversized entry, multi-entry eviction) and confirmed none can index
  out of bounds or split a multi-byte UTF-8 character, consistent with the
  `active_transcript_retains_a_bounded_suffix` test.
- `upload_openai_file` (`files.rs`) intentionally excludes the SAS-signed
  `upload_url` from its `BlobUploadRequest`/`BlobUploadStatus` error variants
  (only the parsed host is retained), matching the
  `upload_openai_file_reports_blob_response_diagnostics_without_sas` and
  `..._transport_diagnostics_without_sas` tests, so blob-storage failures do
  not leak the pre-signed URL/query string into logs or error messages
  returned to callers.
- Grepped the whole shard for `.unwrap()`, `.expect(`, `panic!`, and
  `unreachable!()`; every occurrence outside `#[cfg(test)]` modules is an
  `unreachable!()` guarded by a `match` arm that the enclosing function already
  dispatches away from (e.g. `RealtimeWireAdapter::RealtimeV2` in
  `conversation_handoff_append_message`/`standalone_handoff_message`, which are
  never called for that adapter). No panics are reachable from untrusted input
  in this shard's production code paths.

- `codex-rs/codex-api/src/sse/responses.rs` — the Responses-API SSE event parser and classifier (`process_responses_event`, `process_sse_with_treatment`, `spawn_response_stream`, `try_parse_retry_after`, and the `safety_buffering`/`model_verifications`/`response_model` accessors on `ResponsesStreamEvent`). Traced the error-classification branch order in the `response.failed` handler (context window → quota → usage-not-included → cyber policy → misalignment → invalid-prompt/bio-policy → server-overloaded → rate-limit/generic retryable) against the extensive existing test suite in the same file and confirmed the logic and its tests agree, including the fallback/blank-message cases for cyber-policy and misalignment errors. Verified the `safety_buffering()` precedence logic (top-level field wins over `response.metadata`, `Value::Null`/non-object values correctly fall through to `None` rather than panicking) by hand-tracing `as_object()?` short-circuiting. Confirmed the regex in `rate_limit_regex()` is a hardcoded, compile-time-valid pattern (the only non-test `unwrap()` in the file) and that its `(s|ms|seconds?)` alternation, despite matching only a single `s` for the word "seconds" in leftmost-first NFA semantics, still produces the correct `Duration` because `try_parse_retry_after` treats a bare `"s"` and any `"second…"` prefix identically.
- `codex-rs/codex-api/src/telemetry.rs` — `run_with_request_telemetry` is a thin, side-effect-free wrapper around `run_with_retry` that forwards per-attempt status/error to the telemetry sink; no defects found.
- `codex-rs/codex-client/src/retry.rs` — verified `run_with_retry`'s `for attempt in 0..=policy.max_attempts` loop against the `max_attempts` semantics documented on `ModelProviderInfo::request_max_retries` ("maximum number of times to *retry* a failed request"), i.e. `max_attempts` is a retry count, not a total-attempt cap, so the loop performing up to `max_attempts + 1` total calls is correct, not an off-by-one. `backoff()`'s `attempt as u32 - 1` subtraction is guarded by the preceding `attempt == 0` early return, so it cannot underflow.
- `codex-rs/codex-client/src/sse.rs` and `codex-rs/codex-client/src/lib.rs` — straightforward, no defects found.
- `codex-rs/codex-backend-openapi-models/**` (all 20 files on this shard, including `lib.rs` and `models/mod.rs`) — openapi-generator boilerplate; field/rename mappings, `Option<Option<T>>` double-option encodings, and the two `#[derive(Default)]` enums (`PlanType`, `RateLimitReachedKind`) each carry exactly one `#[default]` variant. No hand-written logic, no defects found.
- `codex-rs/codex-api/tests/{clients,models_integration,realtime_websocket_e2e,sse_end_to_end}.rs` — integration tests exercising retry-on-transport-error (including a pointer-equality assertion that the serialized request body is reused rather than rebuilt across retries), auth-header injection, Azure `store` header behavior, and realtime websocket session/audio/transcript flows against real local mock transports/servers. Assertions match the implementation they exercise; no false-positive-prone or unrelated-failure-masking assertions found.

No `CR-###`-worthy defects were identified in this shard at medium-depth review. This shard is dominated by generated model boilerplate and test code; the one substantial hand-written file (`sse/responses.rs`) is unusually well covered by its own test suite, and hand-tracing the less obvious branches (safety-buffering precedence, retry-after parsing, error classification) did not turn up a case the tests miss.

- `codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/agent_plugin_config.rs`: the plugin-supplied
  `command`/`cwd`/`headers` normalization for Agent Plugins MCP configs
  (`normalize_agent_plugin_stdio_server`, `resolve_contained_host_path`,
  `resolve_existing_path_prefix`) rejects non-bare, non-`./`-relative
  commands, expands `${PLUGIN_ROOT}`/`${PLUGIN_DATA}` only after the
  syntactic shape is validated, and then re-validates containment by
  `std::fs::canonicalize`-ing the resolved path and checking
  `starts_with(allowed_root)`. I traced through the attacker model where the
  plugin package itself ships a symlink (e.g. `plugin_root/link -> /etc`) and
  references it via `command = "./link/passwd"`: `canonicalize` follows the
  symlink fully before the containment check runs, so the escape is caught
  rather than silently accepted. The HTTP transport path
  (`validate_agent_plugin_url`) also rejects credentials/fragments in the URL
  and requires HTTPS for any non-`localhost`/non-loopback host.
- `codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/catalog.rs` and `catalog_tests.rs`: the
  precedence/tie-break logic in `McpCatalogBuilder::build` (stable sort by
  `RegistrationPrecedence`, disabled-name veto persistence, conflict
  reporting) and the environment-authority gating in
  `build_with_environment_authority` (including the "empty server policy
  denies every plugin" and "metadata-only plugin policy" edge cases) match
  their extensive test coverage; I did not find a case where the resolved
  winner diverges from what the tests assert.
- `codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/elicitation.rs`: the strict-auto-review gate
  requires an exact `Value::Bool(true)`/`Value::Bool(false)`/absent marker
  (any other JSON value fails closed to `strict_auto_review_decline()`), and
  only accepts a reviewer's response as an approval when its `meta` carries
  `approvals_reviewer == "auto_review"` and the action/content combination is
  one of the two allow-listed shapes; every other reviewer response — including
  a `None`, an `Err`, or a well-formed but wrongly-tagged response — also
  fails closed. This matches the fail-closed behavior asserted in
  `elicitation_tests.rs::strict_auto_review_fails_closed_without_a_canonical_decision`.
- `codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/client_capabilities.rs`: `server_mcp_extensions`
  only forwards the `userVerification` elicitation extension to a server
  whose *resolved* source is host-owned Apps (`Compatibility` or
  `Extension { host_owned_apps: true }` on the `codex_apps` name plus a
  local environment); a user-configured server registered under the same
  `codex_apps` name via `McpServerSource::Config` does not qualify, matching
  `client_capabilities_tests.rs::user_verification_is_projected_only_to_the_host_owned_plugin_service`.
- `codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/connection_manager.rs`: `call_tool` strips
  `ENTITLEMENT_CONTEXT_KEY` from caller-supplied `meta` before dispatching a
  direct (non-`PreparedMcpCall`) tool call, preventing a direct caller from
  spoofing host-owned trusted-access entitlement metadata.

- `codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/pagination.rs` and `pagination_tests.rs`: page count, per-page item count, cumulative item count, cursor byte-size, cursor-repeat, and overall wall-clock timeout are all independently bounded before following an MCP server's pagination cursor, with tests exercising each bound including the "reject before fetching another page" and "reject before following an oversized cursor" ordering.
- `codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/trusted_access.rs` and `trusted_access_tests.rs`: `TrustedAccessContext::fetch_status` re-checks account id, ChatGPT/workspace/FedRAMP identity, and auth mode both before and after the network round-trip (including while the request is in flight, per `rejects_identity_changes_while_request_is_in_flight`), enforces a response size cap and a fixed timeout, and rejects ambiguous/duplicate `cyber` program entries — a good defense against attaching stale or cross-account entitlement metadata.
- `codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/plugin_config.rs` (`environment_cwd`) and `plugin_config_tests.rs`: relative `cwd` values for executor-owned plugin MCP servers are resolved against the plugin root and explicitly rejected if they escape it (`cwd.starts_with(root)`), with tests covering `../` traversal, symlink escapes, and root-relative edge cases.
- `codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/resource_origin.rs`: bounded (`MAX_ORIGINS`/`MAX_ORIGIN_BYTES`) provenance tracking for app-hosted widget resource reads, with `ResourceOrigin::read` re-validating URI, account-link ambiguity, connector identity, and tool policy at read time rather than trusting the cached origin outright.

- `FilesystemDenyReadPattern::from_input` / `split_glob_pattern` in
  `codex-rs/config/src/config_requirements.rs`: when a glob deny-read pattern
  has a directory prefix, the normalized string is built with
  `format!("{normalized_prefix}/{suffix}")`, which on Windows would mix the
  backslash-separated `AbsolutePathBuf` prefix with a forward-slash suffix
  (e.g. `C:\Users\foo/*.log`). I traced this all the way to the actual glob
  matcher (`build_glob_matcher` in `codex-rs/protocol/src/permissions.rs`),
  which replaces `\` with `/` in the pattern before compiling
  (`pattern.replace('\\', "/")`) and normalizes candidate paths the same way
  before matching (`inferred_native_path_string().replace('\\', "/")`), so the
  mixed separators are normalized away before matching and do not weaken the
  deny-read policy. The `config` crate's own round-trip test for this path
  (`deserialize_filesystem_deny_read_glob_requirements`) is tautological (it
  computes its expected value via the same `from_input` call), so it would not
  have caught a real regression here, but the downstream consumer makes this a
  non-issue today.
- `ConfigRequirementsToml::is_empty()`, `ConfigRequirementsWithSources::merge_unset_fields`
  (`fill_missing_take!` field list), and `ConfigRequirementsWithSources::into_toml()`
  in `codex-rs/config/src/config_requirements.rs`: manually cross-checked every
  one of the 40 fields on `ConfigRequirementsToml` against all three functions.
  All three are exhaustive and in sync with the current struct definition (the
  destructuring patterns used everywhere force a compile error if a field is
  ever added without updating these call sites), so there is no silently-dropped
  managed setting today.
- `codex-rs/config/src/loader/macos.rs` (`CFPreferencesCopyAppValue` /
  `CFString::wrap_under_create_rule`) and the Windows `SHGetKnownFolderPath`
  FFI in `codex-rs/config/src/loader/mod.rs`: retain/release and
  `CoTaskMemFree` calls are correctly paired with the documented ownership
  semantics of each API (`wrap_under_create_rule` matches the "Copy" naming
  convention of `CFPreferencesCopyAppValue`), and null/error paths are handled
  before any use of the returned pointer.
- `sanitize_project_config`, `PROJECT_LOCAL_CONFIG_DENYLIST`, and the
  credential-broker-aware `shell_environment_policy.set` stripping in
  `codex-rs/config/src/loader/mod.rs`: reviewed the denylist and the
  `ZDOTDIR`/`BASH_ENV`/credential-broker-provider-env-key stripping logic used
  to keep an untrusted repository's `.codex/config.toml` from redirecting
  request destinations or hijacking shell startup files/credential-broker
  provider env bindings; the logic is internally consistent with its stated
  intent and is covered by `codex-rs/config/src/loader/managed_project_discovery_tests.rs`
  (including the `managed_project_discovery_preserves_remapped_provider_bindings`
  case, which specifically exercises an attempted env-var hijack from
  project-local config).
- `allowed_symlinked_codex_home` in `codex-rs/config/src/codex_home_symlink.rs`:
  deliberately reads `allow_symlinked_codex_home` only from the base
  `ConfigLayerSource::User { profile: None, .. }` layer (not from profiles,
  system, managed, or project layers), matching the field's doc comment in
  `config_toml.rs` ("Read only from the host's user config at startup").

- `codex-rs/config/src/merge.rs` and `merge_tests.rs`: the credential-provider remapping logic in `merge_toml_values_at_path` (removing stale `[features.network_proxy.credentials.*]` providers whose `env` overlaps a higher-priority provider, with Windows-only case-insensitive comparison) is exercised by dedicated tests (`higher_priority_credential_provider_replaces_overlapping_sources`, `credential_provider_remapping_preserves_inherited_settings`) and behaves as documented.
- `codex-rs/config/src/requirements_layers/layer.rs`: `LOCAL_ONLY_AUTH_REQUIREMENTS` is stripped only from `RequirementSource::EnterpriseManaged` (backend/cloud-delivered) layers before validation, while `SystemRequirementsToml`/`MdmManagedPreferences`/legacy managed sources (which require local machine or MDM-enrollment control) are trusted to set them. This asymmetry matches the module's stated intent ("Authentication requirements that cloud-managed layers cannot set") and is covered by `cloud_auth_requirements_do_not_override_local_or_discard_other_policy` in `stack_tests.rs`.
- `codex-rs/config/src/requirements_layers/hooks.rs` and `stack_tests.rs`: active-platform `hooks.managed_dir`/`hooks.windows_managed_dir` conflicts fail closed (`hooks_append_groups_and_reject_conflicting_managed_dirs`, `active_windows_managed_dir_conflicts_fail_closed`), while inactive-platform conflicts are silently resolved in favor of the highest-priority layer — verified against `inactive_hook_dir_conflicts_do_not_fail_composition`, which matches the code path exactly.
- `codex-rs/config/src/mcp_types.rs`: `RawMcpServerConfig` exhaustively destructures and rejects `bearer_token` for both stdio and streamable_http transports at the primary deserialization path, independent of the additional friendlier check in `mcp_edit.rs::ensure_no_inline_bearer_tokens`.
- `codex-rs/config/src/mcp_requirements.rs`: `McpServerConfig::matches_requirement`'s command-matcher requires exact argument-count equality plus per-position matching, correctly rejecting both truncated and padded argument lists (confirmed against `command_matcher_matches_exact_positional_arguments`).
- `codex-rs/config/src/shell_environment_policy.rs`: rejects mixing legacy `exclude`/`include_only` with the canonical `filters` map, and rejects case-variant duplicate filter keys within one layer, both enforced at `Deserialize` time before any merge can normalize the conflict away.

- `codex-rs/connectors/src/app_tool_policy.rs` and its test file
  (`app_tool_policy_tests.rs`): the enterprise-managed vs. local-config
  precedence rules were traced carefully. Managed `enabled = false` always
  wins over local config (`apply_requirements_apps_constraints` seeds a
  disabled entry into the effective `apps_config` even when no user config
  exists), while managed `enabled = true` never overrides a locally disabled
  app (`app_is_enabled` only reads local config; there is no "managed enable"
  path) — confirmed by `managed_enable_does_not_override_disabled_app`.
  Managed approval-mode overrides
  (`managed_app_tool_approval`) key strictly off the raw `tool_name`, never
  the MCP-server-supplied `tool_title`, so a connector cannot spoof another
  tool's name via its `title` field to inherit a different managed approval
  decision (confirmed by `managed_approval_uses_raw_tool_name`). The
  `tool_title` fallback is used only for resolving the user's own local
  per-tool overrides, which is a same-trust-boundary within one connector and
  is intentionally tested (`evaluator_matches_tool_title_for_user_config`).
- `codex-rs/connectors/src/connector_runtime/mod.rs` and
  `connector_runtime/persistence.rs`: the "publish if newest accepted"
  generation-guard logic (`publish_runtime_if_newest_accepted_with`) was
  traced against the concurrency tests
  (`accepted_generations_finish_persistence_in_order`,
  `codex_apps_tools_cache_publishes_newest_shared_snapshot`,
  `live_catalogs_isolate_scopes_and_reject_older_refreshes`) and correctly
  rejects stale (lower-generation) publishes while holding the acceptance
  mutex through persistence so accepted generations cannot reach disk out of
  order. `read_bounded_cache_file` double-checks the byte count actually read
  (not just the `stat()`-reported size) before trusting the cache file,
  defending against TOCTOU size growth between stat and read.
- `codex-rs/config/src/tui_keymap.rs` and
  `codex-rs/config/src/tui_keymap_chord_tests.rs`: `normalize_keybinding_spec`
  / `normalize_keybinding_stroke` were traced by hand for edge cases (empty
  string, whitespace-only string, modifiers appearing after the key such as
  `"a-ctrl"`, duplicate modifiers, chord length overflow) and each is
  rejected with a clear error, matching the accompanying tests.
- `codex-rs/config/src/strict_config.rs`: the ignored-field/unknown-feature
  detection path (`config_error_from_ignored_toml_value_fields_for_source`)
  correctly prioritizes hard type errors over "unknown field" diagnostics,
  and the "known feature key" allowlist check
  (`unknown_feature_toml_value_path`) is applied for both `[features]` and
  every `[profiles.<name>.features]` table.
- `codex-rs/config/src/thread_config.rs` and
  `codex-rs/config/src/thread_config/remote.rs`: the proto round-trip
  conversions (`model_provider_from_proto`/`model_provider_to_proto`,
  `model_provider_auth_from_proto`) validate required invariants (non-empty
  provider id, non-zero auth timeout, absolute auth cwd) before constructing
  domain types, and gRPC status codes are mapped to a bounded
  `ThreadConfigLoadErrorCode` enum with an explicit (non-wildcard) match that
  will fail to compile if `tonic::Code` grows a new variant that isn't
  triaged.

- `codex-rs/context-fragments/src/fragment.rs` (`ContextualUserFragment::render`/`matches_marked_text`) — marker concatenation and case-insensitive prefix/suffix matching use `str::get` (never panics on non-boundary slicing) and correctly special-case empty markers to "never match," matching the documented contract.
- `codex-rs/context-fragments/src/annotated_content.rs` (`to_annotated_content`/`set_annotated_content`) — correctly pads missing classifications with `"unknown"` for legacy/rollout messages without panicking on length mismatches, and round-trips content/kind pairs symmetrically.
- `codex-rs/core-plugins/src/git_policy.rs` — the automatic/background Git path strips all repository-scoped `GIT_*` environment variables and canonicalizes a scratch `GIT_DIR` that is verified (post-canonicalization) to stay under `codex_home` before use, which is a sound isolation boundary for untrusted/automatic Git invocations.
- `codex-rs/core-plugins/src/agent_plugin_mcp_overlay.rs` (`apply_codex_env_overlay`) — strips remote-sourced env vars from the legacy `.codex-plugin` MCP overlay before merging them into an Agent-Plugin-declared server's environment, preventing a legacy overlay from smuggling remotely-sourced env values into a portable manifest's server.
- `codex-rs/core-plugins/src/executor_hooks.rs` and `executor_hooks_tests.rs` — the temporary allowlist filter (`is_allowlisted_bundled_cleanup_hook`) is applied per-handler after parsing untrusted executor-discovered manifests, and the test suite exercises the marketplace-suffix confusion cases (`openai-bundled-alpha`, `fake-openai-bundled`) as well as MCP-tool routing metadata resolution/rejection; behavior matches the documented "not yet trusted, temporary allowlist" contract.
- `codex-rs/core-plugins/src/artifact_operation.rs` — `recognize_artifact_operation` only matches a fixed marketplace (`openai-primary-runtime`) and a fixed table of plugin/script paths, and validates operation kind, output count range, and output format against the per-skill allowlist before returning a match.

- `codex-rs/core-plugins/src/plugin_bundle_archive.rs`: tar/gzip pack and unpack logic. Path
  traversal is blocked (`checked_tar_output_path` rejects `ParentDir`/`RootDir`/`Prefix` components
  and empty paths), symlink/hardlink entries are rejected outright, and both the packed archive size
  and total extracted byte count are bounded with overflow-checked arithmetic
  (`enforce_total_extracted_size`, `SizeLimitedBuffer`). Verified via
  `plugin_bundle_archive_tests.rs`.
- `codex-rs/core-plugins/src/npm_source.rs`: `npm pack --ignore-scripts` with the package spec
  passed after a literal `--` argument (preventing flag injection through a crafted package/version
  string), archive size capped before reading into memory
  (`NPM_PLUGIN_SOURCE_MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES`), extraction size capped
  (`NPM_PLUGIN_SOURCE_MAX_EXTRACTED_BYTES`), and the unpacked `package.json` name is verified to
  match the requested package before the plugin root is trusted
  (`validate_npm_package_metadata`). Registry URLs are constrained to `https` with no
  embedded credentials, query, or fragment (`normalize_optional_npm_registry`), and package/version
  selectors are restricted to registry-safe characters (`normalize_npm_package`,
  `is_registry_npm_version_selector`), which also blocks local-path or URL version selectors.
- `codex-rs/core-plugins/src/marketplace_policy.rs` and its test suite
  (`marketplace_policy_tests.rs`, `marketplace_policy/curated_tests.rs`,
  `marketplace_policy/curated_loading_tests.rs`, `marketplace_policy/curated_skill_tests.rs`):
  allowed-source matching fails closed on any malformed rule (`invalid_active_rule_fails_closed_...`,
  `invalid_allowed_source_shapes_fail_closed`), managed/reserved marketplace names cannot be
  claimed by an allow-listed local or git source, and symlink aliasing of the curated marketplace
  root/manifest is rejected by `is_expected_managed_path`'s exact-path comparison plus platform
  helper (`symlinked_marketplaces_cannot_borrow_managed_provenance`).
- `codex-rs/core-plugins/src/plugin_metrics.rs` / `plugin_metrics_sidecar.rs`: the `analytics.yaml`
  manifest and script paths are validated with a canonicalization + `is_safe_plugin_relative_path`
  check that fails closed, identifiers and dimension values are restricted to a safe character set,
  and measurement output is read from an already-open file handle/stream rather than re-opened by
  path, which the test `sidecar_reads_the_original_file_after_path_replacement` confirms defeats a
  swap of the output file between write and read.
- `codex-rs/core-plugins/src/loader.rs::clone_git_plugin_source` and its test
  `materialize_git_source_rejects_sha_that_resolves_to_hostile_default_branch`: this is the correct
  reference implementation of SHA-pin verification that the two `high` findings above are missing.

- `codex-rs/core-plugins/src/remote_bundle.rs`: bundle download/extraction is well defended — HTTPS-only download URLs (`is_allowed_bundle_download_url`, with the loopback-HTTP allowance gated behind a `cfg(debug_assertions)` test-only env var), a post-redirect final-URL re-check before trusting the response, a hard cap on downloaded bytes enforced incrementally per chunk, and tar-gz extraction that is unit-tested against path traversal (`extraction_rejects_tar_path_traversal`), oversized archives (`extraction_rejects_total_size_over_limit`), and GNU long-name entries. The plugin-name/marketplace/version validation before install (`validate_remote_plugin_bundle`, `validate_plugin_version_segment`) rejects path-traversal-shaped version strings.
- `codex-rs/core-plugins/src/startup_sync.rs` and `startup_sync_tests.rs`: the Git invocation path is unusually well hardened against supply-chain attack via ambient environment — trusted-`PATH`-only git resolution, stripped `GIT_EXEC_PATH`/`GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR`/`DEVELOPER_DIR`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, and `safe.bareRepository=explicit`. This is backed by targeted regression tests for a hostile `PATH` (`pretrust_startup_sync_uses_installed_git_with_hostile_path`), repository-local transport config injection (`pretrust_git_sync_ignores_repository_local_transport_config`), and a tracked embedded bare repository inside the synced content (`ordinary_clone_rejects_tracked_embedded_bare_repository`). The file-lock-based single-flight guard (`lock_curated_plugins_startup_sync`) is verified not to skip remote checks under concurrency (`concurrent_syncs_serialize_fetches_without_skipping_remote_checks`).
- `codex-rs/core-plugins/src/script_attribution.rs`: command-to-plugin-script attribution is conservative by construction (single unambiguous match required, canonicalized paths, symlink-escape rejection, safe-relative-path validation) and is exercised by a thorough adversarial test suite (`rejects_ambiguous_commands_overlaps_and_symlink_escapes`, `trusted_roots_require_verified_curated_or_remote_cache`, Windows executor path recognition).
- `codex-rs/core-plugins/src/store.rs`: `install_with_manifest`/`replace_plugin_root_atomically` re-reads the staged manifest path and byte-for-byte contents after copying and rejects the install if either changed during staging, which specifically defends against the symlink-manifest-switch TOCTOU scenario covered by `install_rejects_symlinked_manifest_that_hides_lower_precedence_mcp_server` and `install_rejects_symlinked_manifest_directory` in `store_tests.rs`.

- `codex-rs/core/src/agent/control/residency.rs` and `codex-rs/core/src/agent/status.rs`: `is_final` deliberately excludes `AgentStatus::Interrupted` from "final" (so `maybe_start_completion_watcher` keeps waiting past an interruption), while `is_unloadable` in `residency.rs` separately treats `Interrupted` threads as eligible for LRU eviction when idle. These are different concerns (completion-notification vs. residency eviction) and are internally consistent with the code's comments and the `residency_tests.rs` coverage (`interrupted_v2_agent_is_lost_after_residency_eviction`).
- `codex-rs/core/src/agent/control/spawn.rs`: the permission-profile intersection logic in `ensure_v2_agent_loaded` (bounding a reloaded V2 child's environment config to the current parent's authority, rejecting remote-executor permission drift, and intersecting effective permission profiles before accepting a `Ready` config) is careful and defensive; no bypass was found.
- `codex-rs/core/src/agents_md.rs` and its extensive test suite (`agents_md_tests.rs`): the project-root-marker discovery, per-environment byte budget accounting (including truncation and lossy UTF-8 handling), and multi-environment label rendering all matched their test expectations on inspection; the concurrency-bounded ancestor-probe stream (`MAX_CONCURRENT_ANCESTOR_PROBES`) is exercised directly by dedicated tests.
- `codex-rs/core/src/client.rs`: the websocket/HTTP fallback state machine, incremental-request reuse guard (`get_incremental_items`, which validates non-input request fields, checked lengths, and item-equality before treating a request as an extension of the previous one), and the `filter_tool_result_metadata`/`uses_codex_backend` gating that restricts sensitive tool-result metadata and Codex-only headers to `api.openai.com`/approved ChatGPT hosts all read as intentional and internally consistent.
- `codex-rs/core/src/apply_patch.rs` and `apply_patch_tests.rs`: the safety-check-to-approval-requirement mapping is a straightforward pass-through with correct handling of the three `SafetyCheck` outcomes.

- `codex-rs/core/src/config/network_proxy_spec.rs` and its extensive test
  suite (`network_proxy_spec_tests.rs`): the allow/deny merge ordering in
  `for_environment` (owner grants, then exec-policy denies, then re-applying
  the pre-existing "protected" denials last) correctly keeps managed denials
  from being overridden by later owner/exec-policy allow entries, and the
  `hard_deny_allowlist_misses`/`fixed_allowlist` computation fails closed
  (conservative) rather than open when a profile is not managed-sandboxed.
- `codex-rs/core/src/config/config_loader_tests.rs`: tests such as
  `forged_linked_worktree_does_not_inherit_repo_trust` and
  `malformed_untrusted_linked_worktree_does_not_read_root_hooks` exercise
  attacker-controlled `.git`/worktree-pointer forging against the project
  trust resolver and confirm the affected project layer is disabled rather
  than silently inheriting trust from a spoofed root repo.
- `codex-rs/core/src/config/edit.rs` symlink handling, exercised by
  `blocking_set_model_writes_through_symlink_chain` and
  `blocking_set_model_replaces_symlink_on_cycle` in `edit_tests.rs`: writes
  follow a single-hop symlink to its target and safely replace a symlink
  cycle rather than following it indefinitely or writing through it.
- `codex-rs/core/src/compact_remote_v2.rs`, `compact_remote_v2_images.rs`,
  and `compact_remote_v2_attempt.rs`: the retained-message token-budget
  truncation (image-atomic boundaries, client-authored-developer-message
  budgeting, text truncation) is intricate but internally consistent, and is
  covered by targeted unit tests for each boundary case (image-only
  messages, mixed text/image/audio content, oversized client-authored
  developer messages).
- `codex-rs/core/src/config/managed_features.rs`: pinned-feature enforcement
  (`normalize_candidate`/`validate_pinned_features_constraint`) correctly
  re-validates after normalization and rejects a candidate whose normalized
  value disagrees with a managed requirement, rather than trusting the
  pre-normalization candidate.

- `codex-rs/core/src/config/requirements.rs` (`apply_to_config`'s `enforce_residency` handling)
  only logs a startup warning when a configured `model_providers.*.http_headers` entry
  collides with the managed residency header name; it does not itself strip or overwrite the
  header. I traced this further into `codex-rs/model-provider/src/provider.rs`
  (`enforce_managed_residency`, called from `api_provider()` for every provider on the request
  path) and confirmed it unconditionally `HeaderMap::insert`s the managed residency value right
  before the provider config is used, which does override any user/config-supplied value for
  that header at request time. So the warning in `requirements.rs` is advisory only and the
  actual enforcement is sound; it is not a fail-open control.
- `codex-rs/core/src/config/permissions.rs` — the glob/scoped-filesystem-path compilation
  (`compile_filesystem_permission`, `compile_read_write_glob_path`,
  `unsupported_read_write_glob_paths`, `unbounded_unreadable_globstar_paths`,
  `validate_glob_scan_max_depth`, Windows device-path normalization) is dense but is backed by
  matching unit tests in `permissions_tests.rs` that I cross-checked against the implementation
  (trailing `/**` compiling to a subtree special/path entry rather than a literal glob, legacy
  `:project_roots`/`:workspace_roots` profiles not failing open, zero `glob_scan_max_depth`
  rejected, non-macOS read/write glob warnings limited to unsupported patterns). Behavior
  matches the tests and the documented intent in each case I checked.
- `codex-rs/core/src/connectors.rs` — the process-wide `ACCESSIBLE_CONNECTORS_CACHE` is keyed by
  `(chatgpt_base_url, account_id, chatgpt_user_id, is_workspace_account)` and
  `read_cached_accessible_connectors` only returns a hit when the stored key matches the
  requested key and it has not expired; a mismatched key falls through to `None` rather than
  returning another account's cached connector list, so concurrent sessions for different
  accounts cannot read each other's cached data (at worst they thrash the single-slot cache).

- `codex-rs/core/src/context/node_repl_review_evidence.rs` and its test module (`node_repl_review_evidence_tests.rs`): traced the token-bounding loop in `record` (reserved-tail budgeting, per-item truncation with `</` escaping, and image-vs-text token accounting) and the byte-budget eviction loop (`MAX_RETAINED_BYTES`, preferring to discard images before evicting whole responses, falling back to `pop_front` when no images remain to reclaim). Confirmed no infinite loop (every branch either reduces `retained_bytes`, discards an item, or evicts a response) and no arithmetic panics (all subtraction is `saturating_sub`). `bounded_provenance` correctly strips `\n`, `\r`, `[`, `]`, `=`, and `</` from tool/cell/call-id inputs before they are interpolated into the unescaped `tool=... cell=... call=...` provenance string, which prevents a controlled tool/cell/call id from forging extra keys in that string.

  drop-based fail-closed semantics, session-scoped allow/deny caches keyed by
  environment+host+protocol+port) is intricate but internally consistent and is exercised by a
  thorough test suite covering concurrent attribution, cancellation races, and disconnect
  fallbacks. `sync_session_approved_hosts_to` only takes its own commit lock, not the target's,
  but its only caller (`guardian/review_session.rs`) uses it to seed a freshly created review
  session before that session starts handling any network requests, so the theoretical race is not
  reachable in the current call graph.
- `codex-rs/core/src/tools/orchestrator.rs`: the approval → sandbox-selection → retry-with-escalation
  flow (including the `owner_network_policy`/`managed_network_active` handling and the OTel
  sandbox-outcome reporting on every exit path) was traced end to end; every branch that returns an
  error also reports a sandbox outcome or is a case that intentionally doesn't need to.
- `codex-rs/core/src/tools/registry.rs`: `dispatch_any_with_terminal_outcome`'s
  hook/lifecycle/telemetry sequencing (PreToolUse block/rewrite, tool execution, PostToolUse
  block/feedback, `notify_tool_finish_if_unclaimed`'s single-fire guard via `AtomicBool::swap`) is
  consistent and matches its test coverage in `registry_tests.rs`.
- `codex-rs/core/src/tools/runtimes/apply_patch.rs`: the `follow_symlinks` derivation ("only reject
  links when an otherwise-required sandbox was bypassed") and the sandbox-denial detection for both
  executor-managed and locally-sandboxed attempts match the inline comments and the surrounding
  `Sandboxable`/`Approvable`/`ToolRuntime` trait contracts.
- `codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/view_image.rs`: local image reads go through the resolved
  environment's sandboxed filesystem, and `image::load_from_memory` (image 0.25.9) applies a
  512 MiB default `max_alloc` limit, bounding decompression-bomb-style memory blowup even though
  the handler itself imposes no explicit size cap.
- `codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/tool_search_spec.rs`: the aggregate source-description byte
  budgeting (`MAX_TOOL_SEARCH_SOURCE_DESCRIPTION_BYTES`) correctly bounds output even with adversarial
  multi-byte-character descriptions, per `create_tool_search_tool_bounds_aggregate_source_descriptions`.

This shard covers the unified-exec tool runtime stack (`codex-rs/core/src/tools/runtimes/*` and
`codex-rs/core/src/unified_exec/*`), the shared sandbox/approval primitives
(`codex-rs/core/src/tools/sandboxing.rs`), tool-spec planning
(`codex-rs/core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs`), and a handful of turn-scoped bookkeeping modules
(`turn_diff_tracker.rs`, `turn_metadata.rs`, `turn_timing.rs`, `tool_dispatch_trace.rs`,
`tool_namespaces_info.rs`). This is dense, security-sensitive code (credential-broker snapshot
rewriting, escalation policy, sandbox bypass gating), so it received a correspondingly careful
read plus verification rather than a skim.

Concretely verified, not just read:

- `cargo check -p codex-core --lib --tests` compiles clean (one pre-existing, unrelated warning
  in `core/tests/suite/openai_file_mcp.rs`, outside this shard).
- Ran the full unit-test suites that exercise these files and all passed: `unified_exec::*` (75
  tests, including the credential-broker `stdin_approval_preserves_the_reviewed_terminal` TOCTOU
  test and the `process_manager` pruning tests), `tools::runtimes::*` (77 tests, including the
  large `maybe_wrap_shell_lc_with_snapshot_*` suite that runs real subshells to verify credential
  restoration), `tools::sandboxing` (11), `tools::spec_plan` (55), `turn_diff_tracker` (15),
  `turn_metadata` (26), `turn_timing` (10), `tool_dispatch_trace` (4).
- Manually hand-traced `HeadTailBuffer::push_buffer` (`unified_exec/head_tail_buffer.rs`) against
  a concrete two-chunk merge scenario (10-byte budget, 6+6 byte pushes) to confirm the head/tail
  split and `omitted_bytes` accounting matches what an uncapped concatenation-then-truncate would
  produce; it does. This function has no direct unit test (only `push_chunk` is unit-tested) but
  is exercised indirectly by the `process_manager`/`async_watcher` integration tests above.
- Hand-traced `TurnDiffTracker::apply_update`'s rename/overwrite bookkeeping
  (`origin_by_current_path`) against the "delete-then-move-overwrite" and "move-over-existing"
  test cases; the tracked-origin chain resolves correctly for chained renames.
- Checked `sandbox_override_for_first_attempt` / `unsandboxed_execution_allowed` /
  `sandbox_permissions_preserving_denied_reads` in `tools/sandboxing.rs`: the deny-read
  preservation logic (an escalation request must not silently drop `deny` filesystem rules) is
  consistent across all three call sites and covered by
  `deny_read_blocks_explicit_escalation_and_policy_bypass`.
- Checked the credential-broker env-restoration shell-script generation in
  `tools/runtimes/mod.rs` (`maybe_wrap_shell_lc_with_snapshot`, `build_brokered_credential_exports`,
  `build_override_exports_for_keys`) for shell-injection risk: every interpolated value that
  isn't a `is_valid_shell_variable_name`-validated identifier goes through `shell_single_quote`
  before being placed inside a single-quoted literal at its use site (verified all five call
  sites). `is_valid_shell_variable_name` correctly restricts to `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`.
- Checked `UnifiedExecProcessManager::prune_processes_if_needed` /
  `process_id_to_prune_from_meta` (LRU eviction with an interaction-lock guard and an "8 most
  recently used are protected" rule): the logic degrades safely (allows the soft cap to be
  exceeded) rather than evicting a live process when an exited-but-locked process is blocking
  eviction, which matches its comment and the
  `pruning_does_not_evict_live_process_while_exited_process_is_finalizing` test.
- Checked `write_stdin`'s post-approval identity revalidation (`prepare_process_handles` +
  `Arc::ptr_eq`) against process-ID reuse during a pending approval; this is exactly the scenario
  `stdin_approval_preserves_the_reviewed_terminal`'s `"replace\n"` case exercises, and it resolves
  to `UnknownProcessId` rather than writing into the wrong (recycled) process.
- Checked `extract_shell_script` in `zsh_fork/unix_escalation.rs`, which scans for the first
  `-c`/`-lc` triple anywhere in argv rather than assuming position 0. Since the argv it receives
  is always constructed by Codex's own wrapping logic (not raw attacker-controlled shell text),
  the "first match wins" behavior is safe in practice, and `extract_shell_script_supports_wrapped_command_prefixes`
  covers the intended wrapped-prefix cases (`env`, `sandbox-exec -p`).
- Checked the internal-Guardian tool-source gate in `tools/spec_plan.rs`
  (`add_core_tool_sources`'s `is_basic_session_source` branch): it only exposes
  `exec_command`/`write_stdin`/`view_image` when *both* the turn's own permission profile and
  every configured environment's permission profile are `PermissionProfile::Managed`, returning
  early (no tools) otherwise. This is covered by
  `internal_guardian_sessions_require_managed_secondary_environments`, including the negative case
  where a secondary environment uses an unmanaged profile.

No correctness, security, or error-handling defect was found in this shard that meets the bar for
a `CR-###` finding (reproducible, not just a style/design preference). The code is unusually
heavily tested for its complexity, and every subtle piece of logic traced above already has a
targeted test covering the edge case it appears designed for.

- `codex-rs/core/src/unified_exec/stdin_approval.rs` and
  `stdin_approval_tests.rs`: traced `TerminalPermissions::review_requirement`
  and `approval_reason` against all the accompanying test cases (reduced
  permissions, proxy bypass, denied-read policy changes, environment-owned
  network changes, internal grants, and the Windows-sandbox-elevation
  Native-vs-Executor split). The logic is internally consistent, the NUL-byte
  rejection only matters on the manual-approval path (auto-approved writes skip
  shell quoting so NUL bytes are fine there), and `approval_reason` never
  serializes `internal_permissions` into the text shown to the model, matching
  the module's stated invariant.
- `codex-rs/core/src/unified_exec/shell_snapshot.rs`: `prewarm_shell_snapshots`
  and `shell_snapshot_request` correctly gate on `ShellSnapshotV2`, remote
  environments, `allow_login_shell`, `network_policy`, and `UnifiedExecShellMode`
  before attempting a snapshot capture; failures are logged at `debug` and
  swallowed rather than surfaced, which is appropriate for a best-effort warmup
  path.
- `codex-rs/core/src/unified_exec/process_state.rs`: `ProcessState::exited` and
  `::failed` correctly preserve unrelated fields (`failure_message` on exit,
  `exit_code` on failure) rather than clobbering them.
- `codex-rs/core/src/util.rs` `backoff`: `attempt.saturating_sub(1)` correctly
  treats `attempt == 0` the same as `attempt == 1` (base delay, no growth), and
  jitter is bounded to `0.9..1.1` so backoff never collapses to zero or grows
  unbounded from the jitter term alone.
- `codex-rs/core/src/utils/json.rs` `serialized_json_bytes`: the `Write` impl on
  `JsonByteCounter` uses `saturating_add` and returns `bytes.len()` (not a
  short count), so `serde_json::to_writer` will not treat it as a partial write.
- `codex-rs/core/src/web_search.rs`, `windows_system_config.rs`,
  `windows_sandbox.rs`: reviewed the feature-flag precedence
  (`WindowsSandboxElevated` over `WindowsSandbox`), the legacy-key fallback
  parsing, and the metrics emission paths; all match their accompanying unit
  tests (`windows_sandbox_tests.rs`) and don't swallow or misreport the
  elevated-setup-cancelled vs. generic-failure metric distinction.
- The remaining files in this shard
  (`unified_exec/process_manager_tests.rs`, `process_tests.rs`,
  `stdin_approval_tests.rs`, `user_shell_command.rs`/`_tests.rs`,
  `util_tests.rs`, `utils/mod.rs`, `utils/path_utils.rs`,
  `windows_sandbox_read_grants_tests.rs`, `windows_sandbox_tests.rs`,
  `worktree_trust_tests.rs`, and everything under
  `codex-rs/core/tests/common/` and `tests/all.rs`) are test code or thin
  re-exports. They were read in full; the test-support helpers
  (`responses.rs`'s `validate_request_body_invariants`, the WebSocket/SSE test
  servers in `responses.rs`/`streaming_sse.rs`, the `apps_test_server.rs` mock
  responder, and `context_snapshot.rs`'s redaction/normalization helpers) are
  internally consistent with the tests that exercise them and did not reveal
  correctness bugs against the production code they help exercise.

This shard consists entirely of `codex-rs/core` integration-test files (test harness
helpers under `tests/common/`, plus the `tests/suite/*.rs` behavioral test suites and
one Bazel-only Windows/Wine integration test). All 30 assigned files were opened and
reviewed; the largest files (`approvals.rs` 4893 lines, `code_mode.rs` 7489 lines,
`compact.rs` 5412 lines, `client.rs` 3893 lines, `client_websockets.rs` 2945 lines,
`apply_patch_cli.rs` 2487 lines, `compact_remote.rs` 1612 lines) were read in large,
overlapping passes (each substantially or fully covered) rather than skimmed, given
their outsized share of the shard's ~36,000 total lines.

Areas specifically exercised and found correct:

- **Approval / sandbox matrix (`approvals.rs`)**: the table-driven `scenarios()` +
  `run_scenario` harness covers danger-full-access, read-only, workspace-write,
  apply_patch, and unified-exec approval paths, including exec-policy amendment
  persistence, network-policy amendment persistence (allow/deny rules written to
  `default.rules` and later respected), Guardian/auto-review bypass rules for
  `require_escalated` and required-model reviews, and zsh-fork inner-script escalation.
  The `shell_startup_credentials_are_brokered` and `brokered_shell_snapshot_fallback`
  tests specifically assert that real credentials (`ghp_...`, `custom_...` tokens) never
  reach model-visible command output or persisted shell snapshots, and that excluded
  environment variables are not observable by the command. These assertions are
  correctly wired to the fixtures that plant the "real" credential values.
- **apply_patch sandboxing (`apply_patch_cli.rs`)**: path-traversal rejection (`../escape.txt`),
  symlink-swap-after-approval rejection, symlink-escape via a soft link into a read-only
  root, and directory-target decoy hunks used to try to widen permissions are all tested
  and assert the outside file is left unchanged in each case. The one apparently
  permissive scenario (`apply_patch_cli_preserves_existing_hard_link_outside_workspace`)
  is explicitly documented and asserted as intentional pre-existing hard-link semantics,
  not a new escape introduced by the tool, and is out of scope for this test-only shard.
- **Code Mode isolation (`code_mode.rs`)**: tests for `CodeModeOnly` fail-closed behavior
  when the host process is missing/disabled, app-only MCP tools being neither listed nor
  callable from the JS sandbox (and never reaching the upstream MCP server), configured
  MCP-server/tool-namespace omission from Code Mode while remaining directly callable,
  and `view_image` rejecting invalid files without leaking file contents into model-visible
  output.
- **Credential-bearing git metadata (`responses_headers.rs`)**: verifies both the
  `x-codex-turn-metadata` header and the equivalent request-body field strip embedded
  git-remote credentials (`https://alice:token@...`) down to a sanitized URL.
- **Test harness plumbing (`tests/common/*.rs`)**: `TestCodexBuilder`/`TestEnv` correctly
  thread through local vs. Docker/Wine-exec environment selection, path-convention
  conversion (POSIX vs. Windows), and model-catalog fixture construction; no state leaks
  or unsafe environment mutation (`std::env::set_var`) were found — the one comment
  referencing `set_var` explicitly explains why it is avoided.
- **Collaboration/instructions and compaction bookkeeping** (`collaboration_instructions.rs`,
  `compact.rs`, `compact_remote.rs`, `agents_md.rs`): dedup/replacement semantics for
  AGENTS.md and collaboration-mode developer instructions across resumes, forks, and
  subagent spawns are covered with source-list assertions that match the described
  precedence (global before project, creation-time snapshot retained across ordinary
  turns, replacement-once semantics after edits).

No correctness, security, or test-hygiene defects were identified in the reviewed
material. Grep sweeps across the full file list for common smells (`TODO`/`FIXME`/
`unimplemented!`/`todo!`, disabled assertions, hardcoded loopback ports, `set_var`/
`remove_var`) turned up nothing actionable beyond documentation comments and one
deliberately-unreachable fixture URL (`http://127.0.0.1:1/mcp`, used intentionally to
simulate an unreachable MCP dependency).

- Read the full guardian test suite in this shard (`guardian_authorization.rs`,
  `guardian_context_budget.rs`, `guardian_history.rs`, `guardian_mcp_elicitation.rs`,
  `guardian_retained_context.rs`, `guardian_retry.rs`, `guardian_review.rs` (2211 lines,
  read in full across two passes), `guardian_review_cancellation.rs`,
  `guardian_subagent_authorization.rs`). These exercise authorization-version
  invalidation on compaction/rollback/resume/fork, retained-context budgeting, Guardian
  review retry/timeout/denial paths, and cross-thread (parent/child) authorization
  isolation. The assertions consistently check both the positive case (expected content
  reaches the reviewer) and the negative case (secrets/denied paths/forged authorization
  text do not leak into the reviewer transcript or the parent model's own context), and
  the logic for expected message ordering/counts lines up with the scenarios being
  driven. No correctness or security defect found.
- Read `external_auth.rs` in full, including the Bedrock AWS SigV4 signing,
  credential-export subprocess re-invocation trick (`std::env::current_exe()` re-run as
  `aws`), and the external-ChatGPT-auth 401-retry flow. The assertions on
  `authorization`/`x-amz-security-token` headers and the account-id switch mid-flight
  test (`daybreak_discards_in_flight_account_changes_without_apps`) correctly race a
  released gate against a mid-call auth swap, and no real credentials are hardcoded
  (only synthetic test tokens like `header.e30.initial`).
- Read `hooks.rs` (5820 lines, in full) and `hooks_mcp.rs`, `hooks_executor.rs`,
  `interrupt_hooks.rs` covering PreToolUse/PostToolUse/PermissionRequest/SessionStart/
  Stop/Interrupt hook semantics (blocking, rewriting, additional-context injection and
  spilling, async-hook non-blocking guarantees, plugin-sourced hooks, MCP-tool hooks,
  and executor-attached cleanup hooks). Aside from the marker-path collision above, the
  fixtures and assertions are internally consistent and each test's expected side effects
  match what its mocked hook script does.
- Read `image_rollout.rs`, `items.rs`, `injected_models_cache.rs`,
  `compact_remote_trimming.rs`, `compact_resume_fork.rs`, `context_annotations.rs`,
  `current_time_reminder.rs`, `cyber_access_program.rs`, `cyber_exec_policy.rs`,
  `daybreak_access.rs`, `deprecation_notice.rs`, `exec.rs`, `exec_policy.rs`,
  `extension_sandbox.rs`, `fork_thread.rs`, `git_enrichment.rs`. These cover streaming
  item/reasoning/plan-mode event ordering, image resize/rollout persistence, model-cache
  injection races, remote-compaction trimming, thread fork/resume history slicing, and
  git-metadata credential redaction. No defects found; the credential-redaction test
  (`user_turn_git_enrichment_redacts_remote_credentials` in `git_enrichment.rs`) correctly

  request.

Read all 30 files in this shard (`json_result.rs`, `live_cli.rs`, `mcp_auth_elicitation.rs`,
`mcp_auth_refresh.rs`, `mcp_extension_protocol.rs`, `mcp_oauth_refresh_tests.rs`,

Beyond reading, I built and ran the tests to check for latent defects rather than relying on
static reading alone:
- `cargo test -p codex-core --test all --no-run` compiles cleanly (one pre-existing unused-import
  warning, the finding above).
- With `RUST_MIN_STACK=67108864` (this sandbox's default thread stack is too small for this
  binary and otherwise aborts with an unrelated stack overflow on *any* test in the `all` binary,
  including trivial ones — an environment artifact, not a code defect), I ran every test filtered
  to this shard's modules: 176/178 passed outright, and the other 2 failures
  (`mcp_tool_cache::cached_mcp_startup_is_eager_for_root_and_lazy_for_subagents` and
  `mcp_tool_cache::mcp_calls_stay_bound_to_each_thread`) were solely due to the `test_stdio_server`
  helper binary not yet being built in this checkout; both passed once I built
  `codex-rmcp-client`'s `test_stdio_server` bin target. The Linux-only network-approval tests
  correctly report `ignored, requires the trusted Linux proxy bridge` on this macOS host (their
  `#[cfg_attr(not(target_os = "linux"), ignore = ...)]` gates work as intended), and the one
  `#[ignore = "TODO(aibrahim): flaky"]` test is already self-documented as known-flaky.
  `mcp_refresh_cleanup::refresh_keeps_superseded_mcp_server_alive_for_in_flight_calls` passed; the
  sibling `multi_exec_server_sandbox::two_exec_servers_isolate_workspace_write_roots` only failed
  because the `codex` CLI binary itself wasn't built in this checkout (it spawns
  `codex exec-server`), again an environment gap rather than a source defect.
- I specifically chased down one suspicion worth recording: several files in this shard
  (`multi_agent_resume.rs`'s `decoded_body`, `network_approval.rs`'s `decoded_request_body`)
  manually decode zstd-compressed request bodies before parsing JSON when matching on a raw
  `wiremock::Request`, which implies request bodies can be zstd-compressed. `json_result.rs`'s
  `match_json_text_param` parses `req.body` with `serde_json::from_slice` directly, with no zstd
  handling, which looked like it could silently never match if the request were compressed
  (`Feature::EnableRequestCompression` defaults to `true` in `codex-features/src/lib.rs`). I
  traced the actual gating in `core/src/client.rs`'s `responses_request_compression`: compression
  is only applied when `auth.is_some_and(CodexAuth::uses_codex_backend)` and the provider is
  OpenAI — the default test auth used by `test_codex()` in `json_result.rs` isn't ChatGPT-backend
  auth, so no compression is applied and the raw-body match works correctly. I ran the test
  (`suite::json_result::codex_returns_json_result_for_gpt5`) and it passes. This is not a live bug
  today, but is a latent fragility: copying this raw-body-matching pattern into a test that does
  use `CodexAuth::create_dummy_chatgpt_auth_for_testing()` (several other files in the wider suite
  do) would silently break matching. Not filed as a defect since no current test in this shard
  triggers it, and the note in `pending_input.rs`/`agents_md.rs`/`responses_api_proxy_headers.rs`
  (`config.features.disable(Feature::EnableRequestCompression)` with the comment "the streaming
  fixture records raw request bodies for JSON assertions") shows the pattern is already understood
  elsewhere in the codebase.
- `network_approval.rs` and `network_approval_completion.rs` extensively exercise the managed
  network proxy / Guardian network-approval flow (host/port/protocol scoping, session vs. once
  approvals, policy amendments, concurrent-request trigger attribution, remote-vs-local
  environment isolation). The logic and assertions are internally consistent and, where runnable
  on this platform, pass.
- `otel.rs`'s telemetry assertions (`extract_log_field`, tool-decision/sandbox-outcome events,
  network-policy-decision redaction of host/source) were traced by hand against the span/event
  emission code paths they assert on and are correct; the redaction test
  (`network_policy_decisions_omit_source_and_destination`) is a real security-relevant regression
  guard against leaking destination hosts into logs, and it passes.

This shard is entirely integration-test code for `codex-rs/core` (30 files, ~35k
lines total). All 30 assigned files were opened; the smaller files
(`permissions_messages.rs`, `personality.rs`, `plugins.rs`, `prompt_cache_key.rs`,
`prompt_caching.rs`, `prompt_debug_tests.rs`, `quota_exceeded.rs`,
`realtime_initial_items.rs`, `realtime_misalignment.rs`,
`realtime_sideband_endpoint.rs`, `reasoning_effort_override.rs`,
`remote_env_failure_tests.rs`, `request_compression.rs`,
`request_permissions_tool.rs`, `request_user_input.rs`,
`request_user_input_async.rs`, `responses_api_proxy_headers.rs`,
`responses_lite.rs`, `responses_system_proxy.rs`, `resume.rs`,
`resume_warning.rs`, `rollout_budget.rs`) were read in full. The largest files
(`realtime_conversation.rs` [5683 lines], `remote_env.rs` [4028 lines],
`rmcp_client.rs` [4570 lines], `request_permissions.rs` [2254 lines],
`retry_after.rs` [1775 lines], `review.rs` [1521 lines], `remote_models.rs`
[1512 lines], `request_plugin_install.rs` [1339 lines]) were read in large,
representative sections (most test bodies plus every helper function; roughly
half of each file by line count) rather than byte-for-byte in full, with
targeted follow-up reads on the sections most likely to hide a real defect:
permission-escalation/widening boundaries (`request_permissions.rs`), plugin
install accept/decline flows and leak-of-declined-plugin-id checks
(`request_plugin_install.rs`), ChatGPT-auth leakage to attacker-configured MCP
origins (`rmcp_client.rs`: `streamable_http_chatgpt_auth_is_not_sent_to_configured_origin`,
`configured_chatgpt_base_url_does_not_grant_mcp_chatgpt_auth`), and
symlink/`..`-escape sandbox enforcement for the remote filesystem
(`remote_env.rs`: `remote_test_env_sandboxed_read_rejects_symlink_parent_dotdot_escape`,
`remote_test_env_remove_removes_symlink_not_target`).

Across this sampling, permission-grant tests correctly assert that a granted
`request_permissions`/additional-permissions profile does not widen beyond the
literal requested path (cwd write, `/tmp` write, and denied-child-directory
carve-outs are all exercised and asserted to stay blocked), that denied
approvals leave the target file untouched, and that session-scoped grants
persist while turn-scoped grants do not leak across turns. The MCP auth tests
confirm ChatGPT bearer credentials are never forwarded to an MCP server whose
URL/base-url an attacker-controlled project or user config could point at a
third-party origin. The remote-environment filesystem tests confirm symlink
traversal and `..`-escape attempts against a sandboxed root are rejected via
path normalization rather than being silently allowed. The retry/backoff tests
in `retry_after.rs` are consistent with several `TODO(anp) respect Retry-After`
comments documenting a known, already-tracked product limitation (local
backoff is used instead of the server's `Retry-After` header); this is called
out in the test names/doc-comments themselves and is not a defect introduced
by this code.

No test-logic bugs (inverted assertions, wrong variable substituted into an
`assert_eq!`, tautological assertions, or a test that could pass regardless of
the behavior under test) were found in the portions read. I did not find any
credential-bearing literal, unsafe temp-file handling, or command-injection
opportunity introduced by the test fixtures themselves.

Given the sheer size of the four largest files, I cannot rule out a defect in
the roughly-half of each of those files I did not read line-by-line (in
particular, sections of `realtime_conversation.rs` between the reconnect/
misalignment tests and its final ~2150 lines, the back half of
`request_permissions.rs`, and the back half of `rmcp_client.rs` covering
streamable-HTTP OAuth token refresh) — flag those to a follow-up pass if a
deeper audit of this shard is wanted.

- `codex-rs/core/tests/suite/rollout_compression.rs`: the fork/checkpoint/resume/compression flow is internally consistent — it ages rollout files via `set_times` (without truncating, so no data loss), waits for the background compression worker to replace `.jsonl` with `.jsonl.zst`, and verifies via `zstd::stream::decode_all` that the compressed bytes round-trip to the original file bytes before asserting the resumed thread's request only contains history in the expected checkpoint/inheritance boundary.
- `codex-rs/core/tests/suite/rollout_list_find.rs`, `sqlite_state.rs`, `startup_cancellation.rs`: rollout/session-index/state-db lookup and cancellation-during-startup tests use bounded polling loops with explicit timeouts and appropriately distinguish sqlite-backed vs filesystem-fallback lookup paths; no unbounded waits or unchecked races were found.
- `codex-rs/core/tests/suite/skills_extension.rs` (very large: skill catalog budgeting, aliasing, executor/orchestrator/host provider composition, model-switch catalog re-render): the budget-sharing, shortening, and omission assertions (`assert_full_descriptions`, `assert_shortened_descriptions`, `metadata_cost`) are consistent with the constants they're parameterized over (`HOST_CATALOG`, `EXECUTOR_CATALOG`, the various `*_CONTEXT_WINDOW` constants), and the alias-root/order-preservation test constructs directories under a long shared-prefix parent specifically to catch alias-ordering regressions rather than accidentally relying on lexical path order.
- `codex-rs/core/tests/suite/step_settings.rs` / `step_settings_snapshots.rs` / `step_settings_compaction.rs`: the mid-turn model-switch bookkeeping (turn-scoped vs thread-scoped settings, captured budgets/truncation policies surviving resume and fork, MCP confirmation-policy snapshots per step) is exercised with matched turn IDs and model sequences that line up with the mocked request sequences.
- `codex-rs/core/tests/suite/subagent_notifications.rs` and `subagent_service_tier.rs`: parent/child/grandchild context-forking, mailbox delivery, and service-tier propagation assertions correctly distinguish "root policy changes must not silently rewrite an already-running child's captured settings" from "future/idle child turns must pick up the new policy," and the request-body matchers are specific enough (e.g. requiring/excluding particular call IDs and prior prompts) to avoid false-positive matches against unrelated mocked responses.
- `codex-rs/core/tests/suite/token_budget.rs`: context-window id/window-chaining assertions (`token_budget_window_ids`), auto-compact fallback buffer accounting, and the `AutoCompactTokenLimitScope::BodyAfterPrefix` variant are each covered with values that make the pass/fail boundary unambiguous (e.g. the reminder threshold is crossed by a specific, computed token delta rather than an arbitrary large margin).
- `codex-rs/core/tests/suite/tool_parallelism.rs`: the parallel-execution timing assertions use a barrier-synchronized warm-up phase plus a generous 1.6s ceiling, which is reasonable headroom for CI scheduling variance while still being tight enough to catch a regression to serial execution.
- `codex-rs/core/tests/suite/turn_state.rs` and `turn_input_submission.rs`: turn-state header propagation (reset between logical turns, preserved across same-turn follow-ups) and the admission/draining semantics (steer vs start, plan-mode atomic rejection, output-schema-mismatch rejection) are each verified against the exact request sequence recorded by the mock/streaming server, including negative assertions that rejected input never reaches the model.

- `codex-rs/exec-server-protocol/src/rpc.rs` — the bounded `JSONRPCMessage`
  deserializer (`BoundedValueSeed`/`BoundedValueVisitor`, `MAX_JSONRPC_VALUE_NODES`)
  correctly charges one budget unit per JSON node, including inside the
  `arbitrary_precision` number sentinel and the `RawValue` sentinel branches,
  and rejects duplicate object keys. The accompanying `rpc_tests.rs` exercises
  compact-array amplification, the raw-value bypass attempt, and duplicate
  keys, and I traced the accounting by hand to confirm no bypass.
- `codex-rs/exec-server/src/capability_discovery.rs` —
  `declared_file_path`'s traversal guard (reject empty path, reject any
  `/`/`\`-split component equal to `..`, then require
  `root.join(relative_path)?.starts_with(root)`) is backed by
  `PathUri::starts_with`'s segment-wise (not naive string-prefix) comparison
  in `codex-rs/utils/path-uri/src/lib.rs`, so a sibling directory like
  `root-evil` cannot pass as contained in `root`. Per-file (`MAX_FILE_BYTES`)
  and per-root (`BundleBudget`/`MAX_BUNDLE_BYTES_PER_ROOT`) size accounting is
  charged consistently between the pre-check and the actual streamed read.
- `codex-rs/exec-server/src/capability_discovery_cache.rs` — the cache keeps
  at most one entry per `SelectedCapabilityRoot`, always overwriting rather
  than accumulating when the sandbox context for that root changes; this
  causes cache churn when a root's sandbox flips repeatedly but does not
  produce stale or incorrect results, since a mismatched-sandbox entry is
  always treated as missing and refetched before being returned.
- `codex-rs/exec-server/src/client/accepted.rs` — the accepted-websocket
  replacement handoff (single in-flight replacement enforced by a
  `Semaphore::new(1)`, connection-lock held across the final `Failed` check
  and the synchronous channel `send`) correctly prevents a losing race from
  silently dropping a socket that no task will ever consume.
- The remaining files in this shard
  (`codex-rs/core/tests/suite/unified_exec*.rs`, `unstable_features_warning.rs`,
  `user_notification.rs`, `user_shell_cmd.rs`, `view_image.rs`, `web_search.rs`,
  `websocket_fallback.rs`, `window_headers.rs`, `windows_sandbox.rs`,
  `workspace_roots.rs`, `worktree_trust.rs`, `codex-rs/diagnostics/src/lib.rs`
  and `tests.rs`, `codex-rs/exec-server-protocol/src/environment_config.rs`,
