  `codex-rs/exec-server/src/arg0_exec_helper.rs`) are integration tests and
  small protocol/data-structure modules; I read them in full and found no
  correctness, security, or error-handling defects.

- `client_recovery.rs::SessionState::recover_events` (session/process-event resequencing on
  reconnect) — traced through the sequence-gap/exit-slot inference logic by hand with a
  hand-built scenario (exit event immediately after `last_published_seq` plus a later output chunk
  leaving a genuine gap) and confirmed it fails closed with `recovery_gap_error` rather than
  silently dropping or misordering data. The existing test suite
  (`process_event_reorder_rejects_oversized_output`,
  `process_event_reorder_accepts_gap_closing_event_at_limits`,
  `recovery_handles_dense_tail_output_and_newer_notification`,
  `recovery_rejects_output_at_closed_sequence`,
  `recovery_adds_sandbox_denial_to_pending_exit_event`) exercises the boundary conditions this logic
  depends on.
- `client_refresh.rs` (explicit connection-refresh/replacement flow, including the
  `refresh_lock`/`reconnect`/`current_client` locking discipline and cancellation-vs-installation
  race) — the lock-then-`continue` pattern in `refresh_connection` correctly drops both `MutexGuard`s
  before the next loop iteration re-acquires them (no deadlock), and the accompanying
  `client_refresh_tests.rs` suite specifically targets the races the doc comment calls out
  (superseded lookups, stalled Noise handshakes, retirement racing a pending mutation/process start
  before stream cleanup, concurrent refreshes preserving a still-valid session).
- `network_policy_audit.rs::emit_network_policy_decision` — validates length bounds and rejects
  control/whitespace characters on every attacker-influenceable field (`host`, `method`, `client`,
  `reason`, `timestamp`, `process_id`) before the values are interpolated into a `tracing::event!`
  call, which is adequate defense against log-injection via a crafted proxy decision.
- `connection.rs`'s stdio line-framing (`from_stdio_with_max_message_len`) — the oversized/
  unterminated-message handling (including the one-byte lookahead for a CRLF split exactly at the
  size limit) matches its two boundary tests
  (`stdio_connection_accepts_message_at_size_limit`, `stdio_connection_rejects_overlong_unterminated_message`).

- `codex-rs/exec-server/src/no_follow/unix.rs` and `no_follow/mod.rs`: the
  "no follow" filesystem helper walks each path component from `/` with
  `openat(..., O_NOFOLLOW | O_DIRECTORY)` for every intermediate directory and
  opens the leaf with `O_NOFOLLOW` as well, which correctly defeats symlink
  attacks on *any* path component, not just the final one (a common mistake,
  since a single `open(..., O_NOFOLLOW)` on the full path only protects the
  leaf). `write_file` also opens with `O_NONBLOCK` before validating the
  descriptor is a regular file, which avoids blocking on a FIFO planted at the
  target path. `metadata_sync`, `create_directory`, and `remove` all correctly
  reject a symlink anywhere they encounter one rather than silently following
  it.
- `codex-rs/exec-server/src/noise_channel.rs`, `noise_relay/message_framing.rs`,
  `noise_relay/ordered_ciphertext.rs`: the hybrid IK handshake, per-record
  framing, and out-of-order-ciphertext reassembly all bound their inputs
  (message length caps, reorder-window caps, pending-byte caps) and fail
  closed on tampering, replay, and out-of-range values; the accompanying unit
  tests exercise tampered ciphertext, replayed ciphertext, oversized payloads,
  and mismatched prologues/keys, and all pass locally (`cargo test -p
  codex-exec-server --lib`, run against this checkout).
- `codex-rs/exec-server/src/network_policy_decisions.rs`: the network policy
  decider validates the host (non-empty, bounded length, no control/whitespace
  characters) before making the reverse RPC, bounds and sanitizes the
  controller's response reason, and fails closed (`deny("not_allowed")`) on
  timeout, disconnect, or process shutdown; this is well covered by
  `network_policy_decisions_tests.rs` and all cases pass.
- `codex-rs/exec-server/src/local_process.rs`: process registration
  (`start_process`), stdin write deduplication (`exec_write` /
  `AcceptedStdinWriteIds`), and output retention/read paging (`exec_read`) hold
  the `processes` mutex across each check-then-act sequence, so there is no
  double-start, no double-write-on-retry, and no lost wakeup; retained output
  is bounded by both byte count and chunk count. Ran the full local unit-test
  suite for this shard (72 tests covering `fs_sandbox`, `local_file_system`,
  `no_follow`, `noise_channel`, `noise_relay`, `network_policy_decisions`,
  `local_process`, `process`, `process_sandbox`) and all pass on this
  checkout.
- `codex-rs/exec-server/src/fs_sandbox.rs`: the environment passed to the
  sandboxed fs helper process is built from an explicit allowlist
  (`FS_HELPER_ENV_ALLOWLIST`) rather than inherited wholesale, which is
  verified by a test asserting that secrets such as `OPENAI_API_KEY` and
  `HTTPS_PROXY` are dropped while `PATH`/`TMPDIR`/`TMP`/`TEMP` are preserved.

- `codex-rs/exec-server/src/regular_file.rs` (`read_sensitive_file_to_string`): uses
  `O_NOFOLLOW`/`FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT` plus a post-open `is_symlink()`/`is_disk_file()`
  check, giving correct TOCTOU-safe rejection of symlinks at the final path component on both
  Unix and Windows; confirmed against `regular_file_tests.rs`'s symlink-rejection test.
- `codex-rs/exec-server/src/relay.rs` (`run_multiplexed_environment`): the Noise handshake
  admission path (duplicate-stream, too-many-streams, too-many-pending-validations, oversized
  authorization) is checked before the expensive `PendingResponderHandshake::read_request`
  crypto work runs, and `MAX_FAILED_NOISE_HANDSHAKES` bounds retries per physical connection;
  cross-checked against `relay_noise_tests.rs`'s budget-exhaustion and pending-validation
  tests.
- `codex-rs/exec-server/src/rpc.rs` / `rpc_server_requests.rs`: in-flight call bookkeeping
  (semaphore-gated slots, pending-map cleanup on timeout/cancel/close, reserved cleanup
  capacity) is consistent between the client and server-initiated request paths and matches
  the accompanying tests (`rpc_client_metrics_tests.rs`, `rpc_server_requests_tests.rs`),
  including the out-of-order-response and overflow/circuit-breaker cases.
- `codex-rs/exec-server/src/remote/direct.rs` (`require_tls_or_loopback`): correctly requires
  the secure scheme for non-loopback hosts while allowing loopback/`localhost` over the
  insecure scheme, verified against `direct_tests.rs::direct_endpoints_require_tls_except_on_loopback`.
- `codex-rs/exec-server/src/remote.rs` / `remote/direct.rs` / `remote/noise_tests.rs` /
  `remote/direct_tests.rs`: registry/harness-key-authorization secrets, cookies, and redirect
  `Location` headers are deliberately excluded from logs and from followed redirects; this is
  exercised by dedicated tests that capture real log output and assert the secrets are absent.

- `codex-rs/exec-server/src/server/session_registry.rs` — the attach/detach/resume lifecycle
  (active-connection rejection, detached-session TTL expiry via `expire_if_detached`, and the
  race between a resume and a pending expiry) is serialized correctly through the single
  `sessions` mutex and the per-entry `AttachmentState` lock; the tests
  (`long_poll_read_fails_after_session_resume`, `active_session_resume_is_rejected`,
  `transport_disconnect_detaches_session_during_in_flight_read` in `handler/tests.rs` and
  `processor.rs`) exercise the interesting races and pass by inspection of the logic.
- `codex-rs/exec-server/src/shell_snapshot.rs` and `shell_snapshot_tests.rs` — the single-flight
  `OnceCell`-based capture, bounded retry/backoff (`MAX_SNAPSHOT_ATTEMPTS`,
  `SNAPSHOT_RETRY_BACKOFF`), size limits, and the environment merge order (explicit
  `params.env` always wins over restored snapshot state, and managed-proxy env vars are
  stripped only when the managed-proxy marker is present) are consistent with their extensive,
  paused-clock test coverage in `shell_snapshot_tests.rs`.
- `codex-rs/exec-server/src/server/request_dispatcher.rs` — the two-lane (`ordinary`/`control`)
  admission-control design, the handshake-inline gate (`method == INITIALIZE_METHOD ||
  !self.initialized`), and the queue/dispatch/total duration telemetry bookkeeping (including the
  `saturating_sub` adjustment for synchronous route setup time) match the assertions in
  `request_dispatcher_tests.rs`.
- `codex-rs/exec-server/src/server/transport.rs` — rejecting any WebSocket upgrade request that
  carries an `Origin` header is a deliberate and correctly-implemented defense against
  browser-based DNS-rebinding/CSRF against the loopback listener (browsers always attach
  `Origin` to WebSocket handshakes; non-browser clients used by this codebase do not).
- `codex-rs/exec-server/src/server/handler.rs` — the `http/request` streaming-body path
  (`reserve_http_body_stream`/`release_http_body_stream`/`start_http_body_stream`) releases the
  reservation on every error path before returning, and `RouteAwareHttpRequestRunner::run` always
  returns `Some(PendingRouteAwareHttpBodyStream)` on success when `stream_response` is set, so
  there is no reservation leak on the success path either.
- `codex-rs/exec-server/src/websocket_pong_watchdog.rs` and its tests — deadline
  set/extend/reset semantics match the documented behavior (`ping_sent` does not extend an
  existing deadline; `received_pong` clears it).

- `codex-rs/exec-server/tests/file_system_unix.rs` and `file_system_windows.rs`: the extensive
  symlink/junction/hard-link escape tests (`file_system_sandboxed_read_rejects_symlink_escape`,
  `file_system_copy_rejects_symlink_escape_source`/`_destination`,
  `file_system_remove_rejects_symlink_escape`,
  `file_system_operations_can_reject_symlinks_in_any_path_component`, the Windows junction
  equivalent, and `sandboxed_file_operations_cannot_read_helper_siblings`) consistently assert
  that sandbox-restricted filesystem operations cannot escape through symlinks/junctions/hard
  links in any path segment, and that the remote filesystem helper does not inherit the calling
  process's own sandbox exceptions. These read as a coherent, deliberately adversarial test
  suite and I did not find a gap in the coverage or a case where the assertions are weaker than
  they appear.
- `codex-rs/exec-server/tests/http_request.rs`: the body-delta byte-budget and backpressure
  tests (`http_response_body_stream_enforces_queued_byte_budget`,
  `http_response_body_streams_share_queued_byte_budget`,
  `http_response_body_stream_reports_backpressure_truncation`,
  `http_response_body_stream_rejects_oversized_delta`) verify that a malicious/misbehaving
  executor cannot make the client-side router buffer unbounded body bytes across one or many
  concurrent streamed HTTP responses, and that truncation is always surfaced as an explicit
  error rather than a silent/clean EOF. The accounting in the "shared budget" test (two streams
  each queuing half the budget, then one more frame past the limit) is internally consistent
  with the asserted per-stream byte counts.
- `codex-rs/exec-server/tests/http_request_logging.rs`: both tests capture real `tracing` output
  through a custom writer and include a self-check (`"log capture sentinel"` /
  `"http/request send failed"`) proving the capture mechanism itself is working, before
  asserting that query-string tokens, `Set-Cookie` values, and `Location` redirect targets never
  appear in logs for both success and failure paths.
- `codex-rs/exec-server/tests/websocket.rs`: `exec_server_rejects_browser_origin_websocket_handshake`
  confirms the server enforces an `Origin` allow-list at the WebSocket handshake (returning
  `403 Forbidden` for `https://evil.example`), which is the correct mitigation for
  browser-based cross-origin/DNS-rebinding access to the local exec-server socket.
- `codex-rs/exec/src/event_processor_with_human_output.rs` and
  `event_processor_with_jsonl_output.rs`: the final-message bookkeeping
  (`emit_final_message_on_shutdown`, clearing on `Failed`/`Interrupted`, recovering from
  `turn.items` when the streamed final message was missed) is exercised thoroughly by
  `event_processor_with_human_output_tests.rs` and `event_processor_with_jsonl_output_tests.rs`
  and the logic in both files agrees with those tests.

- `codex-rs/exec/src/lib.rs::sandbox_mode_from_permission_profile` and its callers (`thread_start_params_from_config`, `thread_resume_params_from_config`, and the `ThreadFork` branch of `run_exec_session`): I initially suspected that a `PermissionProfile::Managed` profile with unrestricted filesystem access but disabled network could fall through to `None` (no `sandbox` field sent to the server at all), silently downgrading the effective sandbox once no `permissions` profile ID is set. Tracing `active_permission_profile()` (`codex-rs/core/src/config/resolved_permission_profile.rs`) shows it only returns `None` for *legacy* `PermissionProfile` values derived from the old `SandboxPolicy` enum, and `SandboxPolicy::DangerFullAccess`/`WorkspaceWrite` conversions never produce an unrestricted-filesystem + disabled-network combination (only the new named-profile system can express that pairing, and named profiles always have `active_permission_profile() = Some(..)`). The suspicious branch therefore appears unreachable via this legacy fallback path, so no defect is reported here.
- `codex-rs/execpolicy/src/decision.rs`'s `Decision` enum relies on derived `Ord` (`Allow < Prompt < Forbidden`) so that `matched_rules.iter().map(RuleMatch::decision).max()` in both `codex-rs/execpolicy/src/execpolicycheck.rs` and `codex-rs/execpolicy/src/policy.rs` picks the most restrictive decision when multiple rules match the same command. This "most-restrictive-wins" aggregation is applied consistently in both places I could check within/adjacent to this shard.
- `codex-rs/execpolicy/src/amend.rs`'s `append_locked_line` acquires an exclusive `File::lock()` before seeking to the start, reading the full contents to de-duplicate, and appending — protecting against concurrent writers corrupting or duplicating rules, and it correctly inserts a missing trailing newline before appending. The rule-serialization helpers (`blocking_append_allow_prefix_rule`, `blocking_append_network_rule`) go through `serde_json::to_string` for every interpolated value (tokens, host, protocol, decision, justification), which avoids Starlark string-literal injection from rule content.
- The `codex-exec` integration test suite in `codex-rs/exec/tests/` (resume/fork/worktree/sandbox/seatbelt/hooks/output-schema/originator/prompt-stdin coverage) is extensive and, where I could trace the corresponding logic in `lib.rs`, the tests' expectations matched the implementation (e.g. `resolve_resume_thread_id`'s state-DB-first-then-rollout-repair logic, `build_exec_config`'s auto-review approval-policy retry, and the `thread_start`/`thread_resume`/`thread_fork` parameter builders).

- `codex-rs/ext/extension-api/src/state.rs` (`ExtensionData`, `ExtensionDataInit`): reviewed the `TypeId`-keyed attachment map, including `get_or_init`'s documented lock-held-during-init behavior, `insert_if`'s atomic check-and-set, and poison recovery in `entries()`. - `codex-rs/ext/goal/src/accounting.rs`, `src/runtime.rs`, `src/extension.rs`, `src/tool.rs` and both `goal` test files: traced the consecutive-empty-turn and consecutive-execution-failure counters (including the "replacement goal resets the counter" and "successful tool resets failures" cases), the `progress_accounting_lock`/`goal_state_lock` semaphore pair used to serialize concurrent tool-finish accounting (verified against `parallel_tool_finish_accounts_active_goal_progress_once`), and the parent/grandchild descendant-token roll-up logic used for nested subagent budgets (verified against `spawned_descendant_usage_exhausts_root_goal_budget_once` and `grandchild_usage_rolls_up_after_parent_runtime_unloads`). - `codex-rs/ext/guardian-reviewer/src/assessment.rs`: attempted to construct inputs that would make `parse_guardian_assessment`'s tolerant `find('{')`/`rfind('}')` recovery path select an "allow" outcome different from the model's actual final JSON object (e.g. decoy JSON objects before/after the real one, or stray unbalanced braces). In every case the extracted slice becomes invalid JSON (parse fails, propagating an error) unless the slice is exactly one well-formed JSON object, so the fallback cannot be tricked into fabricating a different `outcome` than what the model actually emitted as its outermost JSON object.

The `<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="…">` count is an intentionally coarse approximation (`text.len() - max_bytes`, not the true removed span including the marker's own footprint), which the tests independently pin to the same formula, so this is a documented approximation rather than a defect.
- `codex-rs/guardian-context/src/reviews.rs::render_review_evidence` — `correlation`, `action`, and `rationale` are escaped (`</` → `<\/`) *before* truncation, so a truncation cut can never reassemble an unescaped `</` at the boundary between the kept prefix/suffix and the inserted marker; `decision` is not escaped, but it is host-constructed from fixed enum fields (`assessment.status`, `assessment.risk_level`, `assessment.user_authorization`), not attacker-influenced free text, so omitting escaping there is not exploitable given its current construction in `codex-rs/core/src/context/guardian_review_evidence.rs`.
- `codex-rs/guardian-context/src/profile.rs` and `codex-rs/guardian-context/src/profile/window.rs` — the sync/async retention algorithms (recency cap for sync, protected/ordinary/tool token-and-count-bounded eviction pools for async) match their module-level doc comments ("Sync keeps recent entries; async protects approvals/final answers…") and are exercised by `profile_tests.rs`/`registry_tests.rs` for the boundary cases (offset numbering, five-newest-tool-entries reservation, omission notes vs. granular `TruncationObservation`s). The apparent asymmetry between sync and async protected-message handling is intentional per the documented design, not an oversight.
- `codex-rs/guardian-context/src/node_repl.rs` — the multimodal interleaved renderer (`render_inputs`) and the plain-text `ContextualUserFragment` renderer (`body()`, reached via the shared `render()` default when not in `Multimodal` mode or when no images are present) both independently bound total output to `MAX_RENDERED_BYTES` and produce matching marker text; images are deliberately excluded from this text budget because they are already bounded upstream by `NodeReplReviewEvidence::MAX_RETAINED_BYTES` in `codex-rs/core/src/context/node_repl_review_evidence.rs`, consistent with the file's stated module boundary ("Capture, storage eviction… stay in core").
- `codex-rs/history/src/retained_context.rs::rollback` — the boundary-found vs. fallback-conservative-drop branches, and the `Inherited`-source handling (which drops verified answers/non-inherited user messages more aggressively when no precise boundary can be established), are covered by `retained_context_tests.rs` across delayed acceptance-order recording, adopted/inherited instructions, and legacy checkpoints; behavior matches the documented fail-safe intent.
- `codex-rs/history/src/rollout_payload.rs` and `codex-rs/history/src/tests.rs` — wire-shape round-tripping for `RolloutItem`/`CompactedItem` (including legacy shapes, misaligned `replacement_history_metadata` rejection, and the numeric-to-string `window_id` migration) is thoroughly covered and consistent with the `Serialize`/`Deserialize` hand-rolled impls in `codex-rs/history/src/lib.rs`.

- Command hook execution (`codex-rs/hooks/src/engine/command_runner.rs`): environment is fully replaced via `env_clear()` + replay of the captured session snapshot + per-handler `env` overrides, then scrubbed with `scrub_non_inheritable_env_vars`, and I confirmed the dedicated test `command_hook_does_not_expose_configured_noise_auth_token` asserts the exec-server noise auth token never reaches a command hook's environment even when a handler tries to set it explicitly. Stdin writes and stdout/stderr draining are raced together under one `timeout()` so a hook that never reads stdin still respects its configured deadline (`hook_drains_output_and_times_out_while_stdin_is_blocked`), and process-group/job-object cleanup on timeout/drop is handled per-platform via `ProcessTreeGuard`.
- Hook trust/discovery model (`codex-rs/hooks/src/engine/discovery.rs`, `config_rules.rs`): only `User` and `SessionFlags` config layers can write persisted hook enable/trust state, so a `Project`-layer (e.g. repo-committed) or `Plugin`-layer hook cannot self-approve; a handler is only pushed into the executable `handlers` list when it is `Managed`/`Trusted` or trust is explicitly bypassed, while untrusted/modified hooks still surface in `hook_entries` for UI visibility but never execute. `hook_hash` is computed over a normalized, matcher-and-handler-only identity (ignoring irrelevant fields like an unsupported event's matcher) so cosmetic or platform-driven differences don't spuriously invalidate a previously-trusted hash.
- Async hook scheduling and shutdown (`command_runner.rs::CommandHookRuntime`): the `MAX_CONCURRENT_ASYNC_HOOKS` semaphore is acquired inside the spawned task (not before spawning), so hooks beyond the limit queue rather than get dropped, and `shutdown()` closes the semaphore, aborts all in-flight tasks, and drains the `JoinSet`; `shutdown_aborts_in_flight_async_hooks_without_delivering_context` confirms no late result leaks onto the result channel after shutdown.
- Output parsing fails closed (`codex-rs/hooks/src/engine/output_parser.rs` and each `events/*.rs` handler): non-JSON-looking stdout is treated as plain context/no-op, JSON-looking-but-invalid stdout is a hard `Failed` status rather than a silent no-op, and unsupported/contradictory field combinations (e.g. `permissionDecision:allow` without `updatedInput`, `decision:block` without a non-empty reason, `updatedMCPToolOutput`) are explicitly rejected for synchronous handlers while async/executor-scoped handlers correctly skip control-effect validation since they can't apply control effects (`ConfiguredHandler::can_apply_control_effects`).
- Plugin command templating (`engine/discovery.rs`, exercised by `plugin_hook_sources_expand_plugin_placeholders` in `engine/mod_tests.rs`): `${PLUGIN_ROOT}`/`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`/`${PLUGIN_DATA}`/`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` are substituted via plain string replacement before the command reaches the shell, which would be shell-injectable if the substituted value could contain shell metacharacters — but `PluginId::parse`/`validate_plugin_segment` (`codex-rs/plugin/src/plugin_id.rs`) restrict plugin and marketplace names to ASCII letters, digits, `-`, `_`, and `.`, so the paths built from those segments cannot introduce shell metacharacters through the plugin identity itself.

- `codex-rs/linux-sandbox/src/fd_mount.rs` / `fd_mount_tests.rs` and `codex-rs/linux-sandbox/src/launcher.rs` (`translate_legacy_bwrap_fd_mounts`): the descriptor-authentication path for legacy bubblewrap builds lacking `--ro-bind-fd`. - `codex-rs/otel/src/provider.rs` + `provider_shutdown_tests.rs`: traced the bounded-shutdown-worker design (detached OS thread started eagerly via `prepare_shutdown_worker`, `ManuallyDrop`-wrapped provider handed off through an `mpsc::sync_channel`, `tokio::time::timeout` around a oneshot completion signal) against its test suite, including the macOS `mprotect` fault-injection and Linux seccomp guard-page tests that exercise native-thread-creation failure paths. The design correctly avoids leaking the worker thread on normal `Drop` (the channel's `Sender` drop unblocks the worker's `recv()`), and `shutdown()` is idempotent via the `shutdown_started` `AtomicBool` swap. Sound.
- `codex-rs/otel/src/config.rs` (`STATSIG_API_KEY`): this is a `client-`-prefixed Statsig ingestion key, a class of key Statsig documents as safe to embed in distributed client code (analogous to a Segment/Amplitude write key), and `resolve_exporter` explicitly disables it under `cfg(debug_assertions)` so local builds never emit traffic. Not treated as a leaked credential.
- `codex-rs/otel/src/metrics/mod.rs` (`install_global`) and `client.rs` (`active_inner`/`shutdown`): the "outer handle stays fixed, inner provider swaps via `Arc<RwLock<..>>>`, but `shutdown()` always targets the handle's own original `inner`" design was cross-checked against `cached_global_metrics_follow_reinstalled_provider` and `statsig_disabled_metrics_are_not_exported` in `provider.rs`'s test module; behavior matches the documented intent (existing clones follow reinstallation; each installer only shuts down the exporter it created).

Read for internal consistency only: the owner-table fixtures correctly model a loopback connection as two distinct rows (accept-side and connect-side) and the "reversed tuple" lookup, duplicate-row-fails-closed, and truncated-table-fails-closed tests are logically consistent with fail-closed attribution semantics. The `windows_stable_ingress.rs` integration test's restricted-child-process harness (spawn-as-user, SID-scoped SOCKS/HTTP checks) reads coherently but was not run.

- `codex-rs/otel/src/trace_context.rs` — W3C trace-context propagation and configured-tracestate merging. `context_from_trace_headers` explicitly extracts against a fresh `Context::new()` (not the ambient context) so a malformed incoming `traceparent` cannot silently fall back to an unrelated active span; the `invalid_traceparent_returns_none` test exercises exactly this by attaching a valid parent context first and then confirming an invalid header still yields `None`. `encode_tracestate_member_fields`/`is_configured_tracestate_field_key`/`is_configured_tracestate_field_value`/`is_header_safe_tracestate_member_value` validate configured tracestate strictly enough to guarantee the final header value is comma/`=`/control-character free before it is installed process-wide via `set_tracestate_entries`, and `otel_provider_rejects_header_unsafe_configured_tracestate` in `otel/tests/suite/send.rs` confirms a value containing `\n` is rejected at `OtelProvider::try_new` time rather than being propagated. `merge_tracestate_entries`'s reverse-iteration-for-deterministic-order approach was cross-checked against `otlp_http_exporter_sends_traces_to_collector`, which asserts the exact merged tracestate string (`"example=alpha:one;keep:yes;beta:two,other=value"`); the logic and the test agree.
- `codex-rs/otel/src/tool_result_tests.rs` — verified against the actual `telemetry_preview` implementation in `codex-rs/otel/src/tool_result.rs` (outside this shard, read only to confirm the test's assumptions); the byte-boundary truncation, separator insertion, and `TRUNCATION_NOTICE` placement all match.
- `codex-rs/plugin/src/bundled_hooks.rs` — the unsigned-plugin cleanup-hook allowlist. Matching requires an exact `plugin_id`, an allowed `HookEventName`, `matcher.is_none()`, and (for `HookHandlerConfig::McpTool`) an exact `server`/`tool` pair; for `App` targets it additionally requires `input.is_empty()` and a caller-supplied `app_connector_id` match, which prevents a same-named-but-different-connector tool from being treated as the trusted cleanup target. Cross-checked the `HookHandlerConfig::McpTool` shape in `codex-rs/config/src/hook_config.rs`: the fields elided by the `..` pattern (`timeout_sec`, `status_message`) are not security-relevant, so the destructure does not silently ignore anything that should gate the allowlist decision.

Marketplace names disallow `.` entirely (via the character allowlist), and plugin names allow dots but explicitly reject `.`, `..`, leading/trailing dots, and `..` substrings, closing the traversal angle the comment calls out; tests cover both the acceptance and rejection cases.

The shortcuts for `Unrestricted`/`Disabled`/`External` inputs and the fail-closed handling of unsupported path shapes (unmaterialized `:workspace_roots`, glob grants, platform defaults) all resolve to explicit errors rather than silently widening access.

- `codex-rs/protocol/src/shell_environment.rs` and `shell_environment_tests.rs`: `populate_env`'s ordering (inherit → default `*KEY*`/`*SECRET*`/`*TOKEN*` excludes → custom excludes → `set` overrides → `include_only` → thread-id injection → final `retain(!is_non_inheritable_env_var)`) guarantees `NON_INHERITABLE_ENV_VARS` (including `CODEX_EXEC_SERVER_NOISE_AUTH_TOKEN`, `OPENAI_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE`, `OPENAI_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_CONTEXT`, `OPENAI_FEDERATION_RULE_ID`) are stripped from the final child environment even if a user-provided `set` override tries to reintroduce them, which the test `non_inheritable_environment_is_removed_after_policy_overrides` exercises directly. `scrub_non_inheritable_env_vars` correctly performs a case-insensitive sweep (via `to_ascii_uppercase`/`eq_ignore_ascii_case`) over both the process environment and the command's already-configured env, which is necessary on Windows where env var names are case-insensitive; `command_scrubber_removes_names_from_real_child_environment` verifies this against a real spawned child rather than only the in-memory `Command` builder.
- `codex-rs/realtime-webrtc/src/protocol.rs`, `message_reader.rs` (and their `_tests.rs`): frame length is validated against `MAX_FRAME_BYTES` before any buffer is grown to the attacker/peer-declared size (`decode_frame` is called on the 4-byte header alone first in both `read_message` and `MessageReader::next`), so a malicious/buggy helper process cannot force an unbounded allocation. Partial/fragmented frames across chunk boundaries are handled correctly (`decode_frame` returns `Ok(None)` when the buffer is short), and this is exercised by `reads_fragmented_and_coalesced_messages`, `cancelled_read_preserves_each_partial_header_and_payload`, `rejects_oversized_headers_without_waiting_for_payload`, and `rejects_truncation_at_every_byte_boundary`. `SessionDescription`'s `Debug` impl redacts SDP (which can carry ICE credentials), verified by `signaling_roundtrips_without_diagnostic_secrets`.

for duplicate/unknown thread/turn/call ids. The queueing logic in `code_cell.rs` for
runtime-cell-starts-before-model-visible-item and its lifecycle-event replay on flush is
consistent between the implementation and its tests, including the cross-thread runtime-cell-id
collision case (`runtime_code_cell_ids_can_repeat_across_threads`). The strict "bail on any
invariant violation" pattern used throughout the reducer (unknown thread/turn/call references,
call-id reuse with different content, unsupported model item types) is applied consistently and
is clearly an intentional design choice per the module doc comments, not an oversight.

Also read the three `rmcp-client` Streamable HTTP integration tests
(`streamable_http_remote.rs`, `streamable_http_test_support.rs`,
`streamable_http_user_agent.rs`). The remote-executor timeout test correctly asserts both that
the stalled handshake times out and that the shared exec-server executor is unblocked afterward;
the support module's server/exec-server readiness polling correctly distinguishes "not yet
bound" (`NotFound`) from real I/O errors and checks `try_wait()` for early child exit before
looping.

- `codex-rs/rollout/src/list.rs::AnchorState`/`should_skip`: `AnchorState` ignores the cursor's
  `id` tie-breaker entirely, so when the filesystem-fallback pagination boundary lands in the
  middle of a run of same-second-timestamp rollout files, entries with that exact timestamp that
  weren't returned in the prior page are skipped on all subsequent pages. This looked like a real
  pagination data-loss bug at first read, but it is deliberate and already covered by
  `codex-rs/rollout/src/tests.rs::test_timestamp_only_cursor_skips_same_second_filesystem_ties`,
  whose own comment states this is specific to the second-precision filename fallback path; the
  primary SQLite-backed listing uses millisecond timestamps and does not have this tie. Not a new
  finding.
- `codex-rs/rollout/src/compression.rs` (cold-file compression worker, `materialize_rollout_for_append_blocking`,
  writer-lock-guarded publish/remove, run-marker throttling, stale-temp cleanup): traced the full
  encode → verify (round-trip decode) → re-check-unchanged → publish → re-check-unchanged → remove
  pipeline, including the cross-device `hard_link` failure fallback to `persist_noclobber`
  (rename), and the permission/mtime preservation paths exercised by
  `compression_tests.rs::compression_preserves_read_only_rollout_permissions` and siblings. The
  re-checks around the writer-lock-guarded publication window correctly protect against a
  concurrent live writer invalidating the compressed copy; found no correctness or TOCTOU issue.
- `codex-rs/rollout/src/rollout_reference_index.rs`: verified that `RolloutId` is a type alias for
  `ThreadId` (`codex-rs/protocol/src/thread_id.rs`), so the cross-field comparisons
  (`history_base.thread_id == *rollout_id`, and similarly in `rollout_file_name.rs`) are not a
  type-confusion bug. Also verified the documented "first discovered wins" precedence for a
  rollout ID that exists in both `archived_sessions` and `sessions` (active wins because
  `scan_paths` visits the vec passed to it in LIFO order) is exactly what
  `rollout_reference_index_tests.rs::active_duplicate_wins_without_double_counting` exercises.
- `codex-rs/rollout-trace/src/reducer/tool/terminal.rs`, `tool_dispatch.rs`, `thread.rs`,
  `writer.rs`: reviewed the terminal-operation/session join-key reconciliation (process-id learned
  at begin vs. end, mismatch detection via `bail!`), the code-mode vs. protocol vs. dispatch
  response parsing fallback chain in `parse_terminal_response_payload`, the best-effort
  (log-and-continue) error handling used throughout the trace-recording hot path, and the
  code-mode dispatch-trace suppression (`suppresses_tool_dispatch_trace`, scoped precisely to the
  unnamespaced public code-mode tool). All consistent with the crate's stated "diagnostic-only,
  never blocks production" design, and the covered behaviors match their accompanying unit tests.

- `codex-rs/sandboxing/src/policy_transforms.rs` and its extensive `policy_transforms_tests.rs`: traced the additional-permission intersection/merge logic (`intersect_permission_profiles_with_context`, `granted_file_system_entry_within_request`, `retain_constraining_deny_entries`, glob materialization). The one path that looked suspicious at first read — `granted_file_system_entry_within_request`'s fallback comparison of unmaterialized `requested` entries against a materialized `granted_entry.path` for `FileSystemPath::GlobPattern` — is unreachable for anything that matters in practice: `normalize_additional_permissions` rejects any non-deny glob entry, and deny-access granted entries are already filtered out earlier in the same function by the `!granted_entry.access.can_read()` check. Even if that invariant were bypassed, the effect is fail-closed (the entry would be excluded), not a privilege escalation.
- `codex-rs/sandboxing/src/writer_lock.rs` (rollout crate) and `codex-rs/rollout/src/session_index.rs`: the cross-process writer-lock coordinator and the reverse-scan session index both correctly serialize the specific hazards they're designed for (stale lock cleanup is itself gated by the same coordination lock, so there's no TOCTOU window between `try_lock`/`drop`/`remove_file`; the session-index "first row wins" scan-from-end logic is exercised by tests covering renames and mixed valid/invalid rows).
- `codex-rs/sandboxing/src/seatbelt.rs`: the git-style glob-to-Seatbelt-regex translator (`seatbelt_regex_for_glob`) and the ancestor-rename protection scheme (denying `file-write-unlink` on protected ancestors, added after all broader allow rules) are backed by `seatbelt_tests.rs`, which actually executes `sandbox-exec` against the generated policies (including a rename-bypass regression test that walks every ancestor of a denied/glob-denied/read-only path). I read this logic closely for correctness but did not additionally execute the tests myself in this pass.
- `codex-rs/sandboxing/src/terminal_queries.rs`: the incremental terminal-query responder's state machine (partial-escape-sequence buffering across chunk boundaries, `MAX_QUERY_BYTES` bound, DEC private-mode fallback) correctly bounds memory and flushes any incomplete trailing sequence on stream close; traced by hand against `terminal_queries_tests.rs`'s split-chunk test.
- `codex-rs/rollout/src/state_db.rs`: `reconcile_rollout`/`read_repair_rollout_path`'s "never move a thread's selected rollout path except through the exact same path" invariant (guarding against `thread/revert` ambiguity) is consistent between the fast path and the slow (scan-and-reconcile) path, and matches its test coverage in `state_db_tests.rs`.

- `codex-rs/secrets/src/sanitizer.rs`: regex-based best-effort secret redaction (Bearer tokens, OpenAI `sk-` keys, AWS access key IDs, generic `key=value` assignments) with reasonable ordering (Bearer before OpenAI/AWS patterns) and matching unit tests including false-positive avoidance cases (Unicode look-alikes, short tokens). No correctness issues found for its stated "best effort" scope.
- `codex-rs/shell-command/src/bash.rs`: tree-sitter-based extraction of literal/plain commands from `bash`/`zsh -c`/`-lc` scripts. The allowlist-based rejection of dynamic constructs (expansions, globs, command/process substitution, escapes that change meaning) is thorough and each rejection path has a corresponding test; `parse_shell_lc_literal_commands` is explicitly documented as unsound for proving safety (only for spotting known-dangerous literals), which matches how it's consumed by `is_dangerous_command.rs`.
- `codex-rs/shell-command/src/command_safety/windows_dangerous_commands.rs` and `powershell_tree_sitter.rs`: the Windows/PowerShell/CMD dangerous-command heuristics (ShellExecute/URL launches, forced delete detection across CMD operator-splitting and PowerShell segmentation) and the tree-sitter-based literal PowerShell lowering (`powershell_tree_sitter.rs`) both fail closed aggressively (reject on any unrecognized node kind, Unicode syntax aliases, `#requires` directives, `using` statements, non-canonical numeric spellings) and are backed by an extensive fixture-driven test suite (`powershell_tree_sitter_tests.rs`, `fixtures/powershell_lowering.json`) plus a real-PowerShell-AST oracle test module (`powershell_parser.rs`, Windows-only tests) validating the fail-closed cases against the real parser.
- `codex-rs/shell-command/src/shell_detect.rs`: shell type/path detection, including the getpwuid_r-based (thread-safe) user shell lookup and the elevated-sandbox-compatible PowerShell path filtering (rejecting Store/WindowsApps-hosted `pwsh.exe`/`powershell.exe`), look correct and are covered by targeted unit tests.
- `codex-rs/shell-command/src/powershell.rs`: `extract_powershell_command` rejects unknown flags before `-Command`/`-c`, which is the correct fail-closed posture for treating a command as a recognized "plain" PowerShell invocation.
- `codex-rs/shell-escalation/src/unix/*` (protocol, client, server, socket, stopwatch, execve wrapper): the SCM_RIGHTS-based fd-transfer protocol, the dup2-based fd remapping in `pre_exec` (including the overlapping-descriptor regression test), environment scrubbing before exec (`env_clear()` + `scrub_non_inheritable_env_vars`), and session cancellation/cleanup (`Drop` aborting the task and killing spawned children) were traced through and are consistent with the documented protocol; cancellation paths still attempt to report a `SuperExecResult` after killing an escalated child, which is correct behavior for a clean shutdown.
- `codex-rs/shell-command/src/shell_snapshot*.rs` (capture, exports, literals, render) and `codex-rs/shell-command/src/shell_snapshot_credentials.rs`: this is intricate credential-scrubbing logic for shell-snapshot replay (deciding which captured exports/aliases are safe to replay verbatim vs. must be rewritten to reference brokered credentials vs. must be rejected). The code is heavily biased toward `return None`/`Export::Captured` fallbacks whenever virtualization round-trips don't match exactly, tied-array boundaries aren't fully understood, or a credential value could cross an array-element boundary — a reasonable fail-closed design for this specific risk (leaking real credentials into a persisted/replayed snapshot). Full independent verification of every branch of the credential-aliasing logic (`prepare_snapshot_credentials`) was not performed at this depth given its size and the absence of a targeted counter-example; flagging this as an area a deeper/dedicated pass should focus on if not already covered by the crate's extensive `shell_snapshot_tests.rs` suite.
- `codex-rs/skills/build.rs`: trivial `cargo:rerun-if-changed` emitter for the samples directory; no issues.

Note: `codex-rs/shell-command/src/parse_command.rs` is explicitly annotated in-source ("DO NOT REVIEW THIS CODE BY HAND... tests have been put directly below this function") as a lossy, display-only command summarizer (not a safety/security boundary), and was skimmed accordingly rather than reviewed line-by-line; no findings are reported against it.

- `codex-rs/skills/src/interface.rs` (`resolve_asset_path`, `resolve_plugin_shared_asset_path`,
  `lexically_normalize`): the asset-path resolver rejects absolute paths, rejects any path whose
  first normalized component isn't `assets` for the `LocalOnly` policy, and for `PluginShared`
  fully lexically normalizes the joined path before requiring it to stay under
  `plugin_root/assets` via component-wise `starts_with` (not a raw string prefix, so

- `codex-rs/skills/src/mentions.rs` (`extract_tool_mentions_with_sigil`,
  `parse_linked_tool_mention`): byte-index scanning only branches on ASCII markers (`$`, `[`, `]`,
  `(`, `)`, alnum/`_`/`-`/`:`, ASCII whitespace); since UTF-8 continuation bytes always have the
  high bit set they can never match these single-byte comparisons, so all `&text[..]` slices stay
  on valid UTF-8 boundaries even for multibyte input. Cross-checked against
  `handles_many_sigils_without_looping` and the plugin/app/mcp mention-kind filtering tests.

  directories.

- `migrate_rollouts_on_startup` and its helpers (`rollout_migration/startup.rs`): cursor lookback, busy-rollout retry via plain-basename matching across archive/compression moves, and the "empty rollout owned by a live writer counts as busy" handling are consistent with their corresponding tests (`retries_busy_rollouts_after_archive_and_compression_move`, `treats_writer_owned_empty_rollouts_as_busy`).
- `thread_history::apply_projection` and `materialize_to_sqlite` (`thread_history.rs`, `thread_history_materialization.rs`): the optimistic-concurrency guard (`expected_offset != start_offset` fails the transaction) correctly prevents a stale projection from silently overwriting the checkpoint, and malformed/duplicate/out-of-order rollout lines are skipped with a recorded anomaly rather than aborting the whole projection.
- `unarchive_thread`: file moves are tracked incrementally and rolled back (`restore_rollout_moves`) on any later failure (rename, timestamp touch, or SQLite update), so a partial unarchive does not leave rollout files inconsistent with SQLite state.
- `update_thread_metadata`/`apply_metadata_update`: the paginated-vs-legacy branches, the writer-lock acquisition conditions, and the best-effort-vs-blocking SQLite failure classification (`sqlite_write_failure_should_block`) match their stated rationale in the surrounding comments and are exercised by the corresponding tests.
- Attachment and section CRUD wrappers (`thread_attachments.rs`, `thread_sections.rs`) correctly gate on SQLite availability via `ThreadStoreError::Unsupported` and map domain errors (invalid request vs. thread-not-found vs. internal) based on message-prefix matching consistent with the underlying state-db error text.

**Coverage note:** `rollout_migration_tests.rs` (2693 lines) and `thread_history_materialization_tests.rs` (2739 lines) and `update_thread_metadata.rs` (2428 lines) exceeded this pass's single-read window; roughly the first 60% of each was read in full and the remainder was not opened. No findings above are contingent on the unread portions, but a defect confined to the untouched back halves of those three files would not have been caught here.

Reviewed all 30 files in this shard: the thread-store metadata-sync/section/type
definitions (`codex-rs/thread-store/src/thread_metadata_sync.rs`,
`thread_sections.rs`, `types.rs`) and the full `codex-rs/tools/src` surface
(code mode, dynamic tools, function-call errors, image-detail normalization,
the `json_schema` module including `compaction.rs`/`traversal.rs`/`types.rs`,
MCP tool parsing, plugin-install elicitation, response-history truncation,
Responses API tool conversion, `tool_call.rs`, `tool_config.rs`,
`tool_definition.rs`, plus every corresponding `*_tests.rs` file).

Specific areas verified beyond a read-through, with a rationale for why they
hold up:

- `ThreadMetadataSync`'s generation-based pending-update tracking
  (`merge_pending_update`, `take_pending_update`, `mark_pending_update_applied`)
  was traced step-by-step against the coalescing tests
  (`metadata_irrelevant_items_coalesce_updated_at_touches`,
  `resume_history_keeps_derived_metadata_pending_until_applied`). The
  generation counter correctly prevents a stale `mark_pending_update_applied`
  call from dropping metadata that arrived after the update it is
  acknowledging.
- `ThreadMetadataPatch`/`GitInfoPatch`'s `optional_option` serde adapter
  (`Option<Option<T>>` clearable-field encoding) was checked against
  `serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none", with =
  "optional_option")`: omitted fields correctly stay `None` (no-op), explicit
  `Some(None)` round-trips to a JSON `null` (clear), and `Some(Some(v))`
  round-trips to the bare value. Confirmed via the existing round-trip tests
  and by re-deriving the serde semantics by hand.
- `parse_session_timestamp`'s non-RFC3339 fallback format
  (`"%Y-%m-%dT%H-%M-%S"`) is not dead/wrong code; the same filename-safe
  timestamp convention is used consistently elsewhere in the codebase
  (`codex-rs/rollout/src/metadata.rs`, `codex-rs/memories/write/src/lib.rs`,
  `thread-store/src/local/rollout_migration/startup.rs`), so this is
  intentional legacy-format compatibility.
- `ThreadMetadataSync::for_create` passing an empty `PathBuf` (when
  `params.metadata.cwd` is `None`) into `get_git_repo_root` does not
  accidentally resolve to the process's actual cwd: verified with a standalone
  Rust snippet that `Path::new("").parent()` returns `None`, so
  `get_git_repo_root("")` short-circuits to `None` and no spurious git info is
  attached to a thread with no cwd.
- The JSON Schema sanitize/prune/compaction pipeline
  (`json_schema.rs`, `json_schema/compaction.rs`, `json_schema/traversal.rs`)
  was cross-checked against its extensive test suite covering `$ref`
  reachability (including percent-encoded pointers, cyclic refs, and
  malformed definition tables), the four-pass best-effort size-budget
  compaction, and `prefixItems`/`additionalProperties`/composition-keyword
  inference. Traversal order matches test expectations, and the
  `compact_normalized_schema_len` early-return-0-on-parse-error path cannot
  cause an oversized schema to silently pass, since `parse_tool_input_schema`
  performs the same deserialization at the end and would return the same
  error.
- `code_mode_name_for_tool_name`'s two special-cased separator rules
  (namespace ending in `_`, or tool name starting with `_`) can in principle
  produce identical code-mode names for two distinct `ToolName`s (e.g.
  namespace `"foo_"` + name `"bar"` vs. namespace `"foo"` + name `"_bar"`).
  This is not exploitable as a misrouting bug: the only caller that builds a
  name→`ToolName` map (`codex-rs/core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs`,
  `register_code_mode_executors`) inserts into a `BTreeMap` with
  `Entry::Vacant`/`Entry::Occupied` and logs+skips the second tool on
  collision rather than overwriting the first tool's target, and the
  namespaces actually constructed in the codebase for MCP tools
  (`ToolName::namespaced("memory", ...)`, `ToolName::namespaced("filesystem",
  ...)`, etc.) do not end in `_`, so the collision is currently only a latent
  possibility rather than a live one.
- `retain_tail_from_last_n_user_messages` and
  `truncate_assistant_output_text_to_token_budget` in `response_history.rs`
  were traced by hand against their tests (including the truncate-then-drain
  index arithmetic) and are correct.

- `codex-rs/tools/src/tool_spec.rs` and `tool_spec_tests.rs`: `create_tools_json_for_responses_lite`'s grouping of top-level `Function`/`Freeform`/default-namespace tools into a single `functions` namespace, insertion-index bookkeeping (`functions_index`), and description-preservation logic were traced by hand against the test fixtures (`responses_lite_groups_default_function_and_custom_tools`, `responses_lite_preserves_empty_functions_namespace_description`, `responses_lite_does_not_add_an_empty_functions_namespace`) and match.
- `codex-rs/tools/src/tool_search.rs` / `tool_search_tests.rs`: deferred-tool conversion (`ToolSearchInfo::from_spec`) correctly sets `defer_loading`/clears `output_schema` for function tools in all three source shapes (top-level function, top-level custom, namespace), and `ToolSpec::ToolSearch`/`WebSearch` are correctly excluded from being made searchable themselves.
- `codex-rs/tools/tests/json_schema_policy_fixtures.rs`: exercised against real captured connector schemas (Slack, Google Calendar/Drive, Notion, Outlook) plus an oversized golden fixture; assertions about `$defs`/description pruning and local-ref rewriting line up with `codex-rs/tools/src/json_schema/compaction.rs`, which I read to confirm the described compaction passes and the depth/byte-budget constants exist as claimed.

preserves the same bearer credential), and apparent test-only secrets (the
`"sk-test-key"` literal in `realtime_handoff_e2e.rs` is a fixture value fed to

**Note on review scope:**

`chat_composer.rs`'s `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block (lines ~5080–13083, roughly 230 `#[test]`
functions) is unusually large. I read it in large chunks and sampled broadly across submission,
slash-command, paste, footer, vim, and effort-animation test groups (and grepped for `#[ignore]`,
`TODO`, `FIXME`, and all `ParentOwnedInputBlocked`/`set_parent_owned_thread` occurrences), rather
than reading every one of the ~8000 lines verbatim. I'm confident in the finding above (confirmed
by exhaustive grep across the file), but a handful of narrowly-scoped snapshot/unit tests in that
module were not individually read line-by-line.

- `codex-rs/tui/src/bottom_pane/mcp_server_elicitation.rs`: server-supplied text used to build the
  elicitation/approval prompt (`message`, field `label`/`prompt`, option `label`, and
  `format_tool_approval_display_param_value`'s `Value::String` branch, which is not JSON-escaped
  like the non-string branch) is not explicitly sanitized before being placed into `ratatui`
  `Line`/`Span` content, unlike sibling paths elsewhere in the TUI crate that do sanitize
  user/tool-controlled text before display (`sanitize_user_text` for chat messages,
  `sanitize_terminal_title`, `sanitized_destination` for OSC‑8 hyperlink targets). I checked whether
  this allows a malicious/compromised MCP server to inject ANSI/control sequences into the approval
  UI and confirmed it does not: `ratatui-core`'s `Buffer::set_stringn` (the function `Line`/
  `Paragraph` rendering ultimately calls) filters out any grapheme cluster containing a control
  character (`ratatui-core-0.1.2/src/buffer/buffer.rs`, `.filter(|symbol| !symbol.contains(char::is_control))`)
  before it ever reaches a cell, so raw escape bytes from these fields cannot reach the terminal
  through this rendering path.
- `codex-rs/tui/src/bottom_pane/mentions_v2/filter.rs` and `codex-rs/tui/src/bottom_pane/multi_select_picker.rs`:
  both call into two different fuzzy-scoring systems with opposite "better" directions
  (`codex_utils_fuzzy_match::fuzzy_match`, where smaller is better, per its own doc comment and
  tests, vs. `codex_file_search::FileMatch.score`, a `nucleo`-derived score where larger is better).
  `filter.rs::compare_within_rank` and `multi_select_picker.rs::apply_filter` each sort in the
  direction appropriate to the scoring system in play (ascending for `fuzzy_match` results,
  descending for filesystem/`nucleo` results), so results are not actually inverted despite the
  mixed semantics.
- `codex-rs/tui/src/bottom_pane/custom_prompt_view.rs` and `feedback_note_view.rs` call
  `textarea.set_cursor(initial_text.len())` with a byte length. Verified against
  `TextArea::set_cursor` (`codex-rs/tui/src/bottom_pane/textarea.rs`), which treats the argument as
  a byte offset (`pos.clamp(0, self.text.len())`) and snaps it to the nearest char boundary, so this
  is correct even for multi-byte `initial_text` and does not panic or misplace the cursor.
- `codex-rs/tui/src/bottom_pane/feedback_view.rs`: the OpenAI-internal `go/codex-feedback-internal`

Two `PostToolUse` injection-scan hits on `selection_popup_common.rs`, `hyperlinks_tests.rs`, and `vim_commands_tests.rs` (all tagged `invisible-unicode`) were checked and are false positives: they are legitimate test fixtures exercising ZWJ emoji sequences, combining diacritics, and non-breaking Unicode whitespace, not injected instructions.

All 30 files listed in `shard-141-codex-rs-part137-files.txt` were read in full (no truncation), including the two large files in the set, `codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget.rs` (2104 lines) and `codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/input_restore.rs` (610 lines). This shard is TUI (`codex-rs/tui`) chat-widget plumbing: `ChatWidget` construction, key routing, input queueing/restore/submission, exec-command lifecycle, hook/goal/IDE-context status, backend/Reserve-model banner state, connector caching, and a handful of `bottom_pane` views (title setup, user-verification prompt, voice strip, unified-exec footer) plus their snapshot/unit tests.

No critical, high, medium, or low-severity defects were identified with a reproducible basis. Areas specifically scrutinized:

- **`branch_summary.rs`** — all `git`/`gh` invocations build argv vectors passed directly to `WorkspaceCommandExecutor::run` (not through a shell), so remote names, branch names, and repo slugs pulled from `git remote`/`gh repo view` output cannot be used for command injection even though they are untrusted-ish (repo-local) strings. `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` / `GH_PROMPT_DISABLED=1` / `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` are set as documented to keep these best-effort background probes non-interactive and non-mutating. The default-branch resolution order (remote-tracking HEAD → `git remote show` fallback → local `main`/`master`) verifies each candidate ref exists before using it, avoiding a merge-base call against a dangling ref.
- **`chatwidget/connectors.rs`** — `on_connectors_loaded` itself does not re-check `ConnectorScopeGeneration`, which looked at first like a stale-response bug (contrast with `on_connector_mentions_loaded`, which does check). Traced the call site in `codex-rs/tui/src/app/event_dispatch.rs` (`AppEvent::ConnectorsLoaded` handler) and confirmed the generation (plus thread id and cwd) is validated *before* `on_connectors_loaded` is invoked, and the outbound `AppEvent::FetchConnectorsList` is also gated on generation before the app-server RPC is even issued. So a scope invalidation (account/workspace/thread switch) correctly drops in-flight responses; this is not a bug.
- **`chatwidget/backend_banners.rs`** — the Luna Reserve fallback/return-model state machine (`backend_banner_fallback`, `finish_backend_banner_fallback`, `apply_reserve_fallback_to_pending_turn`, `refresh_backend_banner_visibility`) was traced end-to-end for the save-before-switch / restore-after-recovery invariant described in the module doc comment; the `replaced_model` bookkeeping and account-id checks are internally consistent.
- **`bottom_pane/voice_strip.rs`** — `append_voice_history`'s slice arithmetic (`samples[samples.len().saturating_sub(meter_width)..]` followed by `repeat_n(0, meter_width - samples.len())`) is safe from underflow: the truncated slice length is always `<= meter_width` by construction. Narrow-width control/label truncation logic was checked against `voice_strip_tests.rs` and is exercised at widths down to 22 columns.
- **`chatwidget/exec_state.rs` / `chatwidget/command_lifecycle.rs`** — unified-exec process tracking (begin/end/output-chunk bookkeeping, `MAX_RECENT_CHUNKS` trimming) and the exec-cell end-target dispatch (`ExecEndTarget::{ActiveTracked, OrphanHistoryWhileActiveExec, NewCell}`) were checked for the specific case the code comments call out (an unmatched end for a call that isn't the active tracked cell); the suppression path for duplicate unified-exec "wait" interactions correctly avoids inserting into `running_commands` and is symmetrically cleaned up in `handle_command_execution_completed_now` via `suppressed_exec_calls`.
- **`chatwidget/interrupts.rs`** — `InterruptManager::remove_resolved_prompt` / `matches_resolved_prompt` id-matching per request kind, cross-checked against its own unit tests (exec approval id vs. call id, lifecycle events never matching).
- **`chatwidget/input_queue.rs` / `input_restore.rs` / `input_submission.rs`** — the queued-message / pending-steer / rejected-steer restore-on-interrupt and merge-on-drain paths are intricate (byte-offset renumbering of paste placeholders and mention text elements across merged messages) but internally consistent with the invariants documented in the module comments; no arithmetic that isn't `saturating_*`-guarded.
- **`bottom_pane/textarea/wrapping_tests.rs`, `bottom_pane/title_setup.rs`, `bottom_pane/unified_exec_footer.rs`, `bottom_pane/user_verification.rs(+tests)`** — reviewed for correctness/edge cases (empty state, narrow widths, legacy id parsing in `TerminalTitleItem::FromStr`, all-or-nothing parsing semantics in `parse_terminal_title_items`); no issues found.

Nothing in this shard was only partially reviewed.

- `codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/luna_reserve_return.rs`: `load` bounds the read via `file.take(4096)` before deserializing, so a corrupt or maliciously large cache file cannot cause unbounded memory use; `save` writes through `tempfile::NamedTempFile` + `sync_all` + `persist`, which is a correct atomic-write pattern for the per-thread JSON cache.
- `codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/mcp_startup.rs`: the buffered "ignore updates until next round" / pending-round promotion state machine in `update_mcp_startup_status` was traced through its branches (post-finish stale-update suppression, `Starting`-reset-on-buffer, full-round detection, terminal-only promotion via `finish_mcp_startup_after_lag`) and is internally consistent.
- `codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/misalignment_policy.rs`: traced `clear_misalignment_for_new_turn`'s interaction with both call sites — the explicit "Acknowledge findings and continue" flow (`codex-rs/tui/src/app/misalignment_policy.rs::continue_misalignment`, which calls it directly with `MisalignmentTurnSource::AcknowledgedContinuation` before replaying `TurnStarted`) and the ordinary per-notification path in `protocol.rs` (`MisalignmentTurnSource::ServerNotification`). The apparent gap — an unrelated `TurnStarted` for a different `turn_id` silently clearing an unacknowledged block when `retired_voice` is false — is bounded by `rejects_misalignment_policy_op`, which blocks essentially every `AppCommand` capable of starting a new turn through the ordinary op-submission path while a violation is active; the only route that can produce a differently-ID'd `TurnStarted` for the blocked thread is either the explicit acknowledge RPC (which sets the correct source itself) or a turn started by another authorized client/session against the same thread, in which case clearing the stale local block is appropriate. The safety boundary itself (rejecting the unsafe action) is enforced server-side, not by this client-side composer-disable state.
- `codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/realtime.rs`, `realtime/recording_controls.rs`, `realtime_split_flap.rs`: the typed-vs-voice turn-origin/generation bookkeeping (`RealtimeTurnOrigin`, `RealtimeAgentItemOrigin`, `input_generation` invalidation on typed input, `speaker_suppression_generation`) and the private-reasoning/commentary redaction (`is_private_realtime_agent_item`) were read against the corresponding test suites (`realtime_tests/handoff_privacy.rs`, `realtime_tests/caption_replay.rs`, `recording_controls_tests.rs`, `realtime_split_flap_tests.rs`), which specifically exercise the races this code defends against (stale voice steering a newer typed turn, typed input started mid-voice-answer, replay ordering, caption/answer de-duplication on close). The `flap_sample` construction in `realtime_split_flap.rs` (empty when the visible transcript has no flippable glyphs) cannot reach the `sample[offset % sample.len()]` modulo in `flap_glyph`, because `flap_glyph` is only invoked for graphemes that `is_flippable` accepts, and `visible_target`/`flap_sample` are derived from exactly the same predicate over the same rendered text — so a would-be divide/modulo-by-zero panic is structurally unreachable.
- `codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/plugin_catalog.rs`: `merge_remote_marketplaces`'s retain predicate (`marketplace.path.is_some() || !A && !B`) parses per normal Rust operator precedence (`&&` binds tighter than `||`) to the intended "keep local marketplaces, plus remote entries not superseded by the new remote fetch," not a precedence bug.

- `codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/reasoning_shortcuts.rs` — `next_reasoning_effort`'s
  bounds handling (`checked_sub`, `choices.get(index + 1)`) correctly returns

No findings to report for this shard.

Reviewed all 30 files in this shard, which together comprise the `codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/tests` suite covering bedrock/collaboration model catalogs, compaction status, completion-timestamp formatting, computer-activity (CUA) tool-call rendering, composer submission (image/mention/placeholder remapping, startup-draft handoff, hidden shell-paste literal-prompt handling), config-error snapshots, exec flow (approvals, unified-exec, patch application, orphaned exec-end handling), goal menus/validation, Guardian auto-review assessment and denial-approval flows, shared test helpers/fixtures, history replay (session resume, reasoning replay, MCP tool-call replay, dedup of live-vs-replayed reasoning summaries), Luna Reserve usage banner, MCP server startup sequencing (including post-lag settling and stale-round discarding), misalignment-policy precaution/review flows, permission-shortcut cycling and profile-selection popups (including Windows sandbox prompts), plan mode (reasoning-scope prompts, plan-implementation popup gating), plugin catalog popups, async question editing (vim bindings, history search, digit/letter shortcuts), rate-limit recovery queuing, reasoning-status header tracking, replay-render snapshot determinism, review-mode steer/interrupt queuing, side-conversation restrictions, slash-command dispatch (including queued-command draining across turn boundaries and service-tier persistence), and status/layout rendering (rate-limit warning thresholds, goal status indicator formatting, hook lifecycle rendering, ambient pets, status-line/terminal-title cost and credit fetch dedup).

The three largest files in the shard — `popups_and_settings.rs` (4304 lines), `slash_commands.rs` (3801 lines), and `status_and_layout.rs` (5784 lines) — were reviewed via full enumeration of every top-level `fn`/`async fn` (test and helper) plus representative full reads of the most logic-heavy sections (byte-offset placeholder remapping, rate-limit percentage-threshold warnings, multi-agent Ultra-reasoning concurrency threshold, goal status/budget formatting); the remaining individual test bodies in those three files were not read line-by-line given their size, but no anomalies turned up in the sampled sections, and the code follows the same consistent, careful patterns (explicit byte-range assertions, `TryRecvError` exhaustiveness checks, boundary-value test pairs such as 7 vs. 8 threads) seen throughout the fully-read files.

No correctness bugs, no flaky non-deterministic assertions (the one wall-clock-dependent test, `completion_live_applies_duration_threshold_and_preserves_timestamp_fallback` in `completion_styling_tests.rs`, explicitly brackets `Local::now()` calls before/after the action and accepts either formatted minute to avoid a minute-boundary race), no hardcoded credentials or secrets (matches for "secret"/"token"/"key" are all test fixture data such as glob-deny patterns or `is_secret: false` fields, not real credentials), and no unsafe/misleading test assertions were found. `grep` across all 30 files for `sleep`/`TODO`/`FIXME`/`#[ignore]` turned up only legitimate uses (test fixture command strings like `"sleep 5"`, and one real `std::thread::sleep` in `slash_commands.rs` that sleeps for the production `recommended_paste_flush_delay()` value to deterministically exercise paste-burst debounce behavior, which is appropriate rather than a magic-number sleep).

- **`codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/thread_usage.rs` + `thread_usage_tests.rs`**: the
  request-id correlation, bounded retry/settlement backoff (`THREAD_USAGE_RETRY_DELAYS`,
  `THREAD_USAGE_SETTLEMENT_DELAYS`), and the "transient zero" masking for credits/USD
  estimates are all exercised by a thorough set of async tests (bounded retries, settlement
  requiring a request started after turn completion, deselecting billing surfaces cancels
  polling, etc.). The masking behavior looked suspicious in isolation (it never lets a
  legitimate drop-to-zero through), but thread usage is a monotonically non-decreasing
  running total for a thread, so treating an isolated `0` response as backend eventual-
  consistency lag rather than a real value is consistent with the documented intent and is
  covered by dedicated tests (`transient_zero_cost_preserves_fresh_credits_and_breakdowns`,
  `transient_zero_credits_preserves_credits_only_estimates`).
- **`codex-rs/tui/src/clipboard_html.rs` + `clipboard_html_tests.rs`**: raw `Event::Html`/
  `Event::InlineHtml` nodes are converted to `Event::Text` (so `pulldown_cmark::html::push_html`
  HTML-escapes them), image tags are dropped so pasting cannot trigger remote image
  requests, and non-web link destinations (`javascript:`, `data:`, HTML-entity-obfuscated
  schemes) are rejected as real `<a href>` targets and instead rendered as escaped visible
  text. Verified by reading `terminal_hyperlinks::web_destination`'s call sites and the
  `markdown_clipboard_escapes_raw_html_and_rejects_unsafe_destinations` /
  `markdown_clipboard_images_are_inert` tests, which assert exactly this behavior.
- **`codex-rs/tui/src/clipboard_copy.rs`**: the SSH → tmux → OSC 52, and local →
  native/arboard → WSL PowerShell → terminal fallback chains are each covered by
  dedicated unit tests with injected backends (`copy_to_clipboard_with`), including
  multi-stage failure message composition. OSC 52 payload size is bounded
  (`OSC52_MAX_RAW_BYTES`) before base64 encoding.
- **`codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/tokens/chart.rs` + `chart_tests.rs`**: bucket
  aggregation clamps negative token values and sums duplicate dates
  (`daily_values`), and the width-driven column/graph-width math
  (`shown_columns`, `graph_width`, `month_labels`) was checked for
  underflow at the zero-column boundary; `chart_lines` returns early before
  `month_labels` is reached whenever `shown_columns == 0`, so the
  `shown_columns * 2 - 1` subtraction in `month_labels` never executes with
  `shown_columns == 0`.
- **`codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/user_messages.rs`**: placeholder remapping and byte-range
  rebasing (`remap_placeholders_in_text`, `append_text_with_rebased_elements`,
  `user_message_display_from_parts`) consistently use `str::get` with clamped
  ranges rather than direct indexing, so malformed/overlapping `TextElement` ranges
  degrade gracefully instead of panicking.
- **`codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/worktree_picker.rs`**: stale-response handling in
  `on_managed_worktrees_loaded` / `worktree_request_is_current` (request id, cwd, and
  thread id must all match) was traced against `worktree_browser_actions_and_stale_results`,
  which specifically exercises a stale result arriving after a newer request superseded it.

- `codex-rs/tui/src/debug_config.rs`: `format_network_constraints` / `render_debug_config_lines` only surface header-injection **hosts** and counts, never the actual header names/values from `NetworkHeaderInjectionToml.headers`. The test `debug_config_output_lists_requirement_sources` plants a header value literally named `"secret-looking-value"` and asserts the rendered `/debug-config` output never contains it — confirming the redaction is deliberate and tested, not accidental.
- `codex-rs/tui/src/config_update.rs`: the `-32601 || -32600 && message.contains(...)` guard in `read_effective_config_if_supported` looks suspicious at a glance, but Rust's `&&`/`||` precedence makes it `code == -32601 || (code == -32600 && message-conditions)`, which matches the intent described in the surrounding comment (treat "method not found" alone as sufficient, but require message-sniffing for the more generic "invalid request" code). Not a bug.
- `codex-rs/tui/src/dynamic_tools.rs`: `delegated_prompt`/`parse_delegated_prompt` (the `<codex_delegation>` wrapper used to embed one thread's prompt/output inside another's) escape `&`, `<`, `>` on write and unescape in the safe `&lt;`/`&gt;`/`&amp;` order (amp last) on read, so a prompt that contains the literal delimiter text (e.g. `</input>`) cannot break out of the wrapper and forge a fake `source_thread_id`/`input` boundary. Verified by tracing an example with an embedded literal `"&lt;"` through both directions, and cross-checked against the `delegated_prompts_match_desktop_xml_contract` test.
- `codex-rs/tui/src/custom_terminal.rs` and `custom_terminal/cursor.rs`: `diff_buffers`, `draw`, and `set_cursor_style_with_repair` are intricate (wide-glyph/hyperlink/forced-width handling) but are exercised by an extensive, specific unit-test suite (wide-char clear-to-end boundaries, hyperlink coalescing, forced-width trailing-cell clearing, cursor-style repair with no owned glyph, etc.); no gaps were found between the documented invariants and the implementation.
- `codex-rs/tui/src/exec_cell/live_output.rs`: the bounded live-output buffer (byte budget, head/tail retention, split-CRLF handling, ANSI-sequence-safe truncation marker) was traced by hand for boundary conditions (multi-byte UTF-8 at the truncation boundary, CRLF split across `push_str` calls, unterminated OSC/CSI sequences at the truncation point) and matches its test coverage in `live_output_tests.rs`.

**Not fully reviewed:**

`codex-rs/tui/src/diff_render.rs` is 2560 lines; the non-test logic (lines 1–~950) and the file's tail were read in full, but roughly lines 1849–2399 (all within the `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block, snapshot/wrap tests) were skimmed rather than read line-by-line. Based on the surrounding code this region is homogeneous test scaffolding (more `ui_snapshot_*`/wrap-behavior tests), so the risk of a missed production-code defect there is low, but it is flagged for completeness.

- `codex-rs/tui/src/external_editor.rs` (`editor_directory`, `run_editor`) — the logic that picks an
  editor-buffer directory outside the sandbox's writable roots (so a sandboxed exec subprocess can't
  tamper with or read a buffer the user is editing) is exercised by an extensive set of tests in
  `external_editor_tests.rs` covering symlinked homes, symlinked aliases pointing at the protected
  home, writable-descendant carve-outs, Windows `TEMP`/`TMP` handling, and workspace-fallback
  metadata directories. I traced the writability predicate
  (`can_write_local_path_with_cwd`/`writable_roots` checks) against each test scenario and the logic
  matches (aside from the low-severity error-message issue reported above).
- `codex-rs/tui/src/get_git_diff.rs` — `/diff` generation explicitly disables Git hooks
  (`core.hooksPath=/dev/null`/`NUL`), disables textconv/ext-diff, and neutralizes configured
  `filter.*.clean`/`.process` drivers via `GIT_CONFIG_*` env overrides before running any diff
  command, and always separates paths with `--` to avoid option injection from attacker-named
  untracked files. This is backed by unix integration tests
  (`get_git_diff_does_not_execute_configured_filters_fsmonitor_or_hooks`,
  `get_git_diff_does_not_execute_helpers_while_checking_dirty_submodules`) that actually run `git`
  against a scratch repo and assert the helper scripts never ran.
- `codex-rs/tui/src/history_cell/mcp_result.rs` (`decode_mcp_image`) — fully decodes MCP-supplied
  image content to validate it, which could look like an unbounded decompression-bomb risk from a
  malicious/compromised MCP server. I checked the vendored `image` crate (`0.25.9`) source
  (`src/io/limits.rs`, `src/io/image_reader_type.rs`): `ImageReader::new` applies
  `Limits::default()`, which caps decoder allocation at 512 MiB, so a single decode cannot exhaust
  memory unboundedly under the default configuration used here.
- `codex-rs/tui/src/history_cell/messages.rs` (`sanitize_user_text`) — strips ANSI/CSI escape
  sequences and other control characters from pasted/typed user text before it reaches the terminal.
  Verified that every code path unconditionally removes the raw `ESC` (`\x1b`) byte itself (not just
  well-formed `ESC[...`  CSI sequences), which is the byte required to trigger terminal escape-code
  interpretation; non-CSI escape types (OSC, DCS, etc.) are left as inert, visible residual text
  rather than being fully parsed out, which matches the function's documented contract and its
  dedicated test suite in `messages_tests.rs` — not an escape-injection bypass.

Files opened: 30 (all files listed in
`.moe/review-shards/shard-147-codex-rs-part143-files.txt`). All were read in full; none were large
enough to require partial reading.

- `codex-rs/tui/src/ide_context/ipc.rs` and `codex-rs/tui/src/ide_context/windows_pipe.rs`: the Unix and Windows IDE-context IPC transports both validate the peer's identity *after* connecting (`SO_PEERCRED`/`getpeereid` on Unix, `GetNamedPipeServerProcessId` + token SID comparison on Windows) rather than relying solely on a pre-connect path/metadata check, which closes the obvious TOCTOU window; the Unix path also checks that the socket's parent directory is owned by the current user and not group/world-writable, enforces `O_NONBLOCK`/`FD_CLOEXEC`, and bounds every read behind a caller-supplied deadline. The Windows named-pipe client opens with `SECURITY_SQOS_PRESENT | SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION`, which caps the server's ability to impersonate the client at the "identification" level; `windows_pipe_tests.rs::pipe_server_cannot_impersonate_client` exercises this against a real pipe server and asserts the impersonation level stays at `SecurityIdentification`.
- `codex-rs/tui/src/inline_visualization.rs` and `codex-rs/tui/src/inline_visualization/viewer.rs`: file-path resolution for `::codex-inline-vis{file="..."}` / content-reference directives requires the resolved path to canonicalize inside the thread's own `visualizations/<date>/<thread-id>` directory (rejecting `../` traversal and symlink escapes via `fs::canonicalize` + `starts_with`), restricts to a single path component with a `.html` extension, and caps fragment size at `MAX_FRAGMENT_BYTES` (2 MiB). The materialized viewer is written atomically via `tempfile::NamedTempFile::new_in` + `persist`, and the viewer directory is verified to contain no symlinks before use. The rendered HTML nests the fragment in a `sandbox="allow-scripts"` iframe (no `allow-same-origin`) with a CSP whose `connect-src` is restricted to `blob:`/`data:` (excluding the CDN origins allowed in `script-src`/`img-src`/`font-src`), limiting exfiltration even if the visualized fragment contains attacker-influenced markup. `inline_visualization_tests.rs` exercises the traversal rejection (`../chart.html`), extension rejection (`chart.svg`), oversized-fragment rejection, and the sandbox/CSP attributes directly.
- `codex-rs/tui/src/history_cell/request_user_input.rs`: secret answers are rendered as a fixed-width `"••••••"` placeholder regardless of the actual answer length, avoiding a length side-channel in the transcript.

- `codex-rs/user-verification/*` (error.rs, guard.rs + tests, key_namespace.rs + tests, lib.rs, lifecycle_lock.rs + tests, native_operation.rs + tests, platform_macos.rs, platform_macos/error.rs + tests, platform_macos/key_protection.rs + tests, platform_macos/provider.rs, unsupported.rs): the cancellation/guard design (`UserVerificationRequestGuard`), the cross-process file lock (`LifecycleLock`, using `File::try_lock` with a bounded poll loop), and the owner-thread-confined native operation runner (`run_with_cancellation`, which explicitly joins the worker thread and converts a panicking worker into a graceful `UserVerificationError` rather than letting `thread::scope` re-panic) are all internally consistent with their tests, which exercise real file-lock contention and real thread cancellation rather than mocks. The keychain label derivation (`UserVerificationKeyNamespace::new`) uses SHA-256 + URL-safe base64 so raw account identifiers never appear in a keychain label, confirmed by `namespaces_are_stable_and_separate_accounts`. `key_protection::validate` intentionally does not re-verify the `SecAccessControl` policy on key reuse (only token ID, key class, key type, and key size), relying on keychain-access-group enforcement to keep foreign processes from planting a matching-labeled Secure Enclave key without the biometric access-control flags; the code explicitly documents this trust boundary in a comment, so it reads as a considered tradeoff rather than an oversight.
  - Note: `codex-rs/user-verification/src/credential.rs`, referenced by `mod credential;` in `lib.rs` and used throughout `provider.rs` (`UserVerificationKeyInfo`, `UserVerificationRequest`, etc.), is not part of this shard's file list and was not reviewed here.
