- `codex-rs/utils/cli/src/config_override.rs`, `format_env_display.rs`, `resume_command.rs`, `sandbox_mode_cli_arg.rs`, `approval_mode_cli_arg.rs`, `lib.rs`: `format_env_display` masks all values (map values and bare var names alike) as `*****`, never printing secrets; `resume_command` shell-escapes the resume target via `shlex_join` and prefixes `--` for names starting with `-`, avoiding option-injection when the printed command is copy-pasted.
- `codex-rs/utils/cargo-bin/src/lib.rs`: env-var and Bazel-runfile resolution paths look correct for their stated purpose (test-only binary/resource lookup).

`codex-rs/utils/path-uri/src/lib.rs`, `absolute_path_normalization.rs`, `api_path_string.rs`, `native_path_bytes.rs`, and their accompanying test files (`tests.rs`, `api_path_string_tests.rs`) implement a large, carefully documented `file:` URI abstraction with explicit handling for Windows/POSIX convention inference, UNC/drive roots, opaque (base64) fallbacks for unrepresentable native paths, percent-encoding round-tripping, and lexical containment (`starts_with`/`join_descendant`) used for sandbox-style path checks. I specifically looked for a percent-encoding double-decode path-traversal bypass in `join`/`join_descendant`/`join_native_bytes` (e.g. a literal `%2e%2e` path component being reinterpreted as `..` after storage) and confirmed that `url::Url`'s path-segment push percent-encodes a literal `%` character (verified against the `join_normalizes_relative_uri_segments` test, where pushing `c%d` yields the URI segment `c%25d`), so a literal `%2e%2e` component cannot decode to `..` after a single decode pass; combined with the extensive `RENDER_CASES` table and dedicated tests for double-encoded separators, this closes the traversal-bypass class I was checking for. I did not find a counterexample.

`codex-rs/utils/path-utils/src/system_commands.rs` (trusted-executable discovery that deliberately avoids PATH/PATHEXT/cwd) correctly rejects a `name` argument containing a path separator, uses `dunce::canonicalize` (which resolves symlinks) before checking containment under trusted installation roots, and the accompanying test confirms a symlink pointing outside the trusted directory is rejected. The threat model is explicitly documented as trusting the installation directories themselves, which is a reasonable, stated assumption.

`codex-rs/utils/image/src/lib.rs` (`prompt_image_output_dimensions_for_limits` and the resize/re-encode pipeline) was checked against its own test cases (`HIGH_DETAIL`/`ORIGINAL_DETAIL` budget math) by hand-computing the expected scale factors, and the ICC-profile RGB-only filter (bytes 16..20 must equal `b"RGB "`) correctly prevents mislabeling a CMYK/YCCK-derived profile as RGB after JPEG decode-to-RGB, matching the `resizing_drops_non_rgb_icc_profile` test.

- `codex-rs/utils/pty/src/process.rs` and `codex-rs/utils/pty/src/pipe.rs`: the `ChildTerminator`/`ProcessHandle` lifecycle (`request_terminate`, `signal`, `terminate`, `Drop`) correctly uses `Option::take()` on the mutex-guarded killer so a terminator can only fire once even when both an explicit `signal(Interrupt)` (which self-clears on Windows after a successful call) and a later `Drop`/`terminate()` occur; verified against `driver_backed_interrupt_terminates_once` and the reaping tests in `tests.rs`.
- `codex-rs/utils/pty/src/process_group.rs` and `process_group_tests.rs`: Unix process-group signal helpers (`kill_process_group`, `terminate_process_group`, the macOS EPERM member-fallback path) correctly special-case `ESRCH`/`NotFound` as "already gone" rather than an error, and reject unsafe process-group IDs (0, `u32::MAX`) before signaling; the macOS fallback's PGID re-validation per member (via `getpgid`) avoids signaling processes that have since been reused into a different group.
- `codex-rs/utils/pty/src/unix_io.rs`: the non-blocking PTY I/O driver's EOF-on-stdin-close handling (sending `\n` + the terminal's live `VEOF` character) and its handling of `EWOULDBLOCK`/`EINTR` via `AsyncFd` match the documented behavior and are covered by `pty_close_stdin_preserves_large_input_and_delivers_eof`.
- `codex-rs/utils/pty/src/win/job.rs` and `win/mod.rs`: Windows Job Object containment (`assign_process`, `spawn_contained`, `preserve_descendants`/`terminate` racing safely via a shared mutex) is internally consistent, and the documented small race window between `spawn()` and `assign_process()` is called out explicitly in `pipe.rs` rather than silently ignored.
- `codex-rs/utils/pty/src/pty.rs` `close_inherited_fds_except` (both the macOS `proc_pidinfo`-based implementation and the generic `/dev/fd`-scanning implementation for other Unix targets): correctly preserves CLOEXEC descriptors (needed for `std::process`'s internal exec-error pipe) and explicitly-preserved fds, and both implementations have layered fallbacks that were reasoned through without finding a logic error.
- `codex-rs/utils/sandbox-summary/src/sandbox_summary.rs`: `summarize_sandbox_policy` and `summarize_permission_profile` string formatting matches all of its accompanying unit tests, including the `workspace_roots`-vs-`cwd` de-duplication behavior.
- `codex-rs/utils/sleep-inhibitor/*`: the macOS IOKit assertion wrapper (create/release exactly once via `Drop`), the Linux `systemd-inhibit`/`gnome-session-inhibit` fallback-and-restart logic (including PDEATHSIG arming and treating `InvalidInput` from `kill`/`wait` as "already exited"), and the no-op dummy backend all look correct for their stated purpose.
- `codex-rs/utils/rustls-provider/src/lib.rs`: `ensure_rustls_crypto_provider`'s "install once, otherwise preserve a pre-installed provider" behavior matches both `tests/preinstalled.rs` and `tests/provider.rs`.
- `codex-rs/utils/pty/src/windows_input.rs`: `WindowsTtyInputNormalizer::normalize`'s CRLF-collapsing state machine was traced by hand across several byte sequences (`\r\n`, `\n\n`, `\r\r`, a CRLF split across two writes) and produces the intended single-Enter-per-newline output in each case; matches `windows_input_tests.rs`.

**`codex-rs/utils/stream-parser/*`** — `InlineHiddenTagParser`, `CitationStreamParser`, `TaggedLineParser`/`ProposedPlanParser`, and `Utf8StreamParser` all correctly buffer partial delimiters/code points across chunk boundaries, auto-close unterminated tags at `finish()`, and (per `Utf8StreamParser::push_bytes`) roll back the entire pushed chunk on invalid UTF-8 rather than leaking a partial valid prefix to the inner parser — this rollback-on-error behavior is deliberate and is asserted by `utf8_stream_parser_rolls_back_entire_chunk_when_invalid_byte_follows_valid_prefix`. Verified `InlineHiddenTagParser::find_next_open`'s tie-break (`generic_inline_parser_prefers_longest_opener_at_same_offset`) and `TaggedLineParser`'s line-buffering/prefix-detection logic (including CRLF handling, since Rust's `str::trim_end()` strips `\r`) by hand-tracing several inputs against the existing tests.

**`codex-rs/utils/string/src/truncate.rs`** — `split_string`'s prefix/suffix byte-budget walk only advances `prefix_end`/`suffix_start` on `char_boundary`-aligned offsets (via `char_indices`), so it cannot produce a non-UTF-8-boundary slice even for multi-byte/emoji input; traced the 4-byte-emoji test cases (`split_string_respects_utf8_boundaries`) by hand and they match. `sanitize_metric_tag_value` replaces every non-`[A-Za-z0-9._/-]` character (including all non-ASCII multi-byte characters) with `_` before doing a byte-index truncation to `MAX_LEN`, so the later `trimmed[..MAX_LEN]` slice is always ASCII and cannot panic on a char boundary.

**`codex-rs/utils/string/src/json.rs`** — `AsciiJsonFormatter::write_string_fragment` only receives fragments serde_json has already excluded control characters/quote/backslash from (those go through the default `write_char_escape`), so its ASCII/non-ASCII split cannot double-escape or mis-handle a control character. Verified surrogate-pair encoding for non-BMP characters (🚀 → `🚀`) via `char::encode_utf16`.

**`codex-rs/utils/template/src/lib.rs`** — `Template::parse`/`render` correctly track literal vs. placeholder segments, escape `{{{{`/`}}}}`, and reject nested/empty/unterminated placeholders and duplicate/extra/missing render values; traced several inputs against the paired tests.

**`codex-rs/voice-host/*` epoch/generation invalidation** — `Buffers::set_disabled`, `CaptureBoundary::accepts`, `FramePacker::push`/`discard_capture_gap`, `Playback::next`, `Incoming::{set_suppressed,take}`, and `Ingress::handle_read` all use the same odd-epoch-means-disabled / generation-must-match convention consistently, and each snapshots the epoch/generation once per call so a concurrent mute/unmute cannot produce a torn read within a single invocation. The `CaptureWorker::set_controls` ordering (speaker first, then microphone, with the microphone-reset gated on `previous != current`) is deliberate and explicitly exercised by `combined_mute_and_suppression_cancel_old_speaker_and_capture_work`, which proves a failed speaker-epoch transition does not touch microphone state.

**`codex-rs/voice-host/src/incoming.rs`** — permanently failing the incoming-audio pipe (`state.failed = true`) on any oversized packet, wrong payload type, SSRC change, or permit exhaustion is deliberate fail-closed behavior, explicitly asserted by `consumed_packets_keep_their_budget_until_the_last_owner_drops_them` and `invalid_stream_and_oversize_packets_fail_without_returning_media`; this is a documented design choice (matching the same fail-closed pattern used throughout `device_buffers.rs`/`devices.rs`/`playback.rs`), not an oversight.

**`codex-rs/voice-host/src/main.rs`** — the control-message state machine's per-variant guards (`devices.is_none() && ...`, `transport.is_none()`, `!answered`) all fall through to the exhaustive catch-all arm that lists every `Message` variant and returns `"invalid voice control sequence"` on a guard mismatch, so no message variant can silently no-op. The stdin-reader thread's 2-second-sleep-then-`exit(1)` watchdog only matters if the main thread is still running when stdin reaches EOF (Rust terminates all threads immediately when `main()` returns), which matches the intent described in the file's module doc comment and is exercised by `parent_pipe_loss_terminates_helper_with_blocked_transport_startup`.

**Casts and arithmetic** — grepped this shard for `.unwrap()`/`.expect()`/`panic!`/`unreachable!` and all `as u32`/`as u16`/`as i32`/`as usize` casts outside test modules; the sole non-test `.unwrap()` is `codex-rs/utils/string/src/lib.rs`'s `find_uuids` regex compile, which is over a fixed literal pattern (compile-time constant) and is comment-flagged as relying on the test suite to keep it valid. All numeric casts (`frame.len as u32`, `size as u32` in `incoming.rs`, `(BLOCK * QUEUE_CAPACITY) as u32`, etc.) operate on values already bounded well below the target type's range by an earlier check (e.g. `size > PACKET_BYTES` gates `size as u32` in `Ingress::handle_read`), so none can silently wrap in a way that changes behavior.

  `unmute_reset_rejects_delayed_pre_unmute_audio_and_partial_history`,

**Notes on coverage:**

All 30 files listed in the shard manifest were read in full; none were large
enough to require partial reading. No credential-bearing files were present
in this shard.

- `codex-rs/windows-sandbox-rs/src/deny_read_walker.rs` and its tests (`deny_read_walker_tests.rs`, and the directory-junction/cycle regression in `deny_read_resolver_access_tests.rs::native_walk_preserves_canonical_matches_through_directory_links_and_cycles`): traced the cycle-detection logic (`seen_directories` keyed by canonical path, falling back to the lexical path only when canonicalization itself fails) through the constructed `walk/alias -> target`, `target/cycle -> walk` test fixture and confirmed the second visit to `canonical(walk)` is rejected by `HashSet::insert` returning `false`, terminating the recursion rather than looping.
- `codex-rs/windows-sandbox-rs/src/deny_read_state.rs::sync_persistent_deny_read_acls`: applies the new desired deny-read ACL set before revoking any stale entries for the same principal SID, so a policy change cannot produce a window where a previously-denied path is briefly accessible.
- `codex-rs/windows-sandbox-rs/src/file_write.rs::write_file_atomically` / `create_temporary_file`: uses `OsRng` for the temp file name, opens the destination directory with `open_directory_no_reparse` and creates the temp file with `open_no_reparse` (no-follow), and performs the replace via `NtSetInformationFile`/`FILE_RENAME_INFORMATION` pinned to a `RootDirectory` handle rather than a path string, with cleanup (`FileDispositionInfo` delete-on-close) only for the file it created itself. Cross-checked against `file_write_tests.rs`'s hard-link and held-handle regression tests, which match the intended TOCTOU-resistant behavior.
- `codex-rs/windows-sandbox-rs/src/bin/setup_main/win/firewall.rs`: the offline-sandbox firewall rule sequencing (loopback UDP/TCP block installed before the proxy-port-complement narrowing, and the legacy allow-rule removed only after the new block rules are in place) fails closed at every intermediate step; `configure_rule` also does a read-back verification of `LocalUserAuthorizedList` against the expected SID before treating a rule as applied.
- `codex-rs/windows-sandbox-rs/src/desktop.rs::LaunchDesktop::open_private`: validates the desktop name against the `CodexSandboxDesktop-` prefix plus a bounded, hex-only nonce before using it in `Winsta0\{name}`/`OpenDesktopW`, rejecting the interactive/injected names exercised by `desktop_tests.rs::private_desktop_rejects_interactive_and_injected_names` (embedded `Winsta0\`, embedded NUL, oversized nonce, non-hex nonce).
- `codex-rs/windows-sandbox-rs/src/elevated/runner_pipe.rs::create_named_pipe` / `connect_pipe`: the named pipe DACL grants access only to the resolved sandbox-user SID, and `connect_pipe` additionally verifies the connecting client's PID via `GetNamedPipeClientProcessId` against the PID returned by the just-spawned `CreateProcessWithLogonW`, preventing a same-machine process from squatting on the pipe name even if it guessed it.

- `codex-rs/windows-sandbox-rs/src/token.rs` and `token_tests.rs`: restricted-token construction (`create_token_with_caps_from`), capability/user/logon/Everyone SID ordering, `WRITE_RESTRICTED`/`LUA_TOKEN`/`DISABLE_MAX_PRIVILEGE` flags, and the default-DACL setup that deliberately excludes identity-marker SIDs from object access — reviewed for logical consistency and found internally coherent; the accompanying integration test validates the restricting-SID list via `GetTokenInformation(TokenRestrictedSids)`.
- `codex-rs/windows-sandbox-rs/src/setup_mutex.rs`: the machine-wide setup mutex is created with an explicit SDDL (`D:P(A;;GA;;;SY)(A;;GA;;;BA)`) restricting access to SYSTEM and Administrators, matches its documented contract ("exclusive access by LocalSystem or an elevated administrator"), and correctly treats `WAIT_ABANDONED` as an acquired lock with a comment explaining the self-healing rationale.
- `codex-rs/windows-sandbox-rs/src/no_reparse_dir.rs` and `no_reparse_dir_tests.rs`: `NtCreateFile`-based no-reparse directory opening (`OBJ_DONT_REPARSE`), path validation, and the delete-on-close directory guard are covered by tests that create real junctions (`mklink /J`) and assert both a junctioned leaf and a junctioned ancestor are rejected.
- `codex-rs/windows-sandbox-rs/src/provisioning_client.rs`: `verify_server` authenticates the named-pipe server by cross-checking `GetNamedPipeServerProcessId` against the actual `CodexSandboxService` SCM status before any request bytes are sent; a `bail!` from this check is a generic `anyhow` error (not a recognized `io::Error` kind), so `provision_windows_sandbox_via_service` correctly propagates it as a hard failure rather than silently treating a spoofed pipe as "service unavailable."
- `codex-rs/windows-sandbox-rs/src/unified_exec/backends/legacy.rs` and `elevated.rs`: process/job/handle lifecycle on both the ConPTY and pipe-based paths (token handle closed on spawn failure, job-based termination with a `TerminateProcess` fallback, retry-with-credential-refresh flow) was traced end-to-end and appears consistent; `elevated_tests.rs`'s retry test exercises the second-failure-aborts-retry path with concrete assertions on both the spawn and refresh call observations.

- `codex-rs/windows-sandbox-rs/src/uninstall_windows.rs`, `uninstall_windows/firewall.rs`, `uninstall_windows/principals.rs`, `uninstall_windows/processes.rs`: cleanup ordering (disable accounts → stop processes → wait for logon-session release → remove filters/rules/principals) is careful about races (PID reuse after enumeration is re-checked via token SID before terminating; `DisabledSandboxUsers::restore` is invoked on partial failure to avoid leaving accounts disabled without protections removed).
- `codex-rs/windows-sandbox-rs/src/wfp.rs` and `wfp/filter_specs.rs`: WFP engine/transaction handling uses RAII guards (`Engine`, `Transaction`, `UserMatchCondition`) that clean up on drop/abort; filter add/delete treats "already exists"/"not found" as success where appropriate; `filter_keys_are_unique`/`filter_names_are_unique` tests back the static table.
- `codex-rs/windows-sandbox-rs/src/winutil.rs`: `resolve_sid`/`LookupAccountNameW` correctly retries on `ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_BUFFER` by resizing both the SID and domain buffers; `quote_windows_arg`/`argv_to_command_line` reproduce the standard CommandLineToArgvW quoting algorithm and are exercised by round-trip tests.
- `codex-rs/windows-sandbox-rs/src/wrapper.rs`/`wrapper_tests.rs`: argv is built and parsed as structured flags (not a shell string), so there is no shell-injection surface; the round-trip test covers every flag including JSON-encoded overrides.
- `codex-rs/windows-sandbox-service/src/ipc/home.rs`: `prepare_codex_home` pins ancestor directories, rejects reparse points found under sandbox subdirectories, and re-validates the drive type both before and after canonicalization, with comments explaining the remaining known gap (pathname-based helper opens vs. hardlink races) rather than silently ignoring it.
- `codex-rs/windows-sandbox-service/src/ipc.rs::handle_request`: the fixed-size request buffer is bounds-checked at every stage (`available as usize > MAX_REQUEST_BYTES - request_length` is checked before the `ReadFile` that would otherwise overflow the buffer slice), so a malicious client cannot overrun the 4096-byte request buffer.
- `codex-rs/workload-identity/src/assertion.rs` and `exchange.rs`: assertion file reads are capped via `take(MAX_ASSERTION_BYTES + 1)`, exchange responses are capped at `MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES` (both via `Content-Length` pre-check and a running total across streamed chunks), the token URL is restricted to HTTPS or loopback HTTP with no credentials/query/fragment, and `WorkloadIdentityToken`'s `Debug` impl redacts `access_token`.

- `codex-rs/worktree/src/git.rs`, `git_tests.rs`: the isolation strategy (stripping inherited `GIT_*` env vars, disabling hooks via `core.hooksPath=NUL`/`/dev/null`, disabling `core.fsmonitor`, and dynamically discovering and neutralizing every configured `filter.<name>.{clean,smudge,process,required}` driver — including dotted/`=`-containing driver names and destination-only filters introduced via `includeIf.gitdir:` conditional includes) is well designed and exercised by both the unit tests in `git_tests.rs` and the integration tests in `tests/worktree.rs` (`creation_ignores_inherited_git_environment`, `creation_disables_filters_from_destination_conditional_config`, `checkout_does_not_execute_configured_hooks_fsmonitor_or_filters`).
- `codex-rs/worktree/src/lib.rs`: `WorktreeManager::create`/`list`/`remove` use `--end-of-options` before user-influenced revision strings (preventing flag injection via a crafted `base`), canonicalize and re-verify that computed checkout `cwd`s stay inside the worktree root (`is_safe_worktree_cwd`), and reject symlink-based escapes and aliasing at the bucket/checkout/root level. This is directly covered by `creation_rejects_a_working_directory_that_escapes_through_a_base_symlink`, `listing_skips_worktrees_without_a_safe_source_working_directory`, and the alias/stale-registration tests in `tests/worktree.rs`.
- `codex-rs/worktree/src/metadata.rs`: thread-ownership binding is written atomically via `NamedTempFile` + `persist_noclobber`, with a re-check-on-conflict path that correctly treats "already bound to the same thread" as success and any other concurrent bind as a genuine conflict.
- `codex-rs/worktree/src/settings.rs`, `tests/settings.rs`: config parsing correctly rejects relative `git-worktree-root`, non-boolean `auto-cleanup`, and non-positive/non-integer `keep-count`, and `for_cli` correctly forwards only the shared root while always forcing `auto_cleanup_enabled = false`, ignoring (rather than validating) any Desktop-only cleanup keys — confirmed by `cli_creation_shares_default_and_custom_desktop_pools_without_enabling_cleanup`.
- `codex-rs/workload-identity/src/workload_identity_tests.rs`: covers the token-exchange contract (exact form-encoded field set, optional `workload_identity_context` passthrough, HTTPS-only token URL, absolute assertion-file path requirement, oversized-assertion rejection, incomplete-response rejection), single-flight de-duplication of concurrent resolves/refreshes under a shared mutex, and that `Debug` on the cached token redacts the access token. Note that the implementation file this test suite exercises (`workload_identity.rs`) is not part of this shard, so only the test file itself — not the underlying exchange/cache logic it tests — was reviewed here.
- Ran `cargo test -p codex-worktree` and `cargo test -p codex-workload-identity` against this shard's worktree at `e772a65de55fa84e9faebf786cd1e2c6b50e447c`; all 31 and 7 tests respectively pass.

**File:** `.npmrc`

Contents:
```
shamefully-hoist=true
strict-peer-dependencies=false
node-linker=hoisted
prefer-workspace-packages=true
```

Reviewed specifically for credential leakage (this shard was flagged as the
"repo-root miscellany" group where `.npmrc` commonly carries auth tokens).
There is no `_authToken`, `_auth`, `_password`, custom `registry=` pointing at
a private/authenticated feed, or any other secret-bearing line — the file
only sets pnpm/npm install-behavior flags (hoisting, peer-dependency
strictness, and workspace-package preference for a monorepo). All four
settings are internally consistent for a hoisted pnpm workspace setup
(`node-linker=hoisted` plus `shamefully-hoist=true` is redundant but not
contradictory — pnpm's hoisted linker already flattens `node_modules`, so
`shamefully-hoist` is a no-op in this mode, not a bug) and none of them is a
correctness or security defect. No further findings for this shard.

## Coverage notes

Only one file was in scope for this shard, and it was read and reviewed in
full. No files were skipped or partially reviewed.

- `scripts/codex_package/v8.py` — `verify_release_checksum_manifest`/`ensure_valid_artifact`/`has_checksum`: the downloaded SHA-256 manifest is itself authenticated against a repo-pinned trusted digest (`third_party/v8/rusty_v8_<version>_release_manifests.sha256`) before any artifact hash from that manifest is trusted, and the manifest/artifact files are unlinked on any verification failure so a corrupt/tampered cache entry can't be silently reused. `scripts/codex_package/test_v8.py` exercises the tamper, missing-pin, and CRLF-manifest cases directly and they pass the logic as written.
- `scripts/mcp_conformance/codex_conformance_adapter.py` — OAuth loopback callback validation (`_is_loopback_hostname`, `_validated_callback_url`) correctly restricts the driven authorization redirect to `http` + loopback host, requires the callback to preserve `state` and target the exact same scheme/host/port/path as the original `redirect_uri`, and rejects credentials embedded in the URL or a stray fragment. `_validate_oauth_secret_not_persisted` positively confirms the test's OAuth client secret does not appear in `config.toml` or any `.credentials.json` under the isolated `CODEX_HOME`, and the secret is threaded through as an env-var-name reference (`client_secret_env_var`) rather than being written into config directly.
- `scripts/just-shell.py` — `run_powershell` passes `-CommandWithArgs` with the recipe body and args as separate argv entries (not a concatenated string). I verified against a local PowerShell 7.6.6 install that `-CommandWithArgs`/`-cwa` is a real (experimental) flag that binds the trailing arguments to `$args` inside the script block, analogous to `sh -cu <command> "$0" "$@"` in `run_sh`; neither path builds a shell string from caller-supplied arguments.
- Grepped the whole shard for `shell=True`, `os.system(`, and `os.popen(` — none found. Every `subprocess.run`/`subprocess.Popen`/`subprocess.check_call` call in this shard passes an argument list, so there is no shell-string command-injection surface within these files.
- Archive extraction: `scripts/codex_package/dotslash.py::extract_archive_member` only ever extracts one manifest-named member to a caller-computed destination path (no attacker-influenced `extractall`), and `scripts/codex_package/smoke_tests/fixtures.py`'s `archive.extractall(extracted, filter="data")` uses Python's safe extraction filter. No zip-slip/tar-slip path found in this shard.
- `scripts/codex_package/cli.py::parse_package_version` — the semver regex plus the u64-range/no-leading-zero checks match the accept/reject test matrix in `scripts/codex_package/test_cli.py` exactly, including the `u64::MAX` boundary.

- `scripts/stage_npm_packages.py`: every `subprocess.check_call` /
  `subprocess.check_output` / `subprocess.run` invocation in this release
  script (the `gh run list`, `gh api`, `gh run download`, `zstd -f -d`, and
  the `build_npm_package.py` staging call) passes an argument list rather
  than a shell string, and no `shell=True` is used anywhere, so
  attacker-controlled or malformed `--release-version` / `--package` /
  `--workflow-url` values cannot achieve shell command injection (at worst
  they flow to `gh`/`zstd` as literal, safely-quoted argv entries).
  `install_single_codex_package_archive` extracts the downloaded
  `codex-package-*.tar.gz` with `archive.extractall(dest_dir,
  filter="data")`, which is the Python 3.12+ safe-extraction filter
  (rejects absolute paths, `..` traversal, device/symlink members), so the
  tarball-extraction path is not vulnerable to the classic path-traversal
  tar exploit. `_gha_escape` correctly neutralizes `%`, `\r`, `\n` before
  values are interpolated into `::group::...::` GitHub Actions workflow
  commands, which is the standard mitigation for the GHA workflow-command
  injection class. No hardcoded credentials, tokens, or private keys were
  found in this file; it relies entirely on the caller's already-authenticated
  `gh` CLI session.
- `scripts/mcp_conformance/server.py` and its test suite
  (`test_server.py`): HTTP request handling bounds `Content-Length` to
  `[0, 1_048_576]` before reading the body (so a missing/negative/oversized
  `Content-Length` is rejected rather than hanging on `rfile.read`), the
  mirrored-header decoder (`_decode_mirrored_header`) uses
  `base64.b64decode(..., validate=True)` and rejects control characters in
  plain headers, and the bool/int type-confusion case in `header_echo`
  argument validation (Python's `bool` being a subclass of `int`) is
  explicitly special-cased and covered by tests. This is a local
  conformance-test fixture (binds to `127.0.0.1` by default) rather than a
  production service, and its origin/permissiveness choices are appropriate
  for that role.
- `scripts/mcp_conformance/test_official_conformance.py`: the
  OAuth-secret-handling tests (`_validate_oauth_secret_not_persisted`,
  `redact_sensitive_text`, `_write_auth_registration`,
  `_scrub_retained_artifacts`) exercise real secret-redaction/non-persistence
  guarantees with synthetic dummy secrets (`"reviewer-confidential-client-secret"`,
  `"do-not-retain"`, etc.); no real credential material is present. The
  static-analysis hook on this file flagged an `MD-LINK-TOKEN-IN-QUERY`
  pattern (`?code=`) — inspection confirms this is an OAuth authorization
  callback URL used as test fixture input (`_authorization_url`), not a
  live credential or injected instruction; false positive.
- Grepped all eight shard files for credential-shaped strings
  (`api[_-]?key|secret|token|password|BEGIN (RSA|OPENSSH|PRIVATE)`); the
  only hits are unrelated JSON field names (`input_tokens`,
  `progressToken`) and the intentionally-illustrative
  `env_key = "OPENAI_API_KEY_STAGING"` sample config text printed by
  `scripts/mock_responses_websocket_server.py` (a mock server that never
  reads or forwards a real key).

- `sdk/typescript/src/thread.ts` — `Thread.run()`/`Thread.runStreamed()`: verified the output-schema temp file is always cleaned up via `try/finally` around the generator, including on early `break` (the for-await loop calls `generator.return()`, which runs the `finally`), confirmed by `run.test.ts`'s "writes output schema to a temporary file and forwards it" assertion that the path no longer exists after `run()` resolves. `turn.completed` usage patching (`cache_write_input_tokens ??= 0`) and `turn.failed` short-circuiting into a thrown `Error` were both cross-checked against `run.test.ts`/`runStreamed.test.ts` expectations and match.
- `sdk/typescript/src/outputSchemaFile.ts` — validated `isJsonObject` rejects arrays/primitives/null, and that `mkdtemp`/`writeFile` failures call `cleanup()` before rethrowing so no orphaned temp directory is left on a write failure.
- `sdk/typescript/src/items.ts` — `FileChangeItem`/`PatchApplyStatus` intentionally excludes `"in_progress"` (`codex-rs` only reaches the `InProgress` mapping arm via `ItemStarted`, not `ItemCompleted`, and the SDK only surfaces `item.completed` items through `Turn.items`); this matches the type's own doc comment ("Emitted once the patch succeeds or fails") and is not a bug. `McpToolCallItem.result`/`error`/`McpToolCallStatus` and other item shapes were compared field-by-field against `codex-rs/exec/src/exec_events.rs` and are consistent (the `result`/`error` fields being typed as optional rather than nullable is a minor type-strictness nit with no observed functional impact, since JS truthiness checks treat `null` and `undefined` alike, and no code in this shard relies on `=== undefined`).
- `sdk/typescript/tests/exec.test.ts`, `run.test.ts`, `runStreamed.test.ts`, `abort.test.ts` — exercised the config-override precedence, resume/new-thread argument ordering, PATH/env handling, and abort-signal propagation tests by reading them against `codexExecSpy.ts`/`testCodex.ts`/`responsesProxy.ts`; assertions are internally consistent and exercise real edge cases (raw TOML overrides with embedded quotes/backslashes, Windows `Path` vs `PATH`, duplicate `--config` ordering).
- `sdk/typescript/tests/mcpConformance.test.ts` — confirmed it fails closed (throws) when the conformance harness, baseline files, or built `codex` binary are missing, rather than silently skipping.
- `sdk/typescript/tests/responsesProxy.ts`, `setupCodexHome.ts`, `testCodex.ts`, `tsup.config.ts` — no credential material, and no defects found; `testCodex.ts`'s `getCurrentEnv()` inheriting `process.env` into spawned test processes is scoped to test helpers only (not part of the published package entry `src/index.ts`), so it is not a production credential-leak path.

Note: nothing in this shard writes outside the assigned report path; no repo files were modified.

Reviewed all 25 files in `third_party/voice/` (13 implementation modules, 11 test modules under `test_*.py`, plus `windows_build_inputs.py`/`windows_runtime.py`). This is an unusually defensive, heavily-tested packaging/build pipeline for native voice binaries (ELF/Mach-O/PE inspection, relocation, and signing prior to bundling into a Codex package). Ran the full non-platform-gated test suite plus the macOS-specific suite on this Darwin host (`test_prepare_sources`, `test_bazel_windows`, `test_sdk`, `test_build_native`, `test_macos_runtime`, `test_assemble_package`, `test_prepare_built_runtime` — 66 tests total, all passing, including subtests that compile real shared libraries with `cc`, relocate them, re-sign with `codesign`, and load them via `ctypes` after deleting the original build prefix). `test_linux_runtime.py` and `test_windows_runtime.py` are platform-gated (`skipUnless(sys.platform == ...)`) and could not be executed in this Darwin-only environment; I read them closely instead (ELF/PE header parsing, dynamic-table/import-directory bounds checks, rpath/`$ORIGIN` handling) and found the validation logic internally consistent with the analogous, test-verified macOS code path.

Specifically checked and found sound:
- No `subprocess` call anywhere in the shard uses `shell=True`; all invocations pass argument lists, and environment variables that flow into shell-interpreted contexts (`CFLAGS`/`LDFLAGS`/`AM_MAKEFLAGS` in `build_native.py`) are explicitly whitespace/quote-rejected or file-based response files rather than inline-quoted, with a real end-to-end test (`test_libffi_compiler_receives_literal_defines_without_shell_quotes`) proving no shell reinterpretation occurs.
- Path-escape defenses in `assemble_package.py`, `runtime.py`'s `prepare()`, `sdk.py`, and `prepare_sources.py` (symlink rejection, `is_relative_to` checks, exclusive `mkdir()` for all outputs, `tarfile` extraction with the safe `filter="data"` plus explicit size/member-count/hardlink-expansion caps) are all exercised by tests that attempt the escape and assert both the `ValueError` and that no partial output is left behind.
- Every multi-step "verify then use" operation (runtime digest checks in `assemble_package.py`, receipt/ci.json checks in `runtime.py`/`sdk.py`/`prepare_built_runtime.py`) re-verifies bytes after copying, not only before, guarding against TOCTOU tampering during the copy itself, and this is specifically tested (`test_copy_revalidation_removes_only_new_output`, `test_changed_source_at_copy_is_rejected`).
- `windows_build_inputs.py`'s tool-shadowing detection and `;`-in-path rejection correctly prevent both PATH-injection and same-named-tool shadowing (e.g. Cygwin's `link.exe` vs MSVC's `link.exe`), verified by a real subprocess test that plants a conflicting shell-script executable.
- No credentials, tokens, or secret material appear anywhere in this shard.

- `tools/argument-comment-lint/src/comment_parser.rs` (`parse_argument_comment`, `parse_argument_comment_prefix`, `is_identifier`): traced the byte-slicing logic (all splits occur on ASCII `/*`/`*/` matches, so UTF-8 boundaries are always safe) and manually walked every case in the accompanying unit tests plus several additional hand-constructed inputs (comments containing punctuation, doc-comment-shaped `/** ... */` text, a comment belonging to a preceding argument bleeding into the next argument's gap). All behaved as intended — no false-positive comment matches found.
- `tools/argument-comment-lint/src/lib.rs` (`ArgumentCommentLint::check_call`, `is_anonymous_literal_like`, `is_workspace_crate_name`, self-documenting-method exemption): cross-checked the lint logic against every fixture under `tools/argument-comment-lint/ui/*.rs` (`allow_char_literals.rs`, `allow_self_documenting_methods.rs`, `allow_string_literals.rs`, `comment_matches.rs`, `comment_matches_multiline.rs`, `comment_mismatch.rs`, `ignore_external_methods.rs`, `multiple_method_arguments.rs`, `uncommented_literal.rs`) and confirmed the expected warn/no-warn outcome for each call site by hand-tracing the parameter-offset, self-documenting-method exemption (`args.len() == 1 && method_name == expected_name`), and external-crate filtering (`is_workspace_crate_name`). All matched the fixtures' evident intent.
- `tools/argument-comment-lint/wrapper_common.py` (`parse_wrapper_args`, `build_final_args`, `set_default_lint_env`, `append_env_flag`): ran the bundled test suite directly (`python3 -m unittest test_wrapper_common -v`) — all 6 tests pass — and additionally hand-traced each test's expected output against the implementation to confirm the flag-forwarding/defaulting logic (workspace/package selection, `--all-targets` suppression under `--fix` or an explicit target selector, single `--` separator preservation) is correct.
- `tools/argument-comment-lint/driver.rs` and `tools/argument-comment-lint/src/bin/argument-comment-lint.rs` (`rustc_args`, `is_rustc`, `has_library_selection`, `strict_rustflags`/`append_flag_if_missing`, `normalize_nightly_library_filename`/`normalize_nightly_toolchain`): standard Dylint driver boilerplate; verified the STRICT_LINTS flag string built here is byte-for-byte identical to the one Python's `set_default_lint_env` builds (both covered by their respective unit tests), and traced the nightly-filename-normalization regex/parsing against the Rust unit tests plus the parallel Python `_NIGHTLY_LIBRARY_PATTERN` — the two implementations agree on which filenames get normalized.
- No credential-bearing files (`.env`, `*.pem`, `id_rsa`, `.npmrc`, etc.) exist in this shard; all subprocess invocations across `run.py`, `run-prebuilt-linter.py`, and `wrapper_common.py` use list-form `subprocess.run`/`Command::new` (no `shell=True`, no string concatenation into a shell), so there is no command-injection surface from environment or argv values.

**Not fully reviewed:**
None — all 17 files in the shard list were opened and read in full, and the Python test suite (`test_wrapper_common.py`) was executed directly. The Rust unit tests in `comment_parser.rs`, `lib.rs`, and `argument-comment-lint.rs` (including the `dylint_testing::ui_test` harness that exercises the `ui/*.rs` fixtures) were reviewed by manual trace rather than executed, since running them requires the pinned `nightly-2025-09-18` toolchain with `rustc-dev`/`llvm-tools-preview` components and the `cargo-dylint`/`dylint-link` tooling, which is a heavyweight, environment-specific setup outside what this shard review can assume is present.
